description: Airborne Infection Isolation (AII) room negative pressure, ventilation, and anteroom requirements
violation_template: Plan review comment — Infection Control: The {occupancy} AII room(s) shown on the submitted drawings do not demonstrate compliance with FGI 2022 §2.1-3.2.6.2 and ASHRAE 170-2021 Table 7.1. Each AII room must maintain a continuous negative pressure differential of not less than 0.01 inches water gauge (2.5 Pa) relative to the adjacent corridor and all contiguous spaces, with a minimum of 12 total air changes per hour (ACH), of which at least 2 ACH must be outdoor air. The mechanical schedules do not clearly indicate exhaust discharge directly to the exterior (minimum 25 feet from air intakes and operable openings), and self-closing, gasketed, or automatic-actuating doors are not specified at all anteroom openings. Anteroom provisions per §2.1-3.2.6.2(d) must be clearly detailed on the architectural plans with positive-latching or automatic-closing hardware to prevent simultaneous opening of both doors.
fix_template:
1. Revise the mechanical schedules and room data sheets to confirm each AII room achieves a minimum of 12 total ACH with not less than 2 ACH outdoor air, and demonstrate continuous negative pressure of -0.01" w.g. relative to all adjoining spaces.
2. Provide a pressure relationship diagram (air pressure map) for the isolation room cluster showing directional airflow arrows from clean to less-clean spaces, signed and sealed by the mechanical engineer of record.
3. Detail exhaust duct routing on the mechanical drawings from each AII room exhaust grille to an exterior discharge location at least 25 feet from any air intake, operable opening, or occupied area per ASHRAE 170-2021 §6.2.
4. Add a dedicated anteroom between each AII room and the corridor. Confirm the anteroom is equipped with self-closing hardware or automatic door operators on both doors and that simultaneous opening of both doors is prevented via an interlock or occupancy sensor per FGI 2022 §2.1-3.2.6.2(d).
5. Specify a continuous monitoring system (audible/visual alarm) at the AII room entry to alert staff when the required negative pressure differential is not maintained, per ASHRAE 170-2021 §7.1.
6. Coordinate with the architectural and mechanical drawings to ensure no supply air diffusers are located in a position that would short-circuit room air before it reaches the exhaust grilles.

description: Protective Environment (PE) room positive pressure, HEPA filtration, and separation from AII rooms
violation_template: Plan review comment — Infection Control: The Protective Environment (PE) room(s) for immunocompromised patients shown in the {occupancy} do not demonstrate compliance with FGI 2022 §2.1-3.2.6.3 and ASHRAE 170-2021 Table 7.1. PE rooms must maintain continuous positive pressure of not less than +0.01 inches water gauge relative to the adjacent corridor and all contiguous spaces to prevent infiltration of airborne contaminants. The submitted mechanical design does not confirm HEPA filtration rated at ≥99.97% efficiency at 0.3-micron particulate upstream of all supply air serving PE rooms, a minimum of 12 total ACH, or that the PE anteroom is not shared with an Airborne Infection Isolation (AII) room anteroom. Sharing an anteroom between a PE room and an AII room is specifically prohibited because the opposing pressure relationships cannot be simultaneously maintained.
fix_template:
1. Revise mechanical schedules to confirm PE room supply air passes through HEPA filters rated at ≥99.97% efficiency at 0.3 micron, installed in a location accessible for filter replacement without contaminating the clean side of the air stream per ASHRAE 170-2021 §6.4.
2. Confirm and document on the air-handling unit schedule that each PE room receives a minimum of 12 total ACH with continuous positive pressure of +0.01" w.g. or greater relative to all adjoining spaces.
3. Provide a pressure relationship diagram (air pressure map) signed by the mechanical engineer of record, confirming the PE room is positive relative to its anteroom and the anteroom is positive relative to the corridor.
4. Verify that no PE room anteroom shares its enclosure or air system with an AII room anteroom; revise the floor plan if a shared anteroom condition currently exists per FGI 2022 §2.1-3.2.6.3(e).
5. Specify a continuous differential pressure monitoring device with audible/visual alarm at the PE room entry to alert staff when positive pressure is not maintained, per ASHRAE 170-2021 §7.1.
6. Detail door hardware to confirm self-closing, gasketed doors at both anteroom entries to preserve pressure relationships at all times.

description: Soiled utility and soiled workroom negative pressure and exhaust requirements
violation_template: Plan review comment — Infection Control: The soiled utility/soiled workroom(s) shown in the {occupancy} do not clearly demonstrate negative pressure relative to the corridor and adjacent clean spaces as required by ASHRAE 170-2021 Table 7.1. Soiled utility rooms must be maintained under continuous negative pressure to prevent migration of odors, aerosols, and pathogens into clean patient care areas. The mechanical schedule must confirm a minimum of 10 total air changes per hour, all of which must be exhausted directly to the exterior. The submitted drawings do not indicate that supply air to these rooms is exhausted (not recirculated), nor do they confirm dedicated exhaust with exterior discharge, as required by ASHRAE 170-2021 §7.1 and Table 7.1.
fix_template:
1. Revise the mechanical room data sheet for each soiled utility/workroom to confirm negative pressure relative to the corridor and all adjacent clean spaces, with minimum 10 total ACH, all exhausted to the exterior.
2. Confirm on the mechanical drawings that exhaust from soiled utility rooms is not recirculated and is discharged to the exterior at a location meeting the separation distances required by ASHRAE 170-2021 §6.2.
3. Provide a pressure relationship diagram showing the directional air pressure relationship between the soiled workroom, the corridor, and any adjacent clean utility or patient room.
4. Detail door undercut or transfer air pathway to allow replacement air to enter the soiled room when it is under negative pressure without reversing the pressure relationship.
5. Confirm supply air diffuser placement does not short-circuit to the exhaust grille; exhaust grilles should be located low in the room near soiled receptacles per ASHRAE 170-2021 guidance.

description: Operating room continuous positive pressure relative to corridor and sub-sterile spaces
violation_template: Plan review comment — Surgery / Infection Control: The operating room(s) shown in the {occupancy} surgical suite do not demonstrate continuous positive pressure of not less than +0.01 inches water gauge relative to both the corridor and the sub-sterile corridor/room as required by FGI 2022 §2.1-3.6.3.3 and ASHRAE 170-2021 Table 7.1. Positive pressure in the OR is critical to prevent the infiltration of particulate-laden air from less-clean adjacent spaces into the sterile operative field. The air pressure relationship diagram submitted does not account for all adjacent spaces, including the sub-sterile room and the scrub corridor, and does not confirm continuous pressurization during occupied and unoccupied modes.
fix_template:
1. Revise the mechanical air pressure diagram to confirm each OR is positive (+0.01" w.g. minimum) relative to the corridor, sub-sterile room, and all adjoining spaces under all operating conditions, including when OR doors are closed per FGI 2022 §2.1-3.6.3.3.
2. Specify pressure-independent VAV boxes or dedicated air-handling units for each OR to ensure pressure relationships are maintained regardless of adjacent space loads.
3. Include door sweep and door seal specifications for OR doors to minimize leakage that could compromise positive pressure; confirm automatic-closing hardware is specified.
4. Provide the mechanical engineer's signed/sealed air pressure relationship diagram showing all OR-adjacent spaces with pressure differential values and directional airflow arrows.
5. Confirm the Building Automation System (BAS) will provide continuous OR pressure monitoring with alarms at the OR entrance annunciator per ASHRAE 170-2021 §7.1.

description: Operating room minimum total ACH, outdoor air fraction, HEPA filtration, and unidirectional airflow at operative field
violation_template: Plan review comment — Surgery / Mechanical: The operating room ventilation design shown in the {occupancy} does not meet the minimum requirements of FGI 2022 §2.1-3.6.3 and ASHRAE 170-2021 Table 7.1. Each OR must receive a minimum of 20 total air changes per hour, with not less than 4 ACH being 100% outdoor air. The mechanical schedule does not confirm HEPA filtration (≥99.97% at 0.3 micron) on all supply air streams serving the OR. Additionally, FGI 2022 §2.1-3.6.3.1 requires unidirectional (laminar) downflow supply air diffusers centered over the operative field with a minimum diffuser coverage of the operative zone; the submitted reflected ceiling plan does not document the diffuser array configuration or demonstrate compliance with this requirement.
fix_template:
1. Revise the mechanical schedule and air-handling unit data to confirm each OR receives ≥20 total ACH with ≥4 ACH outdoor (100% outside air), per ASHRAE 170-2021 Table 7.1.
2. Specify HEPA filters (≥99.97% efficiency at 0.3 micron) on all supply air serving ORs; document filter location, accessible service access, and replacement procedure in the mechanical specifications.
3. Provide a reflected ceiling plan for each OR showing the low-velocity laminar-flow HEPA diffuser array dimensions, coverage area, and centerline alignment with the surgical table per FGI 2022 §2.1-3.6.3.1. Diffuser discharge velocity shall not exceed 25-35 FPM at 6 inches below diffuser face.
4. Confirm on the mechanical drawings that OR supply air is not recirculated through the general system; exhaust/return air must be taken from low sidewall registers away from the operative field per ASHRAE 170-2021 §7.1.
5. Coordinate the structural and mechanical drawings to confirm no obstructions (light fixtures, booms, or structure) interrupt the unidirectional flow pattern over the operative field.

description: Minimum clear floor area for general and specialty operating rooms
violation_template: Plan review comment — Surgery / Architecture: The operating room(s) shown in the {occupancy} do not demonstrate the minimum clear floor area required by FGI 2022 §2.1-3.6.2.2, Table 2.1-3. General ORs require a minimum of 400 square feet of clear floor area, exclusive of fixed equipment alcoves, built-in cabinets, and scrub sink alcoves. Cardiac surgery, orthopedic surgery, and neurosurgery ORs require a minimum of 600 square feet clear. The dimensions shown on the submitted floor plan, when field-verified against fixed equipment clearances and code-mandated alcove exclusions, do not yield the required minimum clear area. Failure to provide adequate OR clear area compromises patient and staff safety, limits equipment access, and does not comply with FGI 2022.
fix_template:
1. Provide a dimensioned floor plan for each OR with all fixed equipment, casework, and alcoves clearly labeled; annotate the computed clear floor area in square feet exclusive of all fixed elements per FGI 2022 §2.1-3.6.2.2.
2. For general ORs, demonstrate ≥400 SF clear; for cardiac, orthopedic, or neurosurgery ORs, demonstrate ≥600 SF clear; label the intended surgical specialty on each OR room sheet.
3. If the existing footprint cannot achieve minimum area, revise the floor plan to increase room dimensions or relocate fixed equipment to code-compliant alcoves outside the OR clear area.
4. Confirm 3-foot minimum clearance at all sides of the surgical table within the clear area calculation per FGI 2022 guidance.
5. Coordinate with medical equipment planner to confirm that boom, pendant, and overhead light positions are accounted for in the room layout without encroaching on minimum clear area dimensions.

description: Scrub sink quantity and configuration, and sub-sterile room requirement between operating rooms
violation_template: Plan review comment — Surgery / Plumbing: The surgical suite scrub sink arrangement shown in the {occupancy} does not comply with FGI 2022 §2.1-3.6.6. A minimum of two (2) scrub positions must be provided outside each OR, accessible to the OR entry, with hands-free (knee-operated or foot-pedal) controls and no-touch sensor faucets. The submitted plan does not clearly show the required sub-sterile room between every pair of adjacent ORs; FGI 2022 §2.1-3.6.5 requires a sub-sterile room containing a steam sterilizer or high-level disinfector, pass-through window, and sink between each two ORs sharing the sub-sterile service. Single ORs at end of a suite must still have an adjacent sub-sterile or instrument processing access. Scrub sink alcoves must be sized to allow simultaneous two-person scrubbing without crowding.
fix_template:
1. Revise the floor plan to show a minimum of two (2) scrub sink positions outside the entry of each OR, dimensioned to allow simultaneous use; specify knee-or foot-pedal faucet controls and no-touch sensor faucet trim per FGI 2022 §2.1-3.6.6.
2. Provide a sub-sterile room between every two adjacent ORs sharing the service corridor; the sub-sterile room must contain a steam sterilizer (or equivalent), instrument pass-through windows to each OR, a sink, and storage per FGI 2022 §2.1-3.6.5.
3. Confirm the sub-sterile room is accessed from the sterile/clean corridor, not from the public or soiled corridor, maintaining proper traffic flow separation.
4. Specify on the plumbing drawings that scrub sinks are provided with temperature-limited hot water not exceeding 110°F (43°C) and are connected to the hospital's medical-grade water supply.
5. Confirm scrub sink alcove dimensions provide a minimum of 2'-6" per scrub position and do not obstruct OR door swing or sterile supply traffic flow.

description: Medical/surgical single-patient room minimum clear floor area and headwall-to-footwall clearance
violation_template: Plan review comment — Architecture / Patient Rooms: The medical/surgical single-patient rooms shown in the {occupancy} do not demonstrate the minimum clear floor area required by FGI 2022 §2.1-2.2.2.1 and Table 2.1-2. Each single-patient room must provide a minimum of 120 square feet of clear floor area, exclusive of toilet room, closet, vestibule/anteroom, and built-in casework. Additionally, the clear dimension from the face of the patient headwall (or plumbing/medical gas chase) to the face of the footwall must be not less than 13'-0". The plans as submitted do not annotate these exclusions, and the net clear area and headwall-to-footwall dimension cannot be verified from the information provided.
fix_template:
1. Add a room area schedule or annotation to each patient room on the architectural floor plan, clearly documenting the net clear floor area in square feet excluding toilet, closet, vestibule, and fixed casework, per FGI 2022 §2.1-2.2.2.1.
2. Dimension the clear distance from the face of the headwall (or plumbing/gas chase) to the face of the footwall on the floor plan; confirm this dimension is ≥13'-0" per FGI 2022 Table 2.1-2.
3. Show 3-foot minimum clear aisles at the side and foot of the patient bed on the furniture layout overlay to confirm maneuverability for stretcher transfer and clinical care access.
4. Confirm that the toilet room, if shared between two rooms, is not counted in the clear floor area of either room, and that both rooms independently achieve 120 SF clear.
5. Coordinate the reflected ceiling plan with the floor plan to confirm medical gas headwall rough-in, IV track, and overhead lift provisions (if any) do not encroach on the required clear area when equipment is in use.

description: ICU single-bed and open-bay minimum clear floor area, bed clearances, and hand hygiene requirements
violation_template: Plan review comment — Architecture / Intensive Care: The Intensive Care Unit patient spaces in the {occupancy} do not meet minimum dimensional requirements of FGI 2022 §2.1-2.7.2.1. Single-bed ICU rooms require a minimum of 200 square feet of clear floor area exclusive of toilet, anteroom, and fixed casework, with a minimum clearance of 4'-0" at each side and the foot of the bed. Open-bay ICU configurations require a minimum of 150 square feet per patient bed, with a minimum of 7'-0" clear between bed centerlines. The submitted plan also does not clearly show a dedicated handwashing sink within each ICU patient space or room, as required by FGI 2022 §2.1-2.7.4.2.
fix_template:
1. Revise ICU single-bed room dimensions to achieve ≥200 SF clear floor area (excluding toilet, anteroom, casework); annotate this calculation on the floor plan per FGI 2022 §2.1-2.7.2.1.
2. Dimension and confirm 4'-0" minimum clear aisles at both sides and the foot of the ICU bed; show bed outline at 36"×84" (standard) on the furniture/equipment layout plan.
3. For open-bay ICU configurations, confirm ≥150 SF per bed position and ≥7'-0" centerline-to-centerline spacing between beds; annotate both values on the plan.
4. Locate and label a dedicated handwashing sink within each ICU patient room or, for open-bay, within the bay; confirm the sink is accessible without crossing another patient's space per FGI 2022 §2.1-2.7.4.2.
5. Provide family accommodation space adjacent to or within each single-bed ICU room per FGI 2022 §2.1-2.7.2.1(b); show seating/sleeping area on the furniture layout.
6. Confirm the floor plan shows storage for clean supplies and equipment within or immediately adjacent to each ICU bed space without encroaching on the minimum clear area.

description: LDR and LDRP room minimum clear floor area and toilet room adjacency requirements
violation_template: Plan review comment — Architecture / Obstetrics: The Labor/Delivery/Recovery (LDR) and Labor/Delivery/Recovery/Postpartum (LDRP) rooms shown in the {occupancy} do not demonstrate the minimum clear floor areas required by FGI 2022 §2.1-2.8.3.1. LDR rooms require a minimum of 300 square feet of clear floor area, exclusive of toilet room, closet, and anteroom. LDRP rooms require a minimum of 325 square feet of clear floor area. Additionally, a toilet room must be provided either within the LDR/LDRP room or immediately adjacent and accessible without entering a public corridor. The submitted plans do not annotate the net clear areas exclusive of toilet and fixed elements, and the toilet room relationship to the birth room is not clearly shown.
fix_template:
1. Add a room area schedule or annotation to each LDR and LDRP room on the architectural floor plan documenting the net clear floor area in square feet, excluding toilet room, closet, anteroom, and fixed casework per FGI 2022 §2.1-2.8.3.1; confirm LDR ≥300 SF and LDRP ≥325 SF.
2. Show the toilet room on the floor plan in direct connection to each LDR/LDRP room; confirm access is provided without exiting into a public corridor.
3. Dimension 4'-0" minimum clear aisles at the foot and sides of the birthing bed and show the infant warmer/bassinet position within the room to confirm it fits within the clear area.
4. Confirm a handwashing sink is located within the LDR/LDRP room near the foot of the bed for birth attendance access per FGI 2022 §2.1-2.8.3.2.
5. Provide family accommodation within the room (recliner/sleeping surface) on the furniture layout, as required by FGI 2022 §2.1-2.8.3.1(d), and confirm this area is included in the 300/325 SF calculation.

description: NICU patient station minimum area per bassinet level and family space requirements
violation_template: Plan review comment — Architecture / Neonatal Intensive Care: The NICU patient station(s) shown in the {occupancy} do not demonstrate the minimum floor area per bassinet station required by FGI 2022 §2.1-2.9. Level II intermediate care bassinet stations require a minimum of 100 square feet per station; Level III intensive care bassinet stations require a minimum of 120 square feet per station. In open-bay configurations, a minimum of 4'-0" must be maintained between isolette/crib edges. The submitted plan does not annotate bassinet station areas exclusive of central aisles and nursing stations, and family accommodation space within or immediately adjacent to each bassinet station has not been shown as required by FGI 2022 §2.1-2.9.2.
fix_template:
1. Add area annotations to the NICU plan for each bassinet station, documenting square footage per station exclusive of central circulation aisles and nursing work areas; confirm Level II ≥100 SF/station and Level III ≥120 SF/station per FGI 2022 §2.1-2.9.
2. Dimension the clear separation between isolette/crib edges in open-bay configurations; confirm ≥4'-0" between adjacent equipment edges.
3. Show family accommodation space (minimum seating for at least one parent/caregiver) at each bassinet station per FGI 2022 §2.1-2.9.2; note whether this space is within the station area or in an adjacent family zone.
4. Confirm a handwashing sink is provided for each bassinet station or bay cluster, accessible without crossing another patient's zone per FGI 2022 §2.1-2.9.3.
5. For single-family rooms (SFR) NICU configuration, confirm each room meets the full SFR area and acoustic requirements per FGI 2022 §2.1-2.9 and that a family sleeping area is included within the room.

description: Emergency Department must provide at least one AII room with negative pressure, anteroom, and HEPA exhaust
violation_template: Plan review comment — Emergency Department / Infection Control: The Emergency Department in the {occupancy} does not demonstrate provision of at least one (1) Airborne Infection Isolation (AII) room within the ED treatment area, as required by FGI 2022 §2.1-3.1.3.4. The AII room must comply with all requirements of FGI 2022 §2.1-3.2.6.2: continuous negative pressure of -0.01" w.g. relative to the adjacent corridor and triage areas, a minimum of 12 total ACH (2 ACH outdoor air minimum), self-closing anteroom with interlocked doors, and exhaust discharged directly to the exterior with HEPA filtration or equivalent. Emergency Departments receive patients of unknown infectious status, making AII capability essential for infection prevention and staff protection.
fix_template:
1. Designate at least one treatment room in the ED as an AII room and revise the floor plan to show a compliant anteroom configuration with self-closing, interlocked doors per FGI 2022 §2.1-3.2.6.2.
2. Revise the mechanical schedule and room data sheet for the ED AII room to confirm -0.01" w.g. negative pressure relative to the corridor and anteroom, minimum 12 total ACH with 2 ACH outdoor, and exhaust to the exterior.
3. Specify HEPA filtration (≥99.97% at 0.3 micron) on the AII room exhaust or confirm exterior discharge location is ≥25 feet from any air intake or operable opening per ASHRAE 170-2021 §6.2.
4. Provide a continuous pressure monitoring device with audible/visual alarm at the AII room entry per ASHRAE 170-2021 §7.1.
5. Coordinate the architectural and mechanical drawings to confirm that the AII room is located to allow direct admission from the ED entrance or triage area without passing through the general ED treatment zone, to minimize exposure risk.

description: ED trauma room minimum clear floor area, three-side bed accessibility, and overhead light rough-in
violation_template: Plan review comment — Emergency Department / Architecture: The trauma room(s) / resuscitation bay(s) shown in the {occupancy} do not meet the minimum requirements of FGI 2022 §2.1-3.1.4.2. Each trauma/resuscitation room must provide a minimum clear floor area of 225 square feet per patient position, with accessibility from at least three (3) sides of the patient bed for simultaneous multi-disciplinary team access. The submitted floor plan does not annotate the net clear area exclusive of fixed casework and does not demonstrate three-side accessibility when equipment and personnel are present. Additionally, an overhead surgical-grade light rough-in (ceiling stub and structural backing) is required at each trauma room position; the reflected ceiling plan does not show this provision.
fix_template:
1. Annotate the trauma room floor plan to document the net clear area per patient position (≥225 SF), exclusive of fixed casework, cabinets, and equipment alcoves, per FGI 2022 §2.1-3.1.4.2.
2. Show the trauma gurney/stretcher position (36"×84" minimum) on the floor plan and dimension the clear aisles at three sides; confirm simultaneous access for resuscitation team members without obstruction.
3. Add ceiling rough-in for an overhead surgical-grade light (pendant or track mount) at each trauma room position to the reflected ceiling plan; provide structural backing per fixture manufacturer requirements.
4. Confirm a scrub sink or handwashing sink with hands-free controls is located within or immediately outside the trauma room entry, accessible during resuscitation.
5. Coordinate with medical equipment planner to show location of ceiling-mounted equipment booms, IV poles, and resuscitation cart alcoves within the 225 SF clear area calculation.

description: ED single-patient treatment room minimum clear floor area and hand hygiene fixture at room entry
violation_template: Plan review comment — Emergency Department / Architecture: The single-patient treatment rooms in the {occupancy} Emergency Department do not meet the minimum requirements of FGI 2022 §2.1-3.1.4.1. Each single-patient ED treatment room must provide a minimum of 120 square feet of clear floor area, exclusive of toilet room, anteroom, and fixed casework. The submitted plans do not annotate net clear area calculations, and several rooms appear to fall below the required minimum based on the scaled dimensions. Additionally, a hand hygiene fixture must be located at or within the room entry to facilitate compliance with hand-hygiene protocols upon entering and exiting each treatment space; this is not shown on the plumbing drawings.
fix_template:
1. Add a room data schedule annotating the net clear floor area (in SF, excluding toilet, anteroom, casework) for each ED single-patient treatment room; confirm each achieves ≥120 SF per FGI 2022 §2.1-3.1.4.1.
2. Revise the plumbing plan to show a hand hygiene sink or alcohol-based hand rub (ABHR) dispenser at the entry of each single-patient treatment room; note that ABHR may supplement but should not solely replace a sink in high-risk treatment areas.
3. Confirm door swing, curtain track, and equipment placement do not reduce the effective clear area below 120 SF when the room is in use; show a furniture/equipment layout overlay.
4. Coordinate with electrical to ensure a nurse call/patient communication device and sufficient receptacle count are provided within the minimum room footprint without creating tripping hazards or obstructing the clear area.
5. For any ED treatment bays using curtain separation (open bay), confirm the bay meets or exceeds the 120 SF clear area requirement and that privacy curtain tracks are shown on the reflected ceiling plan.

description: Hand hygiene fixture required at entry of each patient room in inpatient care areas
violation_template: Plan review comment — Infection Control / Plumbing: The {occupancy} patient room plumbing layouts do not demonstrate a hand hygiene fixture at or immediately inside the entry of each patient room as required by FGI 2022 §2.1-2.1.4.1. Hand hygiene compliance at patient room entry and exit is a primary infection control measure; the fixture must be accessible to staff entering the room without requiring passage to the far end of the room. Alcohol-based hand rub (ABHR) dispensers are permitted to supplement hand hygiene provisions but may not serve as the sole hand hygiene resource in rooms caring for patients with C. difficile or other contact-precaution pathogens where soap-and-water washing is clinically required. The plumbing drawings do not show sink locations relative to room entries.
fix_template:
1. Revise the plumbing floor plan to show a handwashing sink positioned at or within 2'-0" of the room entry (inside the room) for each inpatient patient room per FGI 2022 §2.1-2.1.4.1; dimension the sink location from the door frame.
2. Specify hands-free (knee, foot, or sensor) faucet controls on all patient room handwashing sinks; confirm faucet type on the plumbing fixture schedule.
3. Add ABHR dispenser locations to the architectural and plumbing drawings at the entry of each patient room as a supplement to the sink; mount at a height accessible per ADA requirements.
4. Confirm the room entry sink is not obstructed by door swing, IV poles, or equipment storage when the room is occupied; show on the furniture/equipment layout overlay.
5. For rooms designated for contact-precaution patients (C. diff, MRSA, etc.), confirm the handwashing sink is soap-and-water capable and that ABHR is used only as a supplement, not a replacement.
code_references: CDC Guidelines for Hand Hygiene in Healthcare Settings

description: ICU and NICU handwashing sink quantity requirements per patient bay or room
violation_template: Plan review comment — Infection Control / Plumbing: The Intensive Care and/or Neonatal Intensive Care Unit shown in the {occupancy} does not demonstrate adequate hand hygiene sink provisions per FGI 2022 §2.1-2.7.4.2. In open-bay ICU and NICU configurations, a minimum of one (1) handwashing sink must be provided per patient bay; the sink must be accessible to caregivers attending the patient without crossing into an adjacent patient space. In single-patient ICU rooms, a handwashing sink must be provided within the room. The plumbing floor plan as submitted either does not show sink locations in the ICU/NICU bays, or the sinks shown are located in a central service area that requires staff to cross patient spaces to access them, which does not satisfy the per-bay requirement.
fix_template:
1. Revise the plumbing floor plan to show one (1) dedicated handwashing sink per ICU/NICU patient bay in open-bay configurations; dimension each sink location and confirm it is accessible without crossing another patient's zone per FGI 2022 §2.1-2.7.4.2.
2. For single-patient ICU rooms, confirm a handwashing sink is located within each room near the room entry; add to the plumbing plan if absent.
3. Specify hands-free faucet controls (sensor, knee, or foot pedal) on all ICU/NICU handwashing sinks; note on the plumbing fixture schedule.
4. Coordinate with the architectural layout to confirm sink locations do not obstruct the 4'-0" clearance at the sides and foot of each ICU bed or the 4'-0" between NICU isolette edges.
5. Confirm hot water temperature at ICU/NICU sinks is thermostatically limited to ≤110°F (43°C) to comply with scald prevention requirements.

description: Piped medical gas outlets at patient bedheads in ICU, OR, ED, and NICU; WAGD at anesthetizing locations
violation_template: Plan review comment — Medical Gas / Mechanical: The {occupancy} medical gas outlet plan does not demonstrate the required piped gas services at all patient care locations per NFPA 99-2021 Chapter 5 and FGI 2022 §2.1-2.7.3. Piped oxygen and medical vacuum are required at each patient bed position in ICU, NICU, ED treatment rooms, and each OR. Medical air is additionally required at each ICU patient space and each OR. Waste Anesthetic Gas Disposal (WAGD) outlets must be provided at each OR table, procedure table, or other anesthetizing location where anesthesia machines or vaporizers will be used. The submitted medical gas plan does not clearly identify outlet types, quantities, and locations at each of these spaces, and WAGD provisions are not shown.
fix_template:
1. Revise the medical gas outlet plan to clearly label outlet type (O2, vacuum, medical air, WAGD, N2O if applicable), quantity, and mounting height at each patient position in ICU, NICU, OR, and ED treatment rooms per NFPA 99-2021 §5.1.
2. For each OR and procedure room with anesthesia, add WAGD outlet rough-ins at each anesthetizing position on the medical gas plan; confirm WAGD system capacity in the WAGD system schematic.
3. Confirm on the medical gas riser diagram and floor plan that medical air outlets are provided at each ICU patient bed and each OR/procedure room anesthetizing location per NFPA 99-2021 §5.1.3.
4. Show manifold/zone valve locations on the medical gas plan; confirm each zone has a labeled valve box outside the patient care area, accessible to zone occupants per NFPA 99-2021 §5.1.11 (see also FGI-MG-002).
5. Coordinate with the headwall/casework drawings to show outlet panel or boom outlet locations within reach of clinical staff at each patient position, and confirm medical gas connections are compatible with DISS or NFPA-compliant connectors.
6. Include a gas outlet quantity schedule summarizing total outlets per gas type per room for plan review verification.

description: Medical gas zone valves must be accessible, labeled, and located outside patient rooms to isolate each floor or zone
violation_template: Plan review comment — Medical Gas / Life Safety: The medical gas zone valve layout shown in the {occupancy} does not demonstrate compliance with NFPA 99-2021 §5.1.11. Zone valves must be provided to allow each medical gas service to be shut off independently for each floor and each zone (nursing unit, surgical suite, etc.) without interrupting service to the remainder of the facility. Valve box locations must be in the corridor or other accessible area outside of patient rooms; valves located inside patient rooms are not permitted because caregivers cannot safely operate them during a gas emergency when a patient occupies the room. Submitted plans do not clearly identify zone valve box locations and the zones each valve controls.
fix_template:
1. Revise the medical gas plan to show all zone valve boxes in corridor locations (or other accessible areas) outside of patient rooms, labeled with the zone(s) and gas type(s) each controls, per NFPA 99-2021 §5.1.11.
2. Confirm each nursing unit/surgical floor can be isolated independently for each gas type (O2, vacuum, medical air, WAGD, N2O) without interrupting gas supply to other floors or units.
3. Add zone valve box identification tags to the medical gas plan legend; include the tag label format (gas type + zone description) that will be used on installed valve boxes.
4. Confirm valve boxes are recessed in the corridor wall or otherwise protected against accidental operation, and that box covers are labeled with the emergency contact procedure (e.g., "EMERGENCY SHUTOFF — Contact Facilities Engineering").
5. Coordinate with the electrical drawings to confirm a zone valve panel or alarm indicator is shown at the nursing station or head-end to monitor gas pressure downstream of each zone valve per NFPA 99-2021 alarm requirements.

description: Emergency generator automatic transfer within 10 seconds and 96-hour fuel supply for Level 1 facilities
violation_template: Plan review comment — Electrical / Life Safety: The emergency power system shown in the {occupancy} does not demonstrate compliance with NFPA 99-2021 §6.4, NFPA 110, and FGI 2022 §2.1-7.2. The automatic transfer switch (ATS) schedule and one-line diagram do not confirm that the Essential Electrical System (EES) life safety and critical branches will be automatically restored within 10 seconds of normal power failure, as required by NFPA 99-2021 §6.4.1.1.6. Additionally, NFPA 110 Level 1 occupancies (hospitals) require a minimum 96-hour on-site fuel supply for emergency generators; the mechanical drawings do not specify a fuel tank capacity sufficient to meet this requirement. Failure to meet these requirements creates life-threatening delays in power restoration to critical patient care equipment and life safety systems.
fix_template:
1. Revise the ATS schedule and one-line diagram to confirm each ATS serving the life safety branch and critical branch is rated to complete automatic transfer within 10 seconds of loss of normal power per NFPA 99-2021 §6.4.1.1.6; document ATS transfer time ratings on the electrical schedule.
2. Calculate total generator runtime capacity: revise the fuel system drawings to show fuel tank(s) sized to provide ≥96 hours of operation at rated load for all essential electrical loads, per NFPA 110 Level 1 requirements; include tank size (gallons) and consumption rate calculation on the mechanical drawings.
3. Show fuel tank location, secondary containment (if >55 gallons), fill connection, and transfer pump on the site and mechanical plans per applicable EPA and local fire code requirements.
4. Confirm on the one-line diagram that the generator is sized (kW) to simultaneously support all life safety, critical, and equipment branch loads; include a load calculation summary.
5. Detail monthly and annual generator exercise/test provisions per NFPA 110 §8.4; note on the electrical drawings where load bank connections are provided for full-load testing.
6. Confirm automatic generator startup, ATS transfer, and restoration alarms are connected to the fire alarm system or BAS annunciator panel per NFPA 99-2021 §6.4.

description: Essential electrical system branch separation: life safety, critical, and equipment branches on separate transfer switches with no cross-loading
violation_template: Plan review comment — Electrical / Life Safety: The Essential Electrical System (EES) design shown in the {occupancy} one-line diagram does not demonstrate required branch separation per NFPA 99-2021 §6.4.2. The EES must be divided into three (3) separate branches — Life Safety Branch, Critical Branch, and Equipment Branch — each served by a dedicated, separate automatic transfer switch (ATS) and distribution panel. No loads from one branch may be served by the ATS or panel of another branch. The submitted one-line diagram indicates that life safety and critical branch loads share a single ATS or that equipment branch loads are commingled with life safety branch circuits, which is a direct violation of NFPA 99-2021 §6.4.2.2. This deficiency could result in non-essential loads delaying or compromising restoration of power to life safety systems.
fix_template:
1. Revise the one-line electrical diagram to show three separate ATSs — one for the Life Safety Branch, one for the Critical Branch, and one for the Equipment Branch — each individually connected to the generator bus per NFPA 99-2021 §6.4.2.
2. Prepare a branch load assignment schedule listing every circuit, panel, and load by branch type; confirm no life safety loads (egress lighting, fire alarm, smoke control, elevator recall) are on the critical or equipment branch, and vice versa.
3. Remove any shared ATS or cross-branch distribution from the one-line diagram; provide separate distribution panels for each branch fed from their respective ATS.
4. Label all EES panels, ATSs, and branch circuits consistently on the one-line diagram, riser diagram, and panel schedules using the nomenclature 'LS' (Life Safety), 'CR' (Critical), and 'EQ' (Equipment) per NFPA 99-2021.
5. Confirm the panel schedules show no mixing of branch loads within any single EES panel, and that each panel is clearly labeled by branch type at its installation location.
6. Coordinate with the mechanical and plumbing drawings to verify that all motor loads (HVAC, medical gas compressors, sterilizers) served by the EES are assigned to the Equipment Branch, unless they serve life safety or critical functions as defined by NFPA 99-2021 §6.4.2.

description: Patient care corridor minimum clear width in inpatient nursing units and surgery suites; stretcher alcove requirements
violation_template: Plan review comment — Architecture / Life Safety: The patient care corridors shown in the {occupancy} inpatient nursing unit(s) and/or surgical suite(s) do not demonstrate the minimum clear width required by FGI 2022 §2.1-2.1.3. Patient care corridors in inpatient nursing units and surgery suites must maintain a minimum clear width of 8'-0" (8 feet), measured between finished wall surfaces or any projecting obstruction (handrails, recessed casework doors, equipment alcoves). Where stretcher alcoves are provided, the corridor must be widened to a minimum of 10'-0" clear at the alcove location to allow a stretcher to be parked without encroaching on the 8'-0" through-corridor. The submitted corridor widths are shown as nominal dimensions that do not account for finish materials, door frames, handrails, or casework projections.
fix_template:
1. Revise the architectural floor plan to dimension all patient care corridor widths as clear (finished face to finished face) dimensions in inpatient nursing units and surgical suites; confirm minimum 8'-0" clear width throughout per FGI 2022 §2.1-2.1.3.
2. Add handrail profiles to the corridor cross-sections or plan to confirm handrails do not reduce the clear width below 8'-0"; if they do, increase corridor width accordingly.
3. For stretcher alcoves, widen the corridor to ≥10'-0" clear at the alcove location and show the alcove depth (minimum 2'-6" from corridor wall) on the floor plan.
4. Confirm door frames, casework, equipment alcove doors, and any projections into the corridor are accounted for in the clear width calculation; revise any location where projections reduce clear width below the minimum.
5. Coordinate with Life Safety/egress drawings per IBC §1005 to confirm corridor exit capacity is maintained with the minimum widths shown, and that occupant load calculations support the corridor widths provided.

description: Medication room requirements: lockable, ventilated, refrigerator, work counter, adequate lighting, and nurse station adjacency
violation_template: Plan review comment — Architecture / Pharmacy: The medication room(s) shown in the {occupancy} do not demonstrate all required design elements per FGI 2022 §2.1-2.3.3.1. Each medication room must be: (1) lockable with an access-controlled door to prevent unauthorized access; (2) mechanically ventilated to positive pressure (or neutral pressure at minimum) relative to the adjacent corridor to prevent odors or contaminants from entering the medication preparation space; (3) provided with a refrigerator dedicated to medication storage; (4) equipped with an adequate work counter surface for medication preparation; and (5) provided with sufficient lighting (minimum 50 foot-candles at the work surface) for safe medication reading and preparation. The submitted plans do not clearly show locking hardware, ventilation pressure relationship, medication refrigerator location, or lighting levels for the medication room(s).
fix_template:
1. Add access control hardware (cipher lock, card reader, or equivalent) to the medication room door on the hardware schedule and architectural drawings; confirm the room is securable against unauthorized entry per FGI 2022 §2.1-2.3.3.1.
2. Revise the mechanical room data sheet for each medication room to confirm positive or neutral pressure relative to the corridor (supply ≥ exhaust) and a minimum of 4 ACH; exhaust should not discharge into the air-handling unit return without filtration per ASHRAE 170-2021 guidance.
3. Show a dedicated medication refrigerator (not a multi-use refrigerator) on the equipment plan for each medication room; confirm power and clearances per manufacturer requirements.
4. Show the work counter configuration on the floor plan, including counter depth and length sufficient for medication labeling and preparation; confirm counter height is ergonomically appropriate and ADA accessible (or a lowered section is provided) per applicable accessibility standards.
5. Add a lighting fixture schedule note confirming minimum 50 foot-candles (540 lux) at the medication counter work surface; provide an illumination calculation or specify a fixture type validated for this level.
6. Confirm the medication room is located adjacent to or within direct sight of the nursing station to facilitate supervision and minimize transport distance, per FGI 2022 §2.1-2.3.3.1 preferred configuration.

description: Occupied hospitals require negative pressure isolation rooms for airborne infection control per HCAI requirements.
violation_template: {occupancy} project includes isolation rooms. Verify negative pressure design (minimum -0.01 in. w.g.) is shown on drawings with pressure differential monitoring and visual indicators at room entry.
fix_template: Provide pressure differential diagram on mechanical drawings. Show monitoring device location and alarm setpoints per Title 24 Part 4 and ASHRAE 170.

description: Operating rooms and procedure rooms require positive pressure with minimum air changes per hour (ACH) and HEPA filtration.
violation_template: Operating/procedure rooms in {occupancy} must maintain positive pressure relative to adjacent corridors with minimum 20 ACH total (4 ACH outside air). HEPA filtration (99.97% at 0.3 micron) is required.
fix_template:
1. Revise mechanical schedules to confirm 20 ACH minimum (4 ACH OA) for OR/procedure rooms.
2. Provide HEPA filter schedule with efficiency rating.
3. Show pressure relationship diagram indicating positive pressure to adjacent spaces.

description: California Seismic Zone D/E hospitals (Ip=1.5) require OSHPD-preapproved seismic anchorage for medical equipment and nonstructural components.
violation_template: Project is in Seismic Zone {seismic_zone}. All nonstructural components (HVAC units, med gas equipment, electrical distribution) must be anchored per CBC Chapter 13 with OSHPD preapproved hardware.
fix_template:
1. Provide seismic anchorage calculations for all equipment >400 lbs or vibration-producing equipment.
2. Specify OSHPD pre-approved anchorage manufacturer and model.
3. Show anchorage details on structural drawings referencing CBC 2022 Chapter 13.

description: Hospitals must have a code-compliant Essential Electrical System (EES) with separated Critical, Life Safety, and Equipment branches.
violation_template: Essential Electrical System for {occupancy} must comply with NFPA 99-2021 Chapter 6 and Title 24 Part 3. Drawings must show three separate EES branches: Life Safety, Critical, and Equipment.
fix_template:
1. Provide single-line diagram clearly labeled with Life Safety, Critical, and Equipment branch separations.
2. Show transfer time ≤10 seconds for Life Safety branch per NFPA 99.
3. Label all receptacles and equipment served by each EES branch on electrical plans.

description: Medical gas systems including oxygen, vacuum, medical air, and WAGD require NFPA 99 compliance with zone valves and master alarm panels.
violation_template: Medical gas systems in {occupancy} must comply with NFPA 99-2021 Chapter 5. Zone valve boxes (ZVBs), master alarm panels (MAPs), and area alarm panels must be shown on drawings.
fix_template:
1. Provide medical gas system riser diagram with ZVB locations.
2. Show MAP location accessible from nursing station.
3. Provide area alarm panel locations per NFPA 99 Section 5.1.9.
4. Note gas outlet types and quantities per room schedule.

description: Healthcare facilities require ASSE 1070 thermostatic mixing valves at patient-use fixtures to prevent Legionella and scalding.
violation_template: Patient-accessible lavatories and showers in {occupancy} require ASSE 1070-compliant thermostatic mixing valves with 110°F maximum delivery temperature to prevent scalding and Legionella growth.
fix_template:
1. Specify ASSE 1070 mixing valves at all patient-accessible fixtures.
2. Set domestic hot water supply at 140°F minimum (Legionella control) with point-of-use tempering to 110°F max.
3. Provide water temperature management plan per Title 22 CCR.

description: ICU patient rooms require minimum 6 ACH outside air and controlled pressure relationships per ASHRAE 170.
violation_template: ICU/NICU patient rooms in {occupancy} require minimum 6 ACH outside air with positive pressure to corridor per ASHRAE 170 Table 7.1. Current drawings do not confirm compliance.
fix_template:
1. Update mechanical schedules to show 6 ACH OA minimum for ICU rooms.
2. Provide pressure relationship diagram showing positive pressure (+0.01 in. w.g. min).
3. Confirm 100% exhaust — no air recirculation from ICU patient rooms.

description: Hospital patient corridors must maintain minimum 8-foot clear width for emergency egress and equipment movement.
violation_template: Patient care corridors in {occupancy} must maintain minimum 8-foot (96-inch) clear width per CBC Section 1005.1 Exception 5 and Title 24 Part 2 Section 1224.1. Verify corridor widths are unobstructed.
fix_template:
1. Dimension all patient care corridors on architectural plans.
2. Show 8-foot minimum clear width (96 inches) unobstructed.
3. Coordinate medical equipment alcoves and nurse stations to maintain required clear width.

description: Patient rooms, restrooms, and public areas must comply with CBC Chapter 11B accessibility requirements.
violation_template: Patient rooms and associated toilet rooms must comply with CBC Chapter 11B accessibility requirements including turning radius, grab bars, knee clearances, and door hardware.
fix_template:
1. Provide accessibility compliance notes on architectural drawings referencing CBC Chapter 11B.
2. Show 60-inch turning diameter in patient toilet rooms.
3. Dimension grab bar locations and heights (33"-36" AFF).
4. Specify lever door hardware throughout accessible routes.

description: Scrub sinks adjacent to ORs must be hands-free operable and meet minimum quantity requirements per FGI Guidelines.
violation_template: Scrub sink stations adjacent to operating/procedure rooms in {occupancy} must be hands-free (knee or sensor-actuated) with minimum one scrub station per OR per FGI Guidelines 2018.
fix_template:
1. Specify hands-free scrub sinks (knee/sensor actuated) at each OR.
2. Locate scrub sinks adjacent to OR entry — confirm on floor plans.
3. Provide minimum one scrub station per operating room.
4. Note ASSE 1070 compliance for water temperature.

description: Suspended ceilings in patient care areas must be seismically restrained per OSHPD requirements.
violation_template: Suspended ceiling systems in patient care areas of {occupancy} (Seismic Zone {seismic_zone}) require seismic restraint per CBC Chapter 25 and OSHPD-preapproved ceiling system documentation.
fix_template:
1. Specify OSHPD pre-approved seismic ceiling system (e.g., USG Donn DX or equivalent).
2. Provide ceiling suspension details with seismic bracing per CBC Chapter 25.
3. Show hanger wire spacing, perimeter angle, and seismic bracing on reflected ceiling plans.

description: Smoke compartmentalization is required in hospitals with corridor smoke barriers at maximum 200-foot intervals.
violation_template: Smoke barriers in {occupancy} must divide the building into smoke compartments not exceeding 22,500 sq ft with maximum 200-foot travel distance per CBC Section 407.4 and Title 24 Part 2.
fix_template:
1. Show smoke barrier locations on all floor plans.
2. Dimension smoke compartments — confirm ≤22,500 sq ft and ≤200 ft travel distance.
3. Specify smoke-rated door assemblies (S-rated) at smoke barrier openings.
4. Show smoke damper locations at HVAC penetrations of smoke barriers.

description: Sterile Processing Departments (SPD) require a minimum of 4 ACH outside air with negative pressure and specific air distribution.
violation_template: Sterile Processing / Soiled Utility areas in {occupancy} require negative pressure with minimum 10 ACH total air changes. Decontamination area must be at negative pressure relative to clean areas.
fix_template:
1. Show negative pressure in decontamination/soiled areas relative to clean/sterile areas.
2. Confirm 10 ACH minimum total air changes in mechanical schedules.
3. Provide pressure relationship diagram showing airflow direction from clean to soiled.

description: Hospital pharmacies with compounding areas require ISO Class 7 cleanroom conditions with HEPA filtration.
violation_template: Pharmacy compounding areas in {occupancy} require ISO Class 7 cleanroom environment with HEPA-filtered supply air, positive pressure, and 30 ACH minimum per USP <797> and ASHRAE 170.
fix_template:
1. Provide ISO Class 7 cleanroom specifications for pharmacy compounding room.
2. Show HEPA filters (99.97% efficiency) in supply air system.
3. Confirm positive pressure relative to adjacent areas.
4. Note 30 ACH minimum in mechanical schedule.
5. Reference USP <797> and <800> compliance on drawings.

description: Patient care areas require redundant branch circuits with isolated ground receptacles and GFCI protection per NFPA 99.
violation_template: Patient care areas in {occupancy} require a minimum of two individual circuits from separate branch panels per NFPA 99. Isolated ground receptacles (orange face) are required in wet locations (ORs, procedure rooms).
fix_template:
1. Show minimum two branch circuits from separate panels at each patient bed.
2. Specify isolated ground receptacles (IG) in OR and procedure rooms.
3. Label receptacle types and circuit sources on electrical plans.
4. Coordinate with EES branch requirements per NFPA 99 Chapter 6.

description: Storm shelter / FEMA P-361 safe room required for new hospitals in tornado-prone regions (Zone V+)
violation_template: The submitted construction documents for the {occupancy} located in {county} County do not include provisions for a FEMA P-361 compliant storm shelter or safe room as required for new hospital construction in Texas tornado-prone regions (Zone V and above). Texas Health & Safety Code §241.026 and DSHS Chapter 133 mandate that staff shelter facilities meeting FEMA P-361 performance criteria be incorporated into the facility design. The current drawings lack designation of a safe room location, structural detailing to FEMA P-361 wind speed criteria (250 mph), and documentation of occupant capacity calculations for all on-duty staff.
fix_template:
1. Designate a FEMA P-361 compliant safe room on the floor plan with occupant capacity sufficient to shelter all staff on peak shift; submit updated architectural drawings showing safe room location, dimensions, and adjacency to staff work areas.
2. Provide structural calculations demonstrating compliance with FEMA P-361 wind speed criteria (250 mph, 3-second gust) and debris impact resistance requirements, stamped by a Texas-licensed structural engineer.
3. Submit a safe room occupancy analysis documenting the number of staff positions per shift and confirming the safe room square footage meets FEMA P-361 Table 4-1 minimum area-per-occupant requirements.
4. Include signage plan and emergency procedures document indicating safe room activation protocols in the life safety drawings package.
5. Reference: Texas Health & Safety Code §241.026, 25 TAC §133 Subchapter B, FEMA P-361 (2015 or current edition).
code_references: FEMA P-361 Safe Rooms for Tornadoes and Hurricanes

description: Wind design and impact-resistant glazing for coastal Texas counties in wind-borne debris regions (Exposure D)
violation_template: The construction documents for the {occupancy} in {county} County, a coastal Texas county located within an ASCE 7 wind-borne debris region (Exposure Category D), do not specify impact-resistant glazing or approved opening protection as required by the Texas Building Code §1609 and 25 TAC §133.162. All exterior glazing in wind-borne debris regions must meet ASTM E1996 and ASTM E1886 large-missile impact resistance standards, or be protected by approved storm shutters meeting equivalent criteria. The window and curtain wall schedules submitted do not identify impact ratings, and no opening protection plan has been provided.
fix_template:
1. Revise the window and curtain wall schedule to specify glazing products tested and labeled per ASTM E1996 (large missile, Zone 4 or 5 as applicable) and ASTM E1886 for all exterior openings in wind-borne debris regions.
2. Submit manufacturer's product data sheets and independent test reports confirming impact resistance ratings for all proposed glazing assemblies.
3. Provide ASCE 7 wind load calculations with site-specific wind speed from the Texas Building Code wind speed maps, stamped by a Texas-licensed engineer, confirming design wind pressures for the coastal exposure category.
4. If storm shutters are proposed as an alternative, submit a shutter schedule with deployment procedures, hardware details, and test certification to the same ASTM standards.
5. Reference: Texas Building Code §1609, ASCE 7-22 Chapter 26-30, ASTM E1996, ASTM E1886, 25 TAC §133.162.

description: Complete automatic fire sprinkler system (NFPA 13) required throughout all new Texas-licensed hospitals per NFPA 101-2018 with Texas amendments
violation_template: The construction documents for the {occupancy} in {county} County do not provide a complete automatic fire sprinkler system designed and installed in accordance with NFPA 13 as required by 25 TAC §133.162 and the Texas edition of NFPA 101 (2018). All new Texas-licensed hospital construction must include total coverage automatic sprinkler protection throughout the building, including attic spaces exceeding 3 feet in height, elevator machine rooms, mechanical penthouses, and all accessory occupancies. The submitted drawings are either silent on sprinkler coverage in specific areas or indicate partial systems that do not meet the total-coverage mandate.
fix_template:
1. Revise the fire protection drawings to show automatic fire sprinkler coverage throughout all areas of the facility per NFPA 13, including attic spaces >3 ft, elevator machine rooms, mechanical/electrical rooms, and all accessory spaces.
2. Provide a sprinkler system hydraulic calculation summary stamped by a NICET Level III or licensed fire protection engineer demonstrating compliance with NFPA 13 density/area requirements for the applicable hazard classification.
3. Submit a fire protection design narrative describing system type (wet pipe, dry pipe, pre-action) for each zone, water supply source, and backflow prevention configuration.
4. Coordinate sprinkler head locations with reflected ceiling plans to confirm coverage is not obstructed by HVAC diffusers, light fixtures, or equipment per NFPA 13 Chapter 10.
5. Reference: 25 TAC §133.162, NFPA 101-2018 §18.3.5, NFPA 13-2019.

description: Texas hospitals must maintain 96-hour on-site fuel supply for essential electrical system generator with transfer time ≤10 seconds
violation_template: The construction documents for the {occupancy} in {county} County do not demonstrate compliance with the Texas DSHS requirement for a minimum 96-hour on-site fuel supply for the essential electrical system emergency generator as required by 25 TAC §133.162 and NFPA 110. The submitted electrical drawings and specifications indicate a fuel storage capacity insufficient to sustain generator operation for 96 consecutive hours at full essential load demand. Additionally, the automatic transfer switch sequence documentation does not confirm the required ≤10-second transfer time from normal to emergency power for life safety and critical branch circuits.
fix_template:
1. Recalculate fuel storage requirements based on the full essential electrical system load (kW) and the engine-generator set fuel consumption rate (gal/hr at 100% load), and revise tank sizing to provide ≥96-hour runtime; submit updated fuel storage specifications and tank sizing calculations.
2. Confirm automatic transfer switch (ATS) type and settings to achieve ≤10-second transfer time for Life Safety Branch per NFPA 110 §6.4; provide ATS product data sheets and sequence-of-operations narrative.
3. Fuel storage design and tank installation must comply with NFPA 30 (Flammable and Combustible Liquids Code); submit secondary containment, leak detection, and fill/vent detail drawings.
4. Provide a load analysis for all essential electrical system branches (Life Safety, Critical, Equipment) per NFPA 99 and coordinate with the mechanical engineer to include HVAC loads on emergency circuits.
5. Reference: 25 TAC §133.162, NFPA 110-2019 §6.4 and §8.3, NFPA 99-2021 §6.4, NFPA 30.

description: Dedicated N+1 redundant HVAC system for surgical suite required for all Texas-licensed hospital operating rooms
violation_template: The mechanical design for the {occupancy} surgical suite in {county} County does not provide the dedicated, non-shared HVAC system with N+1 (100% standby) air handling unit redundancy required by 25 TAC §133.162 and DSHS Architectural Guidelines for Texas-licensed hospital operating rooms. The submitted drawings indicate that the surgical suite AHU serves both operating rooms and non-surgical areas, which is prohibited, and no standby AHU with automatic failover capability is shown. The documented design conditions do not confirm maintenance of 68–73°F dry-bulb temperature and 30–60% relative humidity throughout all operating modes.
fix_template:
1. Redesign the surgical suite HVAC system to be fully dedicated (no supply air shared with non-surgical occupancies) with a minimum of two equal-capacity air handling units configured for N+1 redundancy with automatic failover controls; update HVAC drawings and equipment schedules accordingly.
2. Provide duct layout and air balance calculations demonstrating that each operating room will maintain 20 total air changes per hour (minimum 4 outdoor air ACH) under normal and standby AHU conditions.
3. Submit controls sequence-of-operations documenting automatic transfer to standby AHU upon primary unit failure, including failover time and alarm notification to nursing/facilities staff.
4. Confirm room pressurization (positive), temperature range (68–73°F), and humidity range (30–60% RH) are maintained throughout all operating modes; provide psychrometric analysis if required.
5. Reference: 25 TAC §133.162, DSHS Hospital Architectural Guidelines, FGI 2022 Table 2.1-2, ASHRAE 170-2021 Table 7.1.

description: Written ICRA plan (minimum Class III/IV) required with construction documents for projects in or adjacent to occupied patient care areas
violation_template: The construction documents submitted for the {occupancy} renovation or addition in {county} County do not include a written Infection Control Risk Assessment (ICRA) plan as required by 25 TAC §133.41 and DSHS Hospital Licensing Standards for any project located in or immediately adjacent to occupied patient care areas. Texas DSHS requires a minimum ICRA Class III or Class IV plan — prepared jointly by the infection preventionist, project manager, and contractor — to be submitted with construction documents prior to DSHS review approval. The submitted package contains neither the ICRA risk matrix nor the corresponding infection control mitigation measures.
fix_template:
1. Prepare a written ICRA document using the ICRA matrix to classify the construction activity type and patient risk group; determine the required ICRA class (minimum Class III for projects adjacent to patient care; Class IV for immunocompromised patient areas) and submit with the construction documents.
2. The ICRA plan must be signed by the hospital's Infection Preventionist and include: project description, construction activity class, patient risk group classification, required control measures (barriers, pressure relationships, air filtration), and monitoring protocols.
3. Include on the construction drawings a phasing plan with physical barrier locations, identification of interim negative pressure or HEPA filtration requirements, and designated construction worker egress routes that avoid patient care corridors.
4. Submit an ICRA inspection and monitoring log template that will be used by the contractor throughout construction and made available to DSHS surveyors upon request.
5. Reference: 25 TAC §133.41, DSHS Hospital Licensing Standards, APIC Implementation Guide for ICRA, FGI 2022 Appendix 1.A.

description: Phased construction in occupied hospitals requires physical barriers, negative pressure anterooms, and HEPA air scrubbers per ICRA Class IV; daily inspection log required
violation_template: The submitted phasing plan and construction documents for the occupied {occupancy} project in {county} County do not adequately demonstrate ICRA Class IV infection control measures as required by 25 TAC §133.41 for construction occurring within or immediately adjacent to occupied patient care areas. The drawings do not show sealed, floor-to-deck physical barriers at the construction boundary, negative pressure anterooms at each entry point to the construction zone, or HEPA-filtered air scrubber placement and quantities sufficient to achieve the required number of air changes per hour in the construction area. A daily contractor inspection log — required to be maintained on-site and available to DSHS surveyors — has not been referenced in the contract documents.
fix_template:
1. Add a dedicated infection control phasing sheet to the construction documents showing the location, type (hard-wall or heavy-duty poly), and height (floor-to-structural deck, sealed) of all construction zone barriers, including all penetrations for utilities sealed with fire-rated materials.
2. Designate a negative pressure anteroom (minimum 25 SF clear area) at each construction zone entry point; provide HVAC or portable unit specifications confirming negative pressure of at least -0.01 in. WG relative to adjacent patient areas.
3. Calculate required HEPA air scrubber capacity (minimum 12 air changes per hour for the construction zone volume) and show unit locations on the plan; submit equipment specifications confirming HEPA filtration to 0.3 micron at 99.97% efficiency.
4. Include a requirement in the project specifications (Division 01) for the contractor to maintain a daily ICRA inspection log documenting barrier integrity, negative pressure readings, HEPA unit operation, and any incidents; log must be retained on-site and provided to DSHS on request.
5. Reference: 25 TAC §133.41, DSHS Hospital Licensing Standards, APIC ICRA Implementation Guide Class IV requirements.

description: DSHS plan review submission requirements: Form H-111, site plan, floor plan, equipment schedule, and applicable MEP drawings required prior to construction
violation_template: The construction documents submitted for the {occupancy} project in {county} County are incomplete for DSHS Health Facility Compliance Division plan review as required by 25 TAC §133.163. A complete submittal must include: a completed and signed Form H-111 (Project Notification and Plan Review Application), civil/site plan, dimensioned floor plan(s) with room use labels, a complete equipment schedule identifying medical equipment, and applicable mechanical, electrical, and plumbing engineering drawings. The current submission is missing one or more of these required components, and DSHS cannot complete its review until all required documents are received.
fix_template:
1. Complete and submit DSHS Form H-111 (Project Notification and Plan Review Application) signed by the project architect or engineer of record and the hospital administrator or authorized representative.
2. Provide a fully dimensioned architectural floor plan(s) at a minimum scale of 1/8" = 1'-0" with all rooms labeled by function, door swings shown, and room areas (SF) indicated for each patient care room and support space.
3. Submit a civil/site plan showing building footprint, property lines, parking, utility connections, and accessible routes per TAS (Texas Accessibility Standards).
4. Include a complete equipment schedule listing all major fixed medical equipment (imaging, surgical tables, sterilizers) with utility connection requirements (electrical, medical gas, plumbing) and clearance zones.
5. Provide mechanical, electrical, and plumbing engineering drawings sufficient to demonstrate compliance with 25 TAC §133.162 and applicable codes; reference: 25 TAC §133.163, DSHS Health Facility Compliance Plan Review Guide.
code_references: DSHS Health Facility Compliance Plan Review Guide

description: Nurse station visibility: direct line-of-sight or electronic monitoring to each patient room door; nursing units >30 beds require 2 or more stations
violation_template: The nursing unit floor plan for the {occupancy} in {county} County does not demonstrate compliance with 25 TAC §133.162, which requires each nurse station to maintain direct line-of-sight or approved electronic monitoring capability (closed-circuit video) to each patient room door within the nursing unit. The submitted floor plan indicates patient rooms that are not visible from the nurse station due to corridor bends or wing configurations, and no video monitoring system is shown or specified. Additionally, the nursing unit exceeds 30 licensed beds but provides only one nurse station, contrary to the requirement for two stations or an approved satellite station configuration.
fix_template:
1. Revise the floor plan to demonstrate direct line-of-sight from the nurse station to each patient room door; where geometry prevents direct sightlines, add a CCTV/video monitoring station at the nurse station covering all patient room doors in the affected corridor.
2. If the nursing unit contains more than 30 licensed beds, add a second nurse station or a fully equipped satellite nurse station at the opposite end of the unit; show staffing zones on the floor plan.
3. Submit a video monitoring system narrative describing camera coverage, monitor locations at the nurse station(s), recording capability, and HIPAA-compliant privacy provisions.
4. Confirm nurse station counter height, knee space, and sight-line elevation are compatible with staff working both seated and standing, and consistent with ADA/TAS accessibility requirements.
5. Reference: 25 TAC §133.162, DSHS Hospital Licensing Standards §133.162(e), FGI 2022 §2.2-2.2.1.

description: Piped medical gas outlets (O2, vacuum, WAGD, medical air) required in ALL procedure rooms where anesthesia or sedation may be administered
violation_template: The medical gas and vacuum systems drawings for the {occupancy} in {county} County do not provide piped medical gas outlets in all procedure rooms where anesthesia or conscious sedation may be administered, as required by 25 TAC §133.162 and NFPA 99. Texas DSHS requires that oxygen (O2), medical-grade vacuum, waste anesthetic gas disposal (WAGD), and medical air outlets be provided at each procedure room location where inhalation anesthesia or moderate/deep sedation agents may be used — this requirement is not limited to designated operating rooms but extends to endoscopy suites, cardiac catheterization labs, interventional radiology, and bronchoscopy rooms. The current drawings show cylinder connections or portable equipment in lieu of piped systems in one or more of these locations.
fix_template:
1. Identify all rooms in the facility where anesthesia or sedation (including moderate/conscious sedation) may be administered and list them in the medical gas design narrative; confirm piped O2, medical vacuum, WAGD, and medical air outlets are provided at each location per NFPA 99 §5.1.
2. Revise medical gas piping plans to extend piped systems to all identified procedure rooms; show outlet quantity, type (DISS, quick-connect), and mounting height per NFPA 99 and manufacturer requirements.
3. Provide WAGD system design with dedicated exhaust fan, capacity calculations, and connection to each anesthesia machine or scavenging interface in every applicable procedure room.
4. Submit medical gas system design documentation per NFPA 99 Chapter 5, including pipe sizing calculations, source equipment sizing (manifolds, compressors, vacuum pumps) accounting for all new outlets.
5. Reference: 25 TAC §133.162, NFPA 99-2021 §5.1, FGI 2022 Table 2.1-5 (Medical Gas Outlets).

description: Medication pass-through window or secured medication cart alcove with direct sight line from nurse station required for nursing units >20 beds
violation_template: The nursing unit floor plan for the {occupancy} in {county} County, which exceeds 20 licensed beds, does not include a medication pass-through window or a secured medication cart alcove accessible from the patient corridor with a direct sight line from the nurse station, as required by 25 TAC §133.162. Texas DSHS regulations require that medication distribution be observable from the nurse station to support patient safety and controlled substance oversight. The submitted drawings show a medication room with a single door opening away from the nurse station, with no pass-through window or recessed cart alcove, and no unobstructed visual connection to the nurse station.
fix_template:
1. Add a medication pass-through window between the medication room and the patient corridor, positioned with a direct sight line from the nurse station; provide a detail drawing showing the window dimensions (minimum 18" wide x 24" tall clear opening), counter height, and locking hardware.
2. Alternatively, provide a recessed medication cart alcove (minimum 3'-6" wide x 2'-0" deep) in the patient corridor within the nurse station's line of sight, with a lockable enclosure and electrical outlet for powered medication carts.
3. Confirm the medication room or alcove is equipped with a controlled-access door lock (card reader or keypad) per DEA requirements for Schedule II controlled substance storage.
4. Show the sight line from the nurse station to the medication pass-through or alcove on the floor plan using a dashed line or sight-line diagram annotation.
5. Reference: 25 TAC §133.162, DSHS Hospital Licensing Standards, Texas State Board of Pharmacy regulations.
code_references: Texas State Board of Pharmacy Regulations

description: Hospital HVAC systems must meet Texas IECC 2021 energy efficiency requirements; mechanical commissioning report required at project closeout
violation_template: The mechanical design documents for the {occupancy} in {county} County do not demonstrate compliance with the Texas IECC 2021 energy efficiency requirements applicable to hospital HVAC systems, as required by 25 TAC §133.162. The submitted mechanical drawings and specifications do not include an IECC compliance form, equipment efficiency documentation (minimum EER/COP per IECC 2021 Table C403.3), or a mechanical commissioning scope confirming that a commissioning report will be prepared and submitted to DSHS at project closeout. Texas DSHS requires the commissioning report to be on file before issuing final licensure approval for new or substantially renovated hospital facilities.
fix_template:
1. Prepare and submit a Texas IECC 2021 Mechanical Compliance Form (COMcheck or equivalent) demonstrating that all HVAC equipment meets or exceeds the minimum efficiency requirements in IECC 2021 Table C403.3 for the applicable climate zone.
2. Revise mechanical specifications (MasterFormat Division 23) to require a commissioning authority (CxA) and commissioning scope covering air handling units, chillers, cooling towers, boilers, VAV systems, and building automation system (BAS) sequences.
3. Add a commissioning plan requirement in the project specifications stating that a final commissioning report — including functional performance test results, air and water balance reports, and training records — will be submitted to DSHS prior to final licensure inspection.
4. Confirm that HVAC controls include demand-controlled ventilation (DCV) where required by IECC 2021 §C403.8 and that economizer provisions are addressed for the applicable climate zone.
5. Reference: Texas IECC 2021 (as adopted by the Texas State Energy Conservation Office), 25 TAC §133.162, ASHRAE Standard 202-2018 (Commissioning Process).

description: As-built floor plans showing each licensed bed location, room dimensions, toilet room configuration, and clearances required to be filed with DSHS prior to licensure
violation_template: The construction documents for the {occupancy} in {county} County do not include as-built (or construction document) floor plans that sufficiently document each proposed licensed bed location with the information required by 25 TAC §133.163 for DSHS licensure. Texas DSHS requires that floor plans filed prior to licensure show each licensed bed position with room clear dimensions, required clearances at the head, foot, and sides of each bed, toilet room configuration (private vs. shared), and accessible route from bed to toilet. The submitted plans do not dimensionally verify minimum room sizes per DSHS standards (minimum 100 SF clear area for single-bed rooms; 80 SF/bed for multi-bed rooms) nor show required clearances.
fix_template:
1. Revise patient room floor plans to show each licensed bed position with dimension strings confirming minimum clear floor area: 100 SF for private rooms, 80 SF per bed for semi-private rooms (excluding toilet room and fixed casework).
2. Annotate required clearances on the floor plan: minimum 36" at the head of bed (wall to bed), 24" on one side, and 36" on the transfer/accessible side; confirm compliance at each bed position.
3. Show the toilet room configuration for each patient room: label as private (within room) or shared (Jack-and-Jill between rooms); confirm accessible toilet rooms meet TAS Chapter 603 requirements with grab bar blocking shown.
4. Submit a licensed bed count summary table on the drawings listing each patient room number, bed count, room type, and toilet room type; total must match the requested licensed bed count on DSHS Form H-111.
5. Reference: 25 TAC §133.163, 25 TAC §133.162, DSHS Hospital Architectural Guidelines, FGI 2022 §2.2-2.1.1.

description: Smoke compartments must not exceed 22,500 SF; cross-corridor smoke barrier doors required at maximum 200-foot intervals on inpatient floors
violation_template: The fire and life safety drawings for the {occupancy} in {county} County do not demonstrate compliance with the smoke compartmentation requirements of 25 TAC §133.162 and NFPA 101-2018 §18.3.7. One or more smoke compartments on the inpatient floors exceed the 22,500 SF maximum area limit, and cross-corridor smoke barrier doors are not provided at maximum 200-foot intervals along the length of inpatient corridors. Smoke barrier walls are required to extend from the floor to the underside of the floor or roof deck above and must provide a minimum 1-hour fire resistance rating with smoke-rated door assemblies (S-label) at all corridor crossings.
fix_template:
1. Revise the life safety floor plan to delineate smoke compartment boundaries such that no compartment exceeds 22,500 SF; annotate each compartment with its area in SF on the drawing.
2. Add cross-corridor smoke barrier doors at intervals not exceeding 200 feet along all inpatient corridors; show door locations on the life safety plan with door hardware designation confirming automatic hold-open with smoke detector release (per NFPA 101 §18.3.7.5).
3. Provide wall sections and details for all smoke barrier walls confirming 1-hour fire-resistance-rated construction (tested per ASTM E119 or UL 263), extending continuously from floor to underside of floor or roof deck, with all penetrations sealed by listed firestop systems.
4. Schedule all smoke barrier doors as minimum 1-3/4" solid-core, 20-minute fire-rated with 'S' smoke label, self-closing and positive-latching hardware, and confirm corridor width is maintained through the door pairs per NFPA 101 §18.2.3.
5. Reference: 25 TAC §133.162, NFPA 101-2018 §18.3.7, NFPA 101-2018 §18.2.3.
