description: Texas-licensed birthing center LDR rooms must provide minimum 300 SF clear area with private toilet/shower within or immediately adjacent to each LDR room
violation_template: The LDR (Labor, Delivery, and Recovery) room floor plan for the {occupancy} in {county} County does not meet the minimum room size and toilet facility requirements of 25 TAC §137 (Birthing Centers) and DSHS Architectural Guidelines. Each LDR room in a Texas-licensed birthing center or hospital birthing unit must provide a minimum 300 SF of clear floor area (excluding toilet room, vestibule, and fixed casework) with a private toilet room and shower accessible directly from within the LDR room or through a private vestibule immediately adjacent to it. The submitted plans show LDR rooms with insufficient clear floor area and/or toilet rooms shared between LDR rooms, which is not permitted.
fix_template:
1. Revise LDR room floor plans to confirm a minimum 300 SF clear area per room, measured from the interior face of walls and excluding the toilet room, entry vestibule, and fixed cabinetry; annotate the clear area on each room plan.
2. Provide a private toilet room with shower (or tub/shower combination) for each LDR room, accessible directly from within the room or through a private vestibule exclusively serving that LDR room; shared toilet rooms between two LDR rooms are not acceptable under 25 TAC §137.
3. Confirm the toilet room meets TAS (Texas Accessibility Standards) accessible toilet room requirements per TAS Chapter 603 with grab bars at toilet, shower seat, and shower controls within accessible reach.
4. Show medical gas outlets (O2, vacuum), emergency call system, and fetal monitoring equipment connection points within the LDR room consistent with 25 TAC §137 equipment requirements.
5. Reference: 25 TAC §137 (Birthing Centers), DSHS Birthing Center Architectural Guidelines, FGI 2022 §2.2-3.5, Texas Accessibility Standards Chapter 603.

description: All Texas-licensed hospitals, including critical access hospitals, must provide at minimum one airborne infection isolation (AII) room meeting FGI 2022 requirements regardless of bed count
violation_template: The construction documents for the {occupancy} in {county} County do not include an airborne infection isolation (AII) room meeting FGI 2022 and ASHRAE 170-2021 requirements as mandated by 25 TAC §133.162 and 25 TAC §169 for all Texas-licensed hospitals, including critical access hospitals, regardless of bed count. Texas DSHS requires a minimum of one AII room per facility that provides continuous negative pressure (minimum -0.01 in. WG relative to the corridor), a minimum of 12 total air changes per hour (2 outdoor air ACH minimum), HEPA-filtered exhaust or direct outdoor exhaust with no recirculation, a self-closing entry door, and an anteroom. The submitted plans do not designate any room as an AII room or provide the required ventilation parameters.
fix_template:
1. Designate at least one patient room on the floor plan as a full-compliance AII room per FGI 2022 §2.2-2.1.2 and ASHRAE 170-2021; label it 'Airborne Infection Isolation Room' with the required ventilation parameters noted on the drawing.
2. Provide mechanical design documentation for the AII room confirming: continuous negative pressure of -0.01 in. WG (minimum) relative to the adjacent corridor, monitored by a visual pressure indicator (Magnehelic gauge or electronic monitor) visible from the corridor; 12 total ACH (minimum 2 outdoor ACH); and 100% exhaust air with no recirculation.
3. Design the AII room exhaust to discharge directly to the outside at a location per ASHRAE 170-2021 §7.2 (minimum 25 feet from any air intake, pedestrian area, or operable window), or provide HEPA filtration on the exhaust where direct outdoor discharge is not feasible.
4. Include an anteroom of minimum 30 SF between the AII room and the corridor with its own HVAC supply/exhaust maintaining slight negative pressure relative to the corridor and positive pressure relative to the AII room (directional airflow to contain pathogens).
5. Reference: 25 TAC §133.162, 25 TAC §169 (Critical Access Hospitals), FGI 2022 §2.2-2.1.2, ASHRAE 170-2021 Table 7.1, CDC Guidelines for Environmental Infection Control.
code_references: CDC Guidelines for Environmental Infection Control in Health-Care Facilities

description: Operating room ventilation must meet NYSDOH-enhanced ACH and HEPA filtration requirements exceeding FGI baseline
violation_template: NYSDOH PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — INFECTION CONTROL / MECHANICAL: The submitted mechanical drawings for the operating room(s) indicate a total air change rate of fewer than 25 ACH, which does not comply with 10 NYCRR §711.2(a)(7) and NYSDOH DAL 10-04. New York State requires a minimum of 25 total air changes per hour (ACH) in all {occupancy} operating rooms, which exceeds the FGI 2022 baseline of 20 ACH. Additionally, all OR supply air must pass through HEPA filtration (minimum 99.97% efficiency at 0.3 microns) prior to delivery to the space; no exceptions are permitted for new construction or major renovation. Failure to provide HEPA-filtered, 25-ACH ventilation in the OR(s) constitutes a material deficiency under NYS Health Code and will result in a disapproval of the submitted construction documents.
fix_template:
1. Revise mechanical schedules and plans to reflect a minimum of 25 total air changes per hour (ACH) in all operating rooms, with a minimum of 20 outdoor ACH as required by NYSDOH DAL 10-04 and 10 NYCRR §711.2(a)(7).
2. Add HEPA filtration units (99.97% efficiency at 0.3 microns) to all OR supply air handling units or terminal boxes; clearly indicate HEPA filter locations and access panels on mechanical drawings.
3. Provide a ventilation schedule table on the drawings listing each OR by room number, supply CFM, exhaust CFM, total ACH, outdoor ACH, pressurization relationship (positive), filtration level, and temperature/humidity setpoints.
4. Submit updated mechanical calculations demonstrating compliance with NYSDOH 25 ACH requirement, signed and sealed by a licensed NYS Professional Engineer.
5. Reference NYSDOH DAL 10-04 and 10 NYCRR §711.2(a)(7) explicitly in the code analysis portion of the NYSDOH OHSM project application submittal.

description: All patient care areas in NYS psychiatric and behavioral health units must use fully ligature-resistant hardware, plumbing, lighting, and door hardware throughout
violation_template: NYSDOH PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — BEHAVIORAL HEALTH SAFETY: The submitted construction documents for the {occupancy} psychiatric/behavioral health unit do not demonstrate compliance with NYSDOH ligature-resistance requirements as required by 10 NYCRR Part 599 and NYSDOH DAL 17-03. New York State mandates that ALL patient care areas within licensed psychiatric and behavioral health units employ ligature-resistant hardware (door handles, hinges, closers), plumbing fixtures (faucets, shower valves, drains), light fixtures (fully recessed or ligature-resistant vandal-resistant), and door hardware (no exposed screws, loops, or anchor points capable of supporting body weight). These requirements exceed the standard hospital construction requirements and apply to all new construction and major renovation projects in {county} County. Drawings must include product cut sheets and a room-by-room ligature-resistance compliance matrix demonstrating that every patient-accessible surface and fixture meets the NYSDOH standard.
fix_template:
1. Provide a complete ligature-resistance compliance matrix (spreadsheet or table on drawings) listing every patient-accessible room, each fixture/hardware type, the specified product, and its certified ligature-resistance rating.
2. Replace all standard door hardware (levers, hinges, closers) throughout patient care areas with NYSDOH-approved ligature-resistant equivalents; provide manufacturer cut sheets demonstrating ligature resistance per NYSDOH DAL 17-03 Appendix A criteria.
3. Specify ligature-resistant plumbing fixtures for all patient-accessible lavatories, toilets, and showers; exposed supply lines and drain configurations must be anti-anchor type; submit plumbing fixture schedule with product data.
4. Revise electrical/lighting plans to show fully recessed or ligature-resistant vandal-resistant light fixtures in all patient care areas; surface-mounted fixtures with exposed attachment points are not acceptable.
5. Coordinate with NYSDOH Office of Mental Health (OMH) reviewer concurrently with OHSM review; attach OMH pre-approval letter to the NYSDOH OHSM construction application.
code_references: VA Ligature Risk Reduction Design Guide (reference standard)

description: New York emergency departments must include a dedicated HAZMAT/chemical decontamination room or shower station for a minimum of 2 patients simultaneously
violation_template: NYSDOH PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS: The submitted emergency department drawings for the {occupancy} facility in {county} County do not indicate a dedicated HAZMAT/chemical patient decontamination room or decontamination shower station as required by 10 NYCRR §711.2 and NYSDOH Emergency Preparedness requirements. New York State mandates that all licensed hospital emergency departments provide a dedicated decontamination space capable of simultaneously decontaminating a minimum of two (2) patients following HAZMAT or chemical exposure incidents. The required decontamination room must include dedicated negative-pressure exhaust separate from the general ED HVAC system, a floor drain connected to an isolated containment system (not the sanitary sewer without treatment), physical separation from clean patient care areas, and access from an exterior entry point to avoid contaminating the main ED. This deficiency constitutes a life-safety and emergency preparedness non-compliance that must be resolved prior to NYSDOH approval.
fix_template:
1. Add a dedicated decontamination room or decontamination shower station to the ED floor plan, sized to accommodate simultaneous decontamination of at least two (2) adult patients on stretchers or standing, with a minimum clear area of 100 SF.
2. Provide a dedicated exhaust system for the decontamination room that is entirely separate from the main ED HVAC; minimum 12 ACH exhaust, negative pressure relative to adjacent spaces, with exhaust discharge at roof level away from air intakes.
3. Specify a floor drain connected to an isolated containment sump or holding tank; show containment system on plumbing drawings; coordinate with {county} County sewer authority regarding HAZMAT discharge permitting.
4. Show a direct exterior entry/access point (separate from main ED entrance) on the site plan and floor plan to allow HAZMAT-contaminated patients to enter the decontamination area without transiting through clean ED spaces.
5. Include decontamination room in the NYSDOH OHSM Emergency Preparedness narrative submitted with the project application, referencing applicable NYSDOH guidelines and the facility's HAZMAT response plan.
code_references: NYSDOH Emergency Preparedness Requirements for Hospitals

description: NYSDOH requires a private toilet room with grab bars and accessible fixtures for each single-bed patient room in new hospital construction
violation_template: NYSDOH PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — PATIENT ROOM DESIGN / PLUMBING: The submitted floor plans for the {occupancy} inpatient nursing unit indicate that one or more single-bed patient rooms in {county} County do not include a private, dedicated toilet room directly accessible from the patient room, as required by 10 NYCRR §711.2(b)(1). New York State regulations prohibit shared toilet facilities for new construction of single-bed inpatient rooms and require that each room have its own private toilet room equipped with a water closet, lavatory, grab bars on both sides of the toilet and behind, and fixtures that comply with NYS accessibility standards. This requirement applies to all new construction and major renovation projects at NYS-licensed hospitals and is more stringent than FGI 2022 in that shared corridor toilet rooms are not an acceptable substitute. Shared toilet room arrangements found in the current submission must be redesigned to provide one private toilet room per single-bed patient room.
fix_template:
1. Redesign the inpatient floor plan to provide a private, dedicated toilet room directly accessible from each single-bed patient room; the toilet room must contain a water closet, lavatory with knee clearance, and sufficient turning radius (60-inch minimum) for wheelchair access.
2. Add grab bars on both sides of the water closet and on the rear wall, per NYS Accessibility Standard dimensions; show grab bar locations, heights, and blocking reinforcement on architectural drawings.
3. Specify all fixtures in the patient toilet room as ADA/NYS-accessible compliant; provide fixture schedule referencing applicable standards.
4. Confirm on drawings that the toilet room door swings outward (or is a sliding/pocket door) to allow emergency egress if a patient collapses against the door.
5. Update the room data sheets and fixture schedule to reflect one toilet room per single-bed patient room throughout the nursing unit, and revise the plumbing fixture count accordingly in the NYSDOH project application.
code_references: NYS Accessibility Standard (equivalent to ADA Standards)

description: NYSDOH strictly limits inpatient rooms to a maximum of 2 beds; no 3-bed or 4-bed rooms permitted in new construction or major renovation
violation_template: NYSDOH PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — PATIENT ROOM DESIGN: The submitted floor plans for the {occupancy} inpatient unit in {county} County depict one or more patient rooms containing three (3) or more patient beds, which is not permitted under 10 NYCRR §711.2(b)(2). New York State regulations strictly limit inpatient patient rooms to a maximum of two (2) beds in all new construction and major renovation projects at NYS-licensed hospitals. Rooms with three or more beds were phased out under prior NYSDOH regulatory guidance and are categorically prohibited in new licensure submissions. Each two-bed room must also comply with minimum square footage, privacy curtain, and patient toilet room requirements applicable to multi-bed rooms under NYSDOH rules. The non-compliant multi-bed rooms identified in the submitted drawings must be redesigned as single- or double-occupancy rooms prior to NYSDOH approval.
fix_template:
1. Redesign all patient rooms exceeding two (2) beds to single-bed or double-bed (two-bed) configurations; revise the affected floor plans, room numbering, and bed count calculations accordingly.
2. Verify that each redesigned two-bed room meets the NYSDOH minimum square footage requirement for multi-bed rooms and includes privacy curtain tracks that fully screen each bed from the other and from the corridor.
3. Update the project program and bed count narrative in the NYSDOH OHSM project application to reflect the revised room configuration; confirm that the total licensed bed count is unchanged or submit a revised Certificate of Need (CON) if the count changes.
4. Ensure each two-bed room provides individual patient bed privacy curtain tracks as required by 10 NYCRR §711.2(b)(3) and that the room layout allows nursing staff to access each bed without disturbing the other patient.
5. Submit revised floor plans with room areas tabulated (net SF per room) and annotated with bed count to facilitate NYSDOH reviewer confirmation of compliance.
code_references: NYSDOH OHSM Design Guidelines for Hospitals

description: Each patient bed in NY licensed hospitals must have a full-length privacy curtain tracking system that fully screens the patient from the corridor when the room door is open
violation_template: NYSDOH PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — PATIENT PRIVACY: The submitted architectural drawings for the {occupancy} inpatient unit in {county} County do not clearly indicate full-length privacy curtain tracking systems at each patient bed position as required by 10 NYCRR §711.2(b)(3). New York State regulations require that every patient bed in a licensed hospital be provided with a ceiling-mounted, full-length privacy curtain track that, when closed, completely screens the patient from view of the corridor when the room door is open, as well as from any other bed in a multi-bed room. The curtain track layout must be shown on the reflected ceiling plan (RCP), with sufficient detail to confirm full perimeter coverage of each bed. Partial curtains, half-height screens, or fixed partitions alone are not a substitute for the required full-length curtain track system. The omission or under-specification of privacy curtain tracks at any patient bed position is a recurring NYSDOH deficiency and must be corrected prior to approval.
fix_template:
1. Add full-length privacy curtain tracks to the reflected ceiling plan (RCP) at every patient bed position; dimension the track layout to confirm it provides complete screening of the patient from the room corridor opening and from adjacent beds in multi-bed rooms.
2. Specify curtain track type, mounting method (ceiling-mounted recessed or surface), and curtain fabric (antimicrobial, flame-resistant per NFPA 101) in the finish schedule and specifications.
3. For single-bed rooms with direct corridor visibility when the door is open, confirm on the RCP that the curtain track extends to the doorway opening width and can be drawn to fully block the line of sight into the room.
4. In multi-bed rooms, show individual curtain tracks for each bed that, when closed, create a fully enclosed private space around each patient area without gaps.
5. Cross-reference the curtain track layout on the architectural floor plan and RCP to the room data sheets, and confirm the privacy curtain track system is included in the interior specifications section of the project manual.
code_references: NYSDOH OHSM Plan Review Checklist — Patient Room Privacy

description: NYSDOH requires nurse station to be located within 30 linear feet of the most distant patient room served; satellite stations or remote monitoring required when exceeded
violation_template: NYSDOH PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — NURSING UNIT DESIGN: The submitted floor plan for the {occupancy} nursing unit in {county} County indicates that the nurse station is located more than 30 linear feet from one or more patient rooms within the unit it serves, in potential conflict with 10 NYCRR §711.2(b)(4). New York State requires that the nurse station serving a patient care unit be positioned so that no patient room within the unit is more than 30 linear feet (measured along the corridor centerline) from the nurse station. Where the nursing unit layout results in patient rooms exceeding the 30 LF threshold, the design must incorporate satellite nurse stations or an NYSDOH-accepted electronic remote patient monitoring system to compensate for the reduced proximity. The current floor plan submission does not include satellite stations or remote monitoring documentation for the rooms exceeding the proximity limit. This deficiency must be resolved through design revision or written justification and documentation of the remote monitoring technology proposed.
fix_template:
1. Scale and dimension the submitted floor plan to measure the corridor-centerline distance from the nurse station to every patient room door in the unit; tabulate these distances and identify all rooms exceeding the 30 LF NYSDOH limit.
2. For rooms exceeding 30 LF, add satellite nurse station(s) at intermediate locations so that no patient room is more than 30 LF from a staffed station, OR provide a written description and product documentation for an electronic remote patient monitoring system (continuous bedside monitoring with central console at nurse station) acceptable to NYSDOH.
3. If a remote monitoring approach is used, include the system layout, monitor locations, and central console location on the floor plan, and submit a narrative describing how the system provides equivalent nursing oversight to a proximate station.
4. Revise the nursing unit design narrative in the project program and NYSDOH application to document compliance with the 30 LF proximity requirement for every patient room.
5. Coordinate nurse station location changes with electrical (nurse call system), data/communications, and casework drawings to reflect the revised or added nurse station position(s).
code_references: NYSDOH OHSM Design Guidelines — Nursing Units

description: NYSDOH requires separate clean utility room and soiled utility room within 60 linear feet of each patient room; combined clean/soiled rooms are not acceptable
violation_template: NYSDOH PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — NURSING UNIT DESIGN / INFECTION CONTROL: The submitted nursing unit floor plan for the {occupancy} facility in {county} County either combines clean and soiled utility functions within a single room, or locates one or both utility rooms more than 60 linear feet from the most distant patient room served by that utility area, in violation of 10 NYCRR §711.2(b)(6). New York State requires that each nursing unit provide a dedicated CLEAN utility room and a physically separate SOILED utility room, with each room located within 60 linear feet (measured along the corridor centerline) of every patient room in the unit. Combining clean and soiled functions — even with physical partitions — within a single room is not acceptable under NYSDOH regulations, as this arrangement creates infection control risks incompatible with licensed hospital operations. The failure to provide properly separated and appropriately located utility rooms is a plan review deficiency requiring redesign.
fix_template:
1. Revise the nursing unit floor plan to provide two physically distinct and separately enclosed rooms: one clearly designated as CLEAN UTILITY and one as SOILED UTILITY; label each room with its designated function on the drawings.
2. Measure and document the corridor-centerline distance from each utility room to the most distant patient room it serves; confirm both rooms are within 60 LF; if not, add a second set of utility rooms at the remote end of the unit.
3. Confirm the clean utility room includes: locked medication-adjacent or separate med room access if applicable, counter space, sink, storage for clean supplies and linen, and positive-pressure ventilation relative to the corridor.
4. Confirm the soiled utility room includes: a clinical sink (hopper or service sink), counter space for soiled item handling, waste receptacles, negative-pressure ventilation relative to the corridor, and direct access to the soiled linen/waste cart staging area.
5. Update the room data sheets, door schedule, and plumbing fixture schedule to reflect the separate clean and soiled utility rooms and reference 10 NYCRR §711.2(b)(6) in the code compliance matrix.
code_references: NYSDOH OHSM Design Guidelines — Nursing Unit Support Spaces

description: NY medication room must be lockable with electronic or keyed access control, have a locked refrigerator, adequate prep counter with lighting, and be directly accessible from the nurse station
violation_template: NYSDOH PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — MEDICATION SAFETY: The submitted floor plan and room data sheet for the {occupancy} nursing unit medication room in {county} County do not demonstrate full compliance with 10 NYCRR §711.2(b)(5), which establishes specific requirements for hospital medication room design in New York State. The medication room must be fully enclosed, lockable via keyed hardware or electronic access control (keypad, badge reader), have an internally locked refrigerator unit for temperature-sensitive medications, provide a dedicated medication preparation counter with task lighting of no less than 50 foot-candles at counter level, and be directly accessible from the nurse station without requiring travel through a public corridor. The current submission either lacks access control documentation, does not clearly locate the medication room relative to the nurse station, or omits required equipment designations. All medication room deficiencies must be addressed prior to NYSDOH approval.
fix_template:
1. Confirm on the floor plan and door schedule that the medication room door is equipped with a lockable access control device (keyed hardware or electronic badge/keypad system); specify the product and manufacturer in the hardware schedule.
2. Add a locked medication refrigerator to the room data sheet and equipment plan; specify the refrigerator type (medical-grade, alarmed for temperature excursion) and verify it is shown in the room on the floor plan.
3. Dimension the medication preparation counter to confirm adequate work surface; add a lighting note specifying minimum 50 foot-candles of task illumination at counter level; reflect this on the electrical/lighting plan.
4. Demonstrate on the floor plan that the medication room door opens directly into or is immediately adjacent to the nurse station without requiring traversal of a patient or public corridor; if not currently located as such, relocate the medication room or provide a written justification and NYSDOH-accepted alternative arrangement.
5. Include the medication room in the room-by-room code compliance matrix in the NYSDOH project application, citing 10 NYCRR §711.2(b)(5) for each required feature (access control, refrigeration, lighting, prep counter, nurse station access).
code_references: NYS Education Law (Pharmacy Practice — access control)
NYSDOH OHSM Medication Room Design Guidelines

description: NYSDOH Part 711 specifies OR minimum clear areas: 360 SF for general ORs, 600 SF minimum for cardiac/orthopedic ORs, with specific NY layout configuration requirements
violation_template: NYSDOH PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — SURGICAL SUITE DESIGN: The submitted surgical suite floor plan for the {occupancy} in {county} County indicates one or more operating rooms that do not meet the minimum clear floor area requirements of 10 NYCRR §711.2(a)(6). New York State requires a minimum of 360 SF of clear floor area (measured between fixed cabinets and walls) for general operating rooms, and a minimum of 600 SF clear for cardiac surgery, orthopedic, or other specialty procedure rooms where additional equipment and personnel are required. These requirements coexist with specific NYSDOH layout configuration standards that mandate particular clearances around the operating table, equipment storage zones along the walls, and defined zones for sterile field, anesthesia, and scrub positions. General ORs that are close to but below the 360 SF minimum, and specialty ORs below 600 SF, represent a non-correctable design deficiency that will result in disapproval. Note that while the NYSDOH general OR minimum (360 SF) is less than FGI 2022 (400 SF), the NYSDOH-specific layout configuration requirements must be satisfied concurrently.
fix_template:
1. Dimension all operating rooms on the floor plan and calculate the net clear area (between fixed casework faces and finished walls); tabulate results on the drawing and confirm general ORs are at minimum 360 SF clear and cardiac/orthopedic/specialty ORs are at minimum 600 SF clear.
2. For any OR below the applicable minimum, revise the room dimensions to meet or exceed the NYSDOH minimum; coordinate with structural, mechanical, and electrical to accommodate revised room boundaries.
3. Show on each OR floor plan the designated zones for: sterile field (around operating table), anesthesia zone (head of table, minimum 4 feet clearance), scrub sink alcove, and wall-mounted/built-in equipment storage; confirm that these zones do not overlap and that the layout meets NYSDOH configuration requirements per the OHSM design guidelines.
4. Indicate on the drawing the table-to-wall clearance on all four sides of the operating table position (minimum 3 feet each side and foot end; minimum 4 feet at head/anesthesia end).
5. Submit a surgical suite summary table with the NYSDOH project application listing each OR by room number, designation (general, cardiac, ortho, etc.), gross room dimensions, and calculated net clear SF.
code_references: NYSDOH OHSM Surgical Suite Design Guidelines

description: NYSDOH requires a handwashing sink or alcohol-based hand rub (ABHR) station at each individual ICU patient space, not shared between bays
violation_template: NYSDOH PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — CRITICAL CARE / INFECTION CONTROL: The submitted ICU floor plan for the {occupancy} in {county} County does not provide individual handwashing sinks or alcohol-based hand rub (ABHR) stations at each patient space as required by 10 NYCRR §711.2(c)(1). New York State mandates that every individual ICU patient bed position — whether in an open-bay, semi-enclosed, or private room configuration — have a dedicated handwashing sink or ABHR dispenser that serves only that patient space and is not shared with any adjacent patient bay. This requirement is consistent with CDC hand hygiene guidelines and NYSDOH infection control standards for critical care environments. The current submission shows shared sinks between patient bays or sinks located at the nursing station only, which does not satisfy the individual-patient-space requirement. Providing one sink or ABHR per patient space is essential to prevent healthcare-associated infections in the ICU and is non-negotiable under NYSDOH regulations.
fix_template:
1. Revise the ICU floor plan to provide a dedicated handwashing sink or ABHR wall-mounted dispenser station within or immediately at the entry to EACH individual patient bed space (open bay or enclosed room); no sharing between adjacent patient bays is permitted.
2. For open-bay ICU configurations, show sink or ABHR locations on the floor plan with a clear indication of which patient bay each fixture serves; position sinks to be reachable by staff entering or exiting the patient space without crossing to an adjacent bay.
3. Update the plumbing fixture schedule to add a lavatory or clinical sink for each ICU patient space not currently shown; calculate the revised fixture count and confirm compliance with NYSDOH minimum fixture ratios.
4. If ABHR dispensers are used in lieu of sinks at individual patient spaces, confirm on the drawings that at least one handwashing sink with soap and water is available within the ICU pod (not more than one patient bay away) for situations where soap and water hand hygiene is required (e.g., C. diff precautions).
5. Add a hand hygiene compliance note to the plumbing drawings referencing 10 NYCRR §711.2(c)(1) and CDC Hand Hygiene Guidelines, and include in the infection control risk assessment (ICRA) submitted with the NYSDOH application.
code_references: CDC Hand Hygiene in Healthcare Settings Guidelines
NYSDOH OHSM Critical Care Design Guidelines

description: New York licensed newborn nurseries (Level I) must provide minimum 40 SF per bassinet; NICU Level III minimum 120 SF per station per FGI 2022 as adopted by NYSDOH
violation_template: NYSDOH PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — NEONATAL CARE DESIGN: The submitted floor plan for the {occupancy} newborn nursery or neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) in {county} County does not meet the minimum space-per-bassinet or space-per-station requirements under 10 NYCRR §711.2(d) and the FGI 2022 guidelines adopted by NYSDOH for neonatal facility design. New York State requires Level I newborn nurseries to provide a minimum of 40 net SF per bassinet position, and Level III NICUs to provide a minimum of 120 net SF per patient station (measured as clear floor area around the incubator or warmer, accessible to staff and equipment on all necessary sides). The current submission appears to show a net area per bassinet/station below these minimums based on the room dimensions and bed/bassinet count indicated. Insufficient space per neonatal patient position creates safety risks associated with equipment access, infection control, and staff workflow, and is a plan review deficiency that must be corrected.
fix_template:
1. Calculate and tabulate on the drawings the net SF per bassinet (Level I nursery) or per patient station (Level II/III NICU), measured as the clear area within the station zone; confirm Level I minimum 40 SF/bassinet and Level III minimum 120 SF/station are met.
2. If the current room area is insufficient, increase the room dimensions or reduce the number of bassinets/stations to achieve compliance; revise the bed/bassinet count and room program accordingly in the NYSDOH project application.
3. Show individual patient station boundaries on the NICU floor plan, dimensioning the clear space around each incubator/warmer on all four sides; indicate the location of the parent/family chair, nursing charting position, and emergency equipment storage within the station footprint.
4. Confirm on the drawings that the NICU provides a handwashing sink within each pod per NYSDOH infection control requirements (ref. NY-ICU-001), family consultation room, breast milk expression room, and staff support spaces as required by FGI 2022 and NYSDOH guidelines.
5. Include the NICU/nursery space compliance table in the NYSDOH OHSM project application, referencing 10 NYCRR §711.2(d) and the applicable FGI 2022 section for the care level, with supporting calculations signed by the architect of record.

description: All projects exceeding $500,000 in construction costs at NYS-licensed hospitals must receive NYSDOH OHSM review and approval before construction commences
violation_template: NYSDOH PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — REGULATORY PROCESS: The project submission for the {occupancy} facility in {county} County indicates a construction cost estimate that meets or exceeds the $500,000 threshold requiring formal NYSDOH Office of Health Systems Management (OHSM) review and written approval prior to commencement of construction under NY Public Health Law §2802 and 10 NYCRR Part 711. The submitted materials do not include a complete NYSDOH Project Application, a programmatic justification narrative demonstrating that the proposed project supports the facility's approved program of services, or a code compliance analysis referencing 10 NYCRR Part 711 and the FGI 2022 guidelines. Commencing construction without written NYSDOH approval constitutes a violation of the NYS Public Health Law and may result in stop-work orders, civil penalties, and potential jeopardy to the facility's operating certificate. The applicant must submit a complete NYSDOH project application package and await written approval before breaking ground.
fix_template:
1. Complete and submit the NYSDOH OHSM Facility Construction Project Application (available at health.ny.gov/facilities/construction), including project description, construction cost estimate, programmatic justification, and architect/engineer information.
2. Prepare and include a code compliance analysis matrix referencing 10 NYCRR Part 711 and identifying each applicable section and how the project design meets each requirement; have this analysis prepared or reviewed by a NYS-licensed architect.
3. Include the following required attachments in the NYSDOH application package: construction drawings and specifications (at design development level minimum), a phasing plan if the project involves occupied areas, and an Infection Control Risk Assessment (ICRA) for projects in or adjacent to patient care areas.
4. Submit a programmatic justification narrative demonstrating how the proposed project supports or maintains the facility's approved program of services and licensed bed/treatment station capacity, per NYSDOH OHSM requirements.
5. Allow a minimum 60-90 day NYSDOH review period from the date of a complete application submission; do not release construction documents for bid or issue a notice to proceed until written NYSDOH OHSM approval has been received and is on file at the facility.
code_references: NYSDOH OHSM Construction Project Application Requirements

description: NYSDOH requires X-ray viewing capability (digital PACS workstation or view box) within or immediately adjacent to each ED treatment bay
violation_template: NYSDOH PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT DESIGN: The submitted emergency department floor plan and equipment layout for the {occupancy} facility in {county} County do not provide X-ray viewing capability within or immediately adjacent to each treatment bay as required by 10 NYCRR §711.2(a)(8). New York State regulations require that every ED treatment bay have access to X-ray viewing capability — either a digital PACS workstation integrated into the treatment bay design or a traditional X-ray view box — located within the bay or in an alcove or workstation immediately adjacent and directly accessible from the bay without traveling through another patient space. Clinicians must be able to review radiographic images without leaving the immediate treatment area or compromising another patient's privacy. The current submission does not indicate PACS workstation locations, data outlet positions for diagnostic workstations, or view box mounting locations at treatment bays, constituting a plan review deficiency under NYSDOH standards.
fix_template:
1. Add to the ED treatment bay floor plan and equipment layout the location of a digital PACS workstation or X-ray view box at each treatment bay; indicate whether the viewing capability is a fixed in-bay workstation, wall-mounted monitor, or shared bay-cluster workstation in an immediately adjacent alcove.
2. Coordinate with the low-voltage/data design to provide data and power outlets at each PACS workstation location; show on the electrical and data plans with appropriate circuit designations.
3. If a centralized PACS viewing workstation is proposed to serve multiple bays (cluster model), demonstrate on the floor plan that the workstation is positioned so that the treating clinician can access it from any bay in the cluster without traveling through another patient bay or a public corridor.
4. Include PACS workstation equipment in the ED equipment list submitted with the NYSDOH application; specify monitor size, data connection type (fiber, Cat6A), and identify the responsible service provider/IT system.
5. Reference 10 NYCRR §711.2(a)(8) in the code compliance matrix and include the X-ray viewing capability compliance note on the ED floor plan keynote legend.
code_references: NYSDOH OHSM Emergency Department Design Guidelines
ACR-AAPM Technical Standard for Electronic Practice of Medical Imaging

description: NYSDOH requires chemical and cleaning supply storage to be in a separate, labeled, locked room entirely separate from medication storage areas; combined storage is prohibited
violation_template: NYSDOH PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — ENVIRONMENTAL SERVICES / MEDICATION SAFETY: The submitted floor plans for the {occupancy} facility in {county} County do not clearly demonstrate that chemical and cleaning supply storage is located in a separate, dedicated, and locked room entirely independent from medication storage areas, as required by 10 NYCRR §711.2(f). New York State regulations prohibit any co-location of chemical cleaning supplies and medications — even within a subdivided or partitioned common room — because of the risk of accidental medication contamination, dispensing errors, and Joint Commission/NYSDOH survey deficiencies. The chemical storage room must be separately labeled ('Chemical Storage' or 'Housekeeping'), independently lockable, and physically enclosed by floor-to-deck partitions on all sides; proximity to or adjacency with the medication room or medication cart alcove is not acceptable. The current submission either co-locates these functions or does not clearly identify the chemical storage room as a separate, enclosed, lockable space.
fix_template:
1. Revise the floor plan to designate a separate, enclosed, independently lockable room specifically for chemical and cleaning supply storage; label the room 'Chemical Storage' or 'Housekeeping Supply Room' on the drawings and confirm it is enclosed by floor-to-deck partitions.
2. Verify and document on the floor plan that the chemical storage room has no direct door opening, pass-through, or shared access with the medication room, medication cart alcove, clean utility room, or any space where medications are stored or prepared.
3. Add a door schedule entry for the chemical storage room specifying a lockable door hardware set (keyed or electronic); confirm the lock is specified in the hardware schedule and that key control is separate from the medication room key system.
4. Include ventilation for the chemical storage room per OSHA and NYSDOH requirements: minimum 10 ACH exhaust, negative pressure relative to adjacent occupied spaces, with exhaust discharge that prevents re-entry of chemical vapors into the building.
5. In the project's code compliance matrix and NYSDOH application narrative, explicitly address the physical separation of chemical and medication storage and reference 10 NYCRR §711.2(f); confirm the facility's policies prohibiting co-storage will be documented in the operational plan.
code_references: NYSDOH OHSM Environmental Services Design Guidelines

discipline: Fire and Life Safety / Regulatory Coordination
description: NYC facilities must comply with both 10 NYCRR Part 711 and NYC Fire Code; FDNY approval required in addition to NYSDOH review, and FDNY filing receipt must be included in NYSDOH submittal
violation_template: NYSDOH PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — FIRE AND LIFE SAFETY / REGULATORY COORDINATION: The submitted construction documents for the {occupancy} facility do not include evidence of concurrent FDNY (Fire Department of New York) filing and approval, which is required for healthcare facilities located within the five boroughs of New York City under 10 NYCRR §711.2 and NYC Administrative Code Title 15. New York City healthcare facilities must satisfy BOTH the NYSDOH 10 NYCRR Part 711 requirements AND the NYC Fire Code (Administrative Code Chapter 15) for fire suppression systems, fire alarm systems, and means of egress — these are independent regulatory frameworks with separate filing, inspection, and approval processes. NYSDOH OHSM requires that the project application package for NYC facilities include a copy of the FDNY job filing receipt or plan approval letter confirming that fire protection systems have been filed with and are under review by FDNY. Absent this documentation, NYSDOH cannot confirm coordinated regulatory compliance for the fire and life safety systems and may withhold approval pending its receipt.
fix_template:
1. File the project's fire protection drawings (sprinkler system, fire alarm system, standpipe system) with the FDNY through the NYC Department of Buildings (DOB) online filing system (NYC DOB NOW) and obtain a job filing number and receipt; attach a copy of the FDNY filing receipt to the NYSDOH OHSM project application.
2. Engage a NYS-licensed fire protection engineer to prepare fire suppression and alarm drawings that simultaneously comply with 10 NYCRR Part 711, the NYC Building Code (2022 edition), and the NYC Fire Code (Administrative Code Title 15); document dual-compliance in the code analysis.
3. Coordinate the egress design with both NYSDOH and NYC DOB/FDNY requirements; where the two regulatory frameworks impose different egress widths, exit counts, travel distances, or rated corridor requirements, apply the more stringent standard and document the reconciliation in the code analysis.
4. Identify on the drawings any areas where NYC Fire Code requirements for healthcare occupancies exceed NFPA 101 Life Safety Code requirements (which NYSDOH references), and confirm that the design meets the higher NYC standard in those areas.
5. Include in the NYSDOH project application a regulatory coordination cover letter describing the dual-approval process (NYSDOH + FDNY/DOB), listing all concurrent filing numbers, and identifying the design team members responsible for each regulatory submission; update this letter and resubmit if FDNY requires revisions that affect the NYSDOH-reviewed documents.
code_references: NYC Building Code 2022 — Chapter 4 (Special Detailed Requirements for Occupancies)
NFPA 101 Life Safety Code 2021 (as referenced by NYSDOH)

description: Hurricane-resistant construction required for Florida hospitals as Risk Category IV buildings
violation_template: AHCA PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — STRUCTURAL / WIND (FL-WIN-001): The submitted construction documents for the {occupancy} project in {county} County do not demonstrate compliance with Florida Building Code (FBC) 7th Edition hurricane wind load requirements for Risk Category IV buildings. Hospitals are classified as Risk Category IV per ASCE 7-22 Table 1.5-1 and must be designed for the 700-year mean recurrence interval wind speed shown in ASCE 7-22 Figure 26.5-2D with applicable Florida amendments. The exterior building envelope — including glazing, exterior doors, wall assemblies, and roofing — must meet FBC §1609 requirements, and HVHZ provisions apply in Miami-Dade and Broward Counties. Wind speed contours and the design basis wind speed must be clearly noted on the structural drawings. This deficiency must be resolved prior to issuance of an AHCA permit.
fix_template:
1. Determine the design wind speed for the project site from ASCE 7-22 Figure 26.5-2D and confirm Risk Category IV classification; note the governing basic wind speed on the cover sheet and structural general notes.
2. Provide a wind load analysis conforming to ASCE 7-22 Chapter 26–31 with Florida-specific amendments; include all exposure category, topographic factor, and directionality calculations.
3. Confirm whether the project site falls within a High-Velocity Hurricane Zone (HVHZ) as defined by FBC §202; if so, all exterior envelope components must carry Miami-Dade County Notice of Acceptance (NOA) or Florida Product Approval.
4. Revise structural drawings to show hurricane-resistant detailing for all roof-to-wall, wall-to-foundation, and floor diaphragm connections per FBC §2308 or engineered design.
5. Include a completed FBC Chapter 16 wind design summary table on the structural drawings for AHCA reviewer verification.
6. Resubmit revised structural drawings and calculations for AHCA Plans and Construction Unit review.

description: Impact-resistant glazing required for exterior windows and doors in wind-borne debris regions
violation_template: AHCA PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — STRUCTURAL / GLAZING (FL-WIN-002): The construction documents for the {occupancy} in {county} County do not adequately specify impact-resistant glazing or approved impact-resistant coverings for all exterior windows and doors. The project site falls within a wind-borne debris region where the basic wind speed equals or exceeds 130 mph per FBC §1609.1.2, requiring all exterior glazed openings to be protected by impact-resistant assemblies with a valid Florida Product Approval or Miami-Dade Notice of Acceptance (NOA). The current drawings reference standard commercial glazing that does not carry an approved impact rating. Product approval numbers, NOA references, and the name of the approved testing laboratory must be included in the specifications and on the window and door schedules.
fix_template:
1. Verify the project site's basic wind speed from ASCE 7-22 Figure 26.5-2D; confirm whether the site is within a wind-borne debris region per FBC §1609.1.2 (130 mph or greater, or 110 mph within 1 mile of the coastline in certain counties).
2. Update the window and door schedule to specify impact-resistant glazing assemblies or approved storm protection coverings for every exterior opening.
3. Obtain and reference a current Florida Product Approval (floridabuilding.org) or Miami-Dade NOA for each product; include the approval/NOA number and expiration date in the specifications.
4. Ensure products comply with FBC §1609.1.2 large- and small-missile impact test requirements as applicable to the specific zone and opening size.
5. Coordinate with the structural engineer to confirm that framing, anchors, and rough opening details match the product approval installation requirements.
6. Revise architectural drawings and specifications and resubmit to AHCA for review.

description: Critical hospital systems must be elevated above Base Flood Elevation in FEMA Special Flood Hazard Areas
violation_template: AHCA PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — FLOOD / ESSENTIAL ELECTRICAL (FL-FL-001): The construction documents for the {occupancy} in {county} County depict essential electrical equipment — including the emergency generator, main switchgear, automatic transfer switches, and/or critical medical imaging systems — at or below the Base Flood Elevation (BFE) for the FEMA-mapped Special Flood Hazard Area (SFHA) in which the project is located. Florida AHCA, in conjunction with FBC Chapter 12 and ASCE 24, requires that all essential systems be elevated to a minimum of 1 foot (freeboard) above the BFE. Failure to meet this requirement renders the facility non-compliant and may result in loss of licensure following a flood event. The FEMA Flood Insurance Rate Map (FIRM) panel number, BFE, and proposed finished floor elevations for all critical system rooms must be documented on the drawings.
fix_template:
1. Identify the applicable FEMA FIRM panel and current BFE for the project site; note the FIRM panel number, effective date, and BFE on the civil/site drawings and the electrical floor plans.
2. Confirm that the design flood elevation (DFE = BFE + 1 ft minimum freeboard) per ASCE 24 is used as the controlling elevation for all essential system room finished floors.
3. Relocate or re-elevate the emergency generator, fuel tanks, main switchgear, ATS panels, UPS systems, and other critical electrical equipment so that the lowest component is at or above the DFE.
4. Evaluate relocation of MRI and other high-value critical equipment to upper floors if ground-level compliance is infeasible.
5. Provide a flood-proofing narrative or architectural/structural flood-proofing measures (dry flood-proofing to ASCE 24 standards) if equipment relocation above DFE is not achievable.
6. Coordinate with the electrical engineer to update equipment layout drawings, equipment schedules, and specifications to reflect the revised elevations.
7. Resubmit revised documents including a completed FEMA Elevation Certificate (or preliminary elevation data) to AHCA.

description: Florida hospitals must maintain a minimum 96-hour on-site fuel supply for emergency generators
violation_template: AHCA PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — EMERGENCY POWER (FL-EP-001): The construction documents for the {occupancy} in {county} County indicate an on-site diesel fuel storage capacity for the emergency generator system that does not meet the minimum 96-hour fuel supply requirement mandated by FAC §59A-3.083(17) at full-load generator operation. AHCA requires Florida-licensed hospitals to maintain sufficient on-site fuel to sustain all Level 1 essential electrical system loads continuously for 96 hours without resupply, consistent with the facility's hurricane preparedness obligations. The submitted specifications indicate a fuel capacity that falls below this threshold. Additionally, the fuel storage tanks and distribution piping must be designed to withstand hurricane-force wind and flood conditions consistent with the requirements noted under FL-WIN-001 and FL-FL-001.
fix_template:
1. Calculate the total full-load fuel consumption rate (gallons per hour) for all emergency generators at 100% design load, accounting for all Level 1 and Level 2 essential electrical loads per NFPA 110.
2. Size on-site fuel storage tanks to provide a minimum of 96 hours of continuous full-load operation; document the calculation clearly in the specifications and on the drawings.
3. Specify above-ground storage tanks (ASTs) or underground storage tanks (USTs) meeting NFPA 30 Chapter 21/22 as applicable; coordinate with the local fire marshal for storage tank permitting.
4. Locate and anchor fuel storage tanks to resist hurricane uplift and flood forces; elevate tank bottoms above the DFE per FL-FL-001 requirements where applicable.
5. Provide a secondary containment system sized for 110% of the largest tank volume per NFPA 30 and applicable FDEP (Florida Department of Environmental Protection) storage tank rules.
6. Include a fuel polishing and day-tank arrangement per NFPA 110 §8.3 to maintain fuel quality over extended storage periods.
7. Update the electrical/mechanical specifications and drawings to reflect the revised tank sizing and protection measures, and resubmit to AHCA.

description: Surgical suite HVAC must maintain required temperature and humidity with 100% redundancy
violation_template: AHCA PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — HVAC / INFECTION CONTROL (FL-HVAC-001): The mechanical design documents for the {occupancy} in {county} County do not demonstrate that the surgical suite HVAC system will maintain the AHCA-required environmental conditions of 68–73°F dry-bulb temperature and 30–60% relative humidity throughout all occupied hours, nor do the documents provide for 100% redundancy of the air handling units (AHUs) serving each surgical suite. FAC §59A-3.083(10) and ASHRAE 170-2021 Table 7.1 both require these environmental parameters. A single point of failure in the AHU serving an operating room creates an unacceptable life-safety and infection-control risk. Furthermore, if energy recovery ventilation (ERV) is incorporated, cross-contamination prevention devices must be specified and their effectiveness documented.
fix_template:
1. Revise the mechanical design to demonstrate — via psychrometric analysis or equipment data — that the proposed AHUs will maintain 68–73°F and 30–60% RH under both peak cooling and minimum load conditions specific to {county} County's climate (ASHRAE Climate Zone 1A or 2A as applicable).
2. Provide a standby (redundant) AHU for each surgical suite served so that either unit alone can maintain full design airflow, temperature, and humidity; document the automatic failover sequence in the sequences of operation.
3. Size humidification and dehumidification equipment to hold the 30–60% RH band year-round; Florida's high latent load requires careful dehumidification coil selection and reheat capacity.
4. If ERV units are incorporated in the surgical suite exhaust/supply system, specify total-energy wheels or heat pipes with documented cross-leakage rates meeting ASHRAE 170 §6.5; plate-type exchangers with 100% outdoor air bypass are acceptable where cross-contamination is a concern.
5. Confirm minimum 20 total air changes per hour (ACH) with at least 4 ACH outdoor air for each OR per ASHRAE 170 Table 7.1; include airflow balance tables on the drawings.
6. Coordinate with the commissioning agent (required per FL-ENV-001) to include functional performance testing of the redundant AHU switchover sequence and environmental setpoint verification.
7. Resubmit revised mechanical drawings, calculations, and sequences of operation to AHCA.

description: Written ICRA required for all construction in or adjacent to occupied patient care areas
violation_template: AHCA PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — INFECTION CONTROL (FL-INF-001): The construction document package submitted for the {occupancy} project in {county} County does not include a completed Infection Control Risk Assessment (ICRA) as required by FAC §59A-3.041. Because the proposed work is located in or immediately adjacent to occupied patient care areas, a written ICRA — signed by the hospital infection control officer and project manager — must be included with the construction document submission. The ICRA must classify the project at no less than ICRA Class III for any occupied acute care facility and must address dust control, negative air pressure containment, HEPA filtration, and interim life-safety measures for the duration of construction.
fix_template:
1. Prepare a written ICRA using the FGI Guidelines for Design and Construction of Hospitals (2022 edition) ICRA matrix or equivalent; classify the project by construction type (A–D) and patient risk group to determine the required ICRA class.
2. For projects in or adjacent to occupied patient care areas, implement Class III or IV ICRA measures as determined by the matrix; document the required measures on an ICRA permit or barrier plan included with the construction documents.
3. Obtain signatures on the ICRA from the hospital Infection Control Practitioner (ICP), the facility manager, and the construction project manager before submitting to AHCA.
4. Include a dust-control barrier plan — showing location, material (minimum 6-mil poly sheeting on a framed partition or gypsum board barrier), and negative pressure HEPA unit placement — as a separate drawing sheet within the construction document set.
5. Specify HEPA-filtered negative air machines (minimum 12 ACH within the construction zone) with continuous pressure monitoring; include the make, model, and CFM capacity in the specifications.
6. Address interim life-safety measures (temporary egress, fire alarm, sprinkler protection) on the drawings if any existing systems will be temporarily impaired.
7. Attach the completed and signed ICRA to the AHCA plan review submittal application and resubmit.
code_references: CDC / APIC Infection Control Risk Assessment Guidelines

description: Complete NFPA 13 sprinkler system required throughout Florida hospitals; dry-pipe prohibited in occupied patient care areas
violation_template: AHCA PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — FIRE / LIFE SAFETY (FL-FLS-001): The construction documents for the {occupancy} in {county} County do not provide for a complete automatic fire sprinkler system throughout the entire facility as required by FAC §59A-3.083(16) and NFPA 101-2018 §18.3.5 as adopted by Florida. All occupied patient care areas must be protected by wet-pipe NFPA 13 sprinkler systems; the use of dry-pipe or pre-action systems within occupied patient care spaces is not permitted under AHCA guidelines. The submitted drawings indicate areas of the facility that are either unsprinklered or served by a dry-pipe system contrary to this requirement. The sprinkler design must be hydraulically calculated and documented by a Florida-licensed fire protection engineer.
fix_template:
1. Confirm that 100% of the facility floor area — including all patient care rooms, corridors, mechanical rooms, attics, and interstitial spaces — is covered by a complete NFPA 13 wet-pipe automatic sprinkler system.
2. Replace any dry-pipe or pre-action sprinkler zones within occupied patient care areas with wet-pipe zones; convert system type designations on the drawings accordingly.
3. If dry-pipe or pre-action systems are retained in non-patient-care areas (e.g., unheated parking structures, loading docks), ensure these areas are clearly delineated on the riser diagram and floor plan and that no occupied patient care spaces are served.
4. Provide hydraulic calculations prepared and sealed by a Florida-licensed fire protection engineer (PE) demonstrating compliance with NFPA 13-2019 Chapter 23 demand-supply analysis.
5. Coordinate sprinkler head selection and coverage with the reflected ceiling plans; confirm compatibility with any HVAC diffusers, lighting fixtures, or ceiling grid per NFPA 13 §10.2.
6. Include the complete sprinkler riser diagram with all control valves, flow switches, and inspector's test connections labeled; coordinate tamper and flow switch monitoring with the fire alarm system drawings.
7. Resubmit revised fire protection drawings and hydraulic calculations bearing the Florida PE seal to AHCA.

description: Florida hospital HVAC, lighting, and envelope must comply with Florida Building Code Energy Conservation; commissioning required
violation_template: AHCA PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — ENERGY / COMMISSIONING (FL-ENV-001): The construction documents for the {occupancy} in {county} County reference California Title 24 energy compliance forms; however, Title 24 does not apply in Florida. Florida hospital energy compliance must be demonstrated using the Florida Building Code, Energy Conservation, 7th Edition (based on ASHRAE 90.1-2019 with Florida-specific amendments). A compliant COMcheck-Web or energy modeling report demonstrating compliance with FBC Energy must be submitted. Additionally, AHCA requires commissioning of all mechanical and electrical systems per FBC Energy §Cx; a commissioning plan prepared by a registered commissioning authority (CxA) must be submitted prior to or with the construction documents.
fix_template:
1. Remove all references to California Title 24 from the construction documents and specifications; confirm that the governing energy code is Florida Building Code, Energy Conservation, 7th Edition.
2. Prepare a COMcheck-Web energy compliance report (or equivalent approved energy model) for the building envelope, mechanical systems, and lighting systems; attach the signed report to the resubmittal package.
3. Verify that the building envelope U-values and SHGC values for glazing meet FBC Energy Table C402.1.3 requirements for Climate Zone 1A or 2A (applicable to {county} County).
4. Confirm that HVAC equipment efficiency ratings meet FBC Energy Section C403 mandatory and prescriptive requirements; document equipment efficiencies on the mechanical schedule.
5. Confirm that interior lighting power densities comply with FBC Energy §C405.3 or an approved whole-building method; include a lighting power density summary on the electrical drawings.
6. Engage a registered Commissioning Authority (CxA) — independent of the design team for projects ≥50,000 SF — and prepare a commissioning plan addressing mechanical, electrical, plumbing, and building envelope systems per FBC Energy §C408.
7. Include the commissioning plan (or a letter of intent from the CxA) with the AHCA resubmittal; the completed commissioning report will be required prior to AHCA final inspection.
code_references: Florida Building Code Energy Conservation 7th Ed.

description: Hospital pharmacies must meet AHCA licensing, Florida Board of Pharmacy, and USP 797/800 sterile compounding standards
violation_template: AHCA PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — PHARMACY / INFECTION CONTROL (FL-PHR-001): The pharmacy construction documents for the {occupancy} in {county} County do not demonstrate compliance with the dual regulatory requirements applicable to Florida hospital pharmacies. AHCA hospital licensing standards (FAC §59A-3.083(14)) govern the spatial and operational requirements of the pharmacy within the hospital; simultaneously, the Florida Board of Pharmacy (Chapter 465 FS and Rule 64B16 FAC) governs pharmacy licensure, including sterile compounding clean room design under USP 797 and hazardous drug handling under USP 800. The current documents lack the ISO classification designation, pressure differential requirements, and HEPA filtration details required for the sterile compounding suite, and do not address hazardous drug storage and deactivation areas per USP 800.
fix_template:
1. Confirm the scope of sterile compounding activities and classify each area by ISO cleanliness level per USP 797 (2023 revision): anteroom (ISO 7 minimum), buffer room (ISO 7 for low-risk, ISO 5 for medium/high-risk), and primary engineering controls (ISO 5 LAF or BSC).
2. Provide HVAC pressure differential diagrams showing positive pressure cascade from buffer room to anteroom for non-HD compounds and negative pressure for hazardous drug buffer rooms per USP 800 Section 7.
3. Specify HEPA-filtered air handling with appropriate total ACH (not less than 30 ACPH for buffer room per USP 797); include airflow direction, supply/return diffuser locations, and pressure monitoring gauges on the mechanical drawings.
4. Designate a separate, negative-pressure hazardous drug (HD) storage area and a deactivation/decontamination sink area per USP 800; include appropriate spill containment features.
5. Coordinate the pharmacy design with the Florida Board of Pharmacy (64B16-28 FAC) sterile compounding permit application requirements; provide a pharmacy layout plan at a scale sufficient for Board review.
6. Engage the hospital's designated pharmacist-in-charge (PIC) to review and approve the pharmacy layout drawings before AHCA resubmittal.
7. Resubmit revised pharmacy drawings including ISO classifications, pressure differential schedule, HVAC details, and USP 797/800 compliance narrative to AHCA; note that a separate Florida Board of Pharmacy plan approval may also be required.

description: New hospitals and major renovations exceeding $1M must be reviewed by AHCA Office of Plans and Construction before construction begins
violation_template: AHCA PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — REGULATORY / PLAN REVIEW (FL-GEN-001): The construction documents submitted for the {occupancy} project in {county} County indicate a project cost (estimated construction value) that meets or exceeds the $1,000,000 threshold requiring mandatory AHCA plan review under FAC §59A-3.1065. Review of the submitted application reveals that the required application form is incomplete: the licensed health care facility number, the licensed health care facility contact, and the designer-of-record licensure information (Florida PE or RA license number) are not fully provided. No construction activity subject to AHCA jurisdiction may commence prior to issuance of an AHCA Construction Permit. Phased submissions are accepted; however, each phase must receive written AHCA authorization before that phase of work begins.
fix_template:
1. Complete the AHCA Plans and Construction Unit application form in full, including: Florida facility license number, facility administrator contact information, estimated construction cost, project description, and all design professional license numbers (Florida PE, RA, or both as applicable).
2. Confirm whether the project scope triggers major renovation thresholds under FAC §59A-3.1065(2); if so, include a written project description and a cost estimate prepared by the contractor or a certified cost estimator.
3. For phased submissions, prepare a phasing plan identifying each phase, its scope, and the planned AHCA submission date; submit the phasing plan to AHCA for concurrence before the first phase documents are submitted.
4. Pay the applicable AHCA plan review fee per FAC §59A-3.1065(7); attach the fee calculation worksheet to the application.
5. Submit complete construction documents — including architectural, structural, mechanical, electrical, plumbing, and fire protection drawings — to the AHCA Plans Review Unit at: Agency for Health Care Administration, Bureau of Health Facility Regulation, Plans and Construction Unit, 2727 Mahan Drive, Tallahassee, FL 32308, or via the AHCA ePortal where accepted.
6. Do not proceed with any foundation, framing, or mechanical/electrical rough-in work until the AHCA Construction Permit is in hand.

description: Hospital dietary areas must comply with AHCA licensing and FDOH food hygiene regulations with separate health department inspection
violation_template: AHCA PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — DIETARY / FOOD SERVICE (FL-DIET-001): The dietary and food service area construction documents for the {occupancy} in {county} County require compliance under two separate regulatory programs. AHCA reviews the dietary area as part of the hospital license under FAC §59A-3.083(13); however, the Florida Department of Health (FDOH) also has jurisdiction over institutional food service operations under Chapter 64E-11 FAC (Food Hygiene). The construction documents do not indicate that the FDOH food service plan review has been initiated, and the submitted kitchen layout does not include the required three-compartment sink sizing calculation, the mechanical exhaust hood specification meeting NFPA 96, or handwashing sink locations at the code-required intervals. A separate FDOH food service plan review and inspection approval is required before the dietary area may operate.
fix_template:
1. Submit a separate food service establishment plan review application to the applicable FDOH county health department concurrent with or following AHCA submission; obtain the FDOH application form from the county health department in {county} County.
2. Revise the dietary drawings to show: (a) three-compartment warewashing sink with minimum compartment sizes per 64E-11.003 FAC, with a grease-interceptor detail if required; (b) dedicated handwashing sinks within 25 feet of all food preparation areas and at each service station; and (c) a hand sink immediately inside the kitchen entrance.
3. Specify a Type I commercial exhaust hood over all cooking equipment producing grease-laden vapors per NFPA 96-2021; include the hood static pressure, CFM, make-up air volume, listed fire suppression system, and clearances on the mechanical drawings.
4. Show floor finish, base, and wall finish materials in the kitchen that are smooth, nonporous, and cleanable; provide cove base at all floor-wall junctions in food preparation areas.
5. Confirm adequate refrigeration and dry storage areas per FAC §59A-3.083(13) to support the patient census; include equipment schedule with capacities.
6. Coordinate the FDOH inspection schedule with the construction timeline to ensure dietary operations are not opened prior to FDOH approval.
7. Include a copy of the FDOH plan review approval (or acknowledgment of submission) with the AHCA closeout documentation.

description: Florida hospital roofing systems must be HVHZ-approved or engineered to resist hurricane uplift per FBC and ASCE 7
violation_template: AHCA PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — STRUCTURAL / ROOFING (FL-WIN-003): The roofing system specified for the {occupancy} in {county} County does not demonstrate compliance with Florida Building Code hurricane wind uplift requirements for Risk Category IV structures. The construction documents neither reference a Florida Product Approval for the proposed roof assembly nor provide engineered uplift calculations demonstrating compliance with FBC §1504 and the component-and-cladding (C&C) wind pressures derived from ASCE 7-22 Chapter 30. For projects within the High-Velocity Hurricane Zone (Miami-Dade and Broward Counties), a Miami-Dade Notice of Acceptance (NOA) for the complete roof system — including membrane, insulation, and fastening pattern — is mandatory. Hospitals must remain operational during and after a design-level hurricane; the roof system is a critical life-safety element.
fix_template:
1. Determine the governing roof-zone design wind pressures (corners, edges, field) using ASCE 7-22 Chapter 30 Method 2 or 3 for the project site and Risk Category IV; tabulate these on the structural or roof drawings.
2. For projects in Miami-Dade or Broward Counties (HVHZ): select a roofing system that carries a current Miami-Dade NOA covering the complete assembly (membrane, insulation, substrate, fasteners); include the NOA number and product manufacturer on the roofing specification.
3. For projects outside the HVHZ: select a roofing system with a current Florida Product Approval from the Florida Building Commission product approval database; verify that the tested uplift capacity (per ASTM E1592 or equivalent) equals or exceeds the calculated design uplift pressures.
4. Specify fastener spacing patterns (field, edge, and corner zones) consistent with the NOA or Florida Product Approval installation requirements; show these on a roof fastening pattern drawing.
5. Address roof-to-wall and parapet attachment details per FBC §1504 and the structural engineer's prescriptive or engineered connection design; confirm continuous load path from roof to foundation.
6. Coordinate roof penetrations (HVAC curbs, skylights, hatches) with individual NOA or product approvals for those penetrations; ensure each is tested or engineered for the applicable uplift pressures.
7. Resubmit revised roofing specifications, fastening pattern drawings, uplift calculations, and NOA/product approval references to AHCA.

description: Florida AHCA requires a family consultation/waiting area adjacent to each ICU at minimum 1 room per 12 beds
violation_template: AHCA PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — ARCHITECTURAL / PATIENT CARE (FL-ICU-001): The floor plan submitted for the {occupancy} intensive care unit (ICU) in {county} County does not include a family consultation/waiting room within or immediately adjacent to the ICU as required by FAC §59A-3.083(6). AHCA requires at least one dedicated family consultation room for each group of 12 ICU beds or fraction thereof. The current layout shows a shared waiting area in the main hospital corridor that is not specifically designated for ICU family use and does not meet the adjacency requirement. The family consultation room must be enclosed, acoustically private, and accessible without passing through the ICU clinical area.
fix_template:
1. Count the total number of licensed ICU beds on each ICU floor or nursing unit; determine the required number of family consultation rooms at the ratio of 1 room per 12 ICU beds (or fraction thereof) per FAC §59A-3.083(6).
2. Designate enclosed, dedicated family consultation room(s) within or immediately adjacent (direct access without traversing the ICU clinical zone) to each ICU; label these rooms clearly on the floor plan.
3. Size each family consultation room to accommodate a minimum of 4–6 persons comfortably (typically 120–150 SF minimum); provide seating, a small table, and appropriate acoustic separation (STC 45 minimum partition assembly) from adjacent corridors and waiting areas.
4. Ensure each family consultation room is accessible to persons with disabilities per FBC Chapter 11 and ADA Standards; provide an accessible route from the public corridor and a compliant accessible door hardware.
5. Provide a family waiting area separate from the consultation room in the immediate ICU zone if the ICU census exceeds 12 beds; label this waiting area on the floor plan and dimension it.
6. Revise the architectural floor plan, room data sheets, and room schedule to reflect the new consultation and waiting rooms, including square footage and door hardware designations.
7. Resubmit revised floor plans to AHCA for review.

description: Florida hospitals require Certificate of Need (CON) approval from AHCA before plan review for new hospitals, bed additions, or major capital expenditures
violation_template: AHCA PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — REGULATORY / CERTIFICATE OF NEED (FL-GEN-002): The plan review application submitted for the {occupancy} project in {county} County proposes a scope of work — establishment of a new hospital, addition of licensed beds, or a capital expenditure exceeding applicable AHCA thresholds — that requires prior Certificate of Need (CON) approval under Chapter 408 Part I, Florida Statutes, and FAC §59C-1. AHCA's Plans and Construction Unit is unable to initiate plan review for CON-reviewable projects without confirmation that the required CON has been granted and is current. Submission of construction documents for plan review prior to CON approval does not constitute a waiver of the CON requirement and will not be processed to completion.
fix_template:
1. Determine whether the proposed project falls within a CON-reviewable service category per Chapter 408.036 FS; categories include new hospital establishment, addition of licensed acute care or specialty beds, establishment of open-heart surgery or organ transplant programs, and capital expenditures exceeding AHCA-published thresholds (updated annually in the Florida Administrative Register).
2. If CON review applies, contact AHCA's Certificate of Need office to confirm the applicable batching cycle and application requirements: Agency for Health Care Administration, Bureau of Health Facility Regulation, Certificate of Need Unit, 2727 Mahan Drive, Tallahassee, FL 32308; phone (850) 412-4369.
3. Submit a CON application during the applicable batching cycle; include a detailed project description, financial feasibility analysis, need methodology, and architectural space program as required by FAC §59C-1.008.
4. Obtain written CON approval (or an exemption determination letter if the project qualifies for CON exemption under §408.036(3) FS) before submitting construction documents to the AHCA Plans and Construction Unit.
5. Attach a copy of the CON approval letter or exemption determination to the AHCA plan review application when submitting construction documents; the Plans Review Unit will not docket the submittal without this documentation.
6. Note that CON approval does not substitute for AHCA plan review (FL-GEN-001) or any required local building permits; all three approvals are typically required in parallel tracks.

description: Seismic peer review required for new hospitals in SDC D or E
violation_template: PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — STRUCTURAL / SEISMIC: The proposed {occupancy} is classified as Risk Category IV (Essential Facility) per IBC 2021 §1604.5 and is located in Seismic Design Category D or E. Washington Administrative Code WAC 246-320-226 requires an independent structural peer review by a licensed structural engineer registered with the Structural Engineers Association of Washington (SEAW) for all new essential facilities in SDC D or E. No evidence of a peer review engagement or peer review scope letter has been included in the construction document submittal. This deficiency must be resolved prior to plan approval.
fix_template:
1. Retain a SEAW-registered licensed structural engineer to perform an independent seismic peer review of the lateral force-resisting system, seismic design criteria, and structural analysis in accordance with ASCE 7-22 Chapter 11.
2. Submit a peer review scope letter and the peer reviewer's credentials (Washington PE license number and SEAW membership) to WADOH as part of a supplemental submittal.
3. Provide peer review comments and the engineer-of-record's written responses as an addendum prior to permit issuance.
4. Ensure the peer reviewer's stamp and signature appear on the final structural review letter submitted to WADOH.

description: Seismic isolation or supplemental energy dissipation evaluation required for tall or large hospitals in SDC D/E
violation_template: PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — STRUCTURAL / SEISMIC ISOLATION: The proposed {occupancy} exceeds 3 stories or 50,000 SF of gross floor area and is located in Seismic Design Category D or E. Per WAC 246-320-226 and ASCE 7-22 Chapter 17, the structural engineer of record must evaluate seismic base isolation and/or supplemental energy dissipation systems for the project. The construction documents do not include a written engineering justification addressing why seismic isolation or supplemental damping was not incorporated into the structural design. Provide the required written analysis and justification prior to plan approval.
fix_template:
1. Prepare a written engineering evaluation, signed and stamped by the licensed structural engineer of record, addressing the feasibility and cost-benefit of seismic base isolation per ASCE 7-22 Chapter 17 for this facility.
2. If seismic isolation is determined not to be feasible or cost-effective, provide a narrative justification citing specific technical, operational, or geometric constraints that preclude its use.
3. If supplemental energy dissipation (fluid viscous dampers, buckling-restrained braces, etc.) was evaluated as an alternative, include that analysis in the justification package.
4. Submit the written justification to WADOH as a supplemental item; peer review of the justification by the SEAW-registered peer reviewer (per WA-SEI-001) is required.
