description: Seismic bracing required for medical gas, fire sprinkler, and HVAC piping (Ip=1.5)
violation_template: PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — SEISMIC BRACING (NONSTRUCTURAL): The construction documents for the proposed {occupancy} do not include a seismic bracing schedule or bracing design for medical gas piping, fire sprinkler piping, and/or HVAC ductwork and piping systems. Per WAC 246-320-226 and ASCE 7-22 Chapter 13, all nonstructural components in Washington hospitals must be designed with an Importance Factor of Ip=1.5. Bracing calculations and a bracing schedule indicating support spacing, brace types, and connection details must appear on the construction documents. This deficiency must be corrected prior to plan approval.
fix_template:
1. Prepare seismic bracing calculations for all medical gas piping, fire sprinkler mains and branches, and HVAC ductwork and piping systems in accordance with ASCE 7-22 §13.3 using Ip=1.5.
2. Include a seismic bracing schedule on the mechanical, plumbing, and fire protection drawings identifying maximum brace spacing, brace types (lateral and longitudinal), and connection details to structure.
3. Specify that all seismic brace assemblies shall be manufactured and labeled per OSHPD-approved or equivalent prequalified brace assemblies with load ratings matching the calculated demand.
4. Add a construction note on drawings referencing NFPA 99 Chapter 5 seismic requirements for medical gas systems and the Washington-adopted edition of ASCE 7.

description: On-site potable water storage required for 72-hour hospital operation
violation_template: PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — EMERGENCY WATER SUPPLY: The construction documents for the proposed {occupancy} do not demonstrate compliance with WAC 246-320-256, which requires Washington licensed hospitals to maintain on-site potable water storage sufficient to support a minimum 72-hour facility operation at reduced capacity following disruption of the municipal water supply. No water storage tanks, cisterns, or alternate backup supply connections are shown or specified on the drawings. Provide calculations demonstrating the 72-hour water demand and show the storage system on the plumbing and civil drawings.
fix_template:
1. Calculate the 72-hour reduced-capacity potable water demand for the facility based on licensed bed count, dietary, sterilization, and minimum domestic uses; document this calculation in the plumbing design narrative.
2. Show on the plumbing drawings a water storage system (above-ground or below-ground tanks, rooftop cisterns, or pre-approved alternate supply connection) sized to meet the 72-hour demand calculation.
3. Specify tank materials, fill/drain connections, overflow, pressure maintenance, and water quality provisions (UV disinfection or equivalent) to prevent stagnation in stored water.
4. Coordinate the storage tank locations and structural loads with the structural engineer of record; provide roof or slab loading calculations where tanks are elevated.

description: Washington State Energy Code compliance and mechanical commissioning required
violation_template: PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — ENERGY CODE / COMMISSIONING: The construction documents for the proposed {occupancy} do not include a Washington State Energy Code (WSEC Commercial 2021) compliance form for HVAC, lighting, and building envelope, or a mechanical commissioning plan. Per WAC 246-320 and WSEC-C 2021, hospital projects must demonstrate compliance with the Washington-adopted energy code, which includes requirements that are more stringent than ASHRAE 90.1 in several areas. Additionally, a mechanical commissioning plan prepared by an independent commissioning authority (CxA) must be submitted, with the final commissioning report provided to WADOH at project closeout. These items must be included in the construction document package.
fix_template:
1. Complete and include WSEC Commercial 2021 compliance forms (COMcheck or equivalent Washington Energy Code compliance documentation) for the HVAC system, lighting, and building envelope as part of the construction document package.
2. Identify areas where WSEC-C 2021 imposes requirements more stringent than ASHRAE 90.1 (e.g., additional economizer requirements, improved envelope U-values in climate zone 4C or 5) and document compliance on the mechanical and architectural drawings.
3. Identify a qualified independent commissioning authority (CxA) and include a commissioning scope plan with the construction documents; the CxA must not be employed by the contractor or equipment suppliers.
4. Submit the final mechanical commissioning report, including functional performance test results for all air-handling systems, to WADOH as a project closeout document prior to facility licensure.

description: Design-phase ICRA required and must accompany construction document submittal
violation_template: PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — INFECTION CONTROL RISK ASSESSMENT (ICRA): The construction document submittal for the proposed project in the {occupancy} does not include a design-phase Infection Control Risk Assessment (ICRA). Per WAC 246-320-131, WADOH requires that a formal ICRA be completed during the design phase for any project involving construction, renovation, or demolition in or adjacent to occupied patient care areas. The ICRA must assess risk to patients in surrounding areas, define containment strategies, and be submitted with the construction documents. ICRA completed only at the construction phase does not satisfy this requirement.
fix_template:
1. Convene an ICRA team comprising infection prevention, facility management, and project design representatives; complete the design-phase ICRA matrix identifying patient risk group (Class I–IV) and construction activity type (Class A–D).
2. Document containment and barrier strategies determined during the ICRA process and show physical barrier locations on the construction drawings (phasing plan or demolition plan sheets).
3. Prepare the ICRA report in a format consistent with the Association for Professionals in Infection Control and Epidemiology (APIC) ICRA guidance and include it as an appendix to the construction document submittal.
4. Identify the infection preventionist responsible for reviewing ICRA compliance during construction and include their contact information in the submittal.

description: Patient room temperature 70-75°F maintained by independent HVAC with separate thermostatic controls
violation_template: PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — PATIENT ROOM TEMPERATURE CONTROL: The HVAC design documents for the proposed {occupancy} do not demonstrate compliance with WAC 246-320-171, which requires patient room temperatures to be maintained between 70°F and 75°F by HVAC systems independent from non-patient areas. Review of the mechanical drawings indicates that patient rooms in the affected zone share HVAC systems with non-patient corridors, support spaces, or administrative areas without independent thermostatic control. Each patient room or patient care zone must have independent thermostatic controls capable of maintaining the required temperature range regardless of adjacent space conditions.
fix_template:
1. Redesign the HVAC distribution in patient room areas to provide terminal units (VAV boxes with reheat, fan-coil units, or equivalent) dedicated to or independently controlled for each patient room or patient care zone.
2. Provide individual thermostatic controls (wall-mounted thermostat or nurse-accessible zone sensor) for each patient room or zone capable of maintaining 70–75°F without interaction with adjacent non-patient spaces.
3. Include a room-by-room HVAC schedule on the mechanical drawings confirming supply/exhaust airflow rates and temperature setpoint ranges for all patient rooms per WAC 246-320-171 and FGI Table 2.1-2.
4. Demonstrate on the mechanical riser or system diagram that the patient room HVAC systems are served from dedicated air-handling units or terminal units not shared with unregulated occupancies.

description: Secure outdoor activity area required for adult psychiatric inpatient units
violation_template: PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — SECURE OUTDOOR ACTIVITY AREA (PSYCHIATRIC): The construction documents for the proposed adult psychiatric inpatient unit do not show a secure outdoor activity area as required by WAC 246-322-230. Each adult inpatient psychiatric unit in a Washington-licensed psychiatric facility must be provided with a dedicated secure outdoor activity area with a minimum of 400 SF, perimeter fencing or equivalent secure enclosure, and shade provision. The submitted floor plans and site plan do not include such an area associated with the adult inpatient unit. This deficiency must be resolved prior to plan approval.
fix_template:
1. Identify on the site plan a secure outdoor activity area of minimum 400 SF directly accessible from the adult psychiatric inpatient unit without passing through unsecured areas.
2. Show perimeter security fencing (minimum 8-ft height, anti-climb, with no footholds) or equivalent secure enclosure around the outdoor area on the architectural and civil drawings.
3. Provide shade by means of a permanent shade structure, covered walkway, or mature trees; indicate the shade structure on the drawings with dimensions.
4. Confirm that the outdoor activity area design incorporates anti-ligature principles consistent with the interior of the inpatient unit (no exposed overhead anchors, no chain-link fencing that could be used as a climbing or ligature anchor).
5. Reference WAC 246-322-230 on the applicable drawing sheet notes.

description: Two-way audio nurse call with staff location integration required at each patient bed
violation_template: PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — NURSE CALL SYSTEM: The technology specifications and low-voltage drawings for the proposed {occupancy} indicate a single-call-light nurse call system at patient beds. WAC 246-320-226 requires new Washington hospital construction to provide two-way audio nurse call capability at each patient bed, not a single visual call light only. Additionally, new construction must integrate the nurse call system with a staff location or real-time location system (RTLS) or staff badge/identification system. The current design does not meet these requirements. Revise the nurse call specifications and drawings accordingly.
fix_template:
1. Specify a UL-listed two-way audio nurse call system for all patient bed locations in the proposed {occupancy}; provide the manufacturer's product data sheets confirming two-way audio capability at the bed station.
2. Show on the low-voltage/technology drawings the head-end nurse call controller, corridor light/dome light units, staff stations, and the pathway for integration with the staff location or RTLS badge system.
3. Provide a sequence of operations or functional description describing how the nurse call system integrates with staff location data to direct calls to the nearest available caregiver.
4. Confirm that the nurse call system and RTLS integration comply with UL 1069 (Hospital Signaling and Nurse Call Equipment) and applicable WAC 246-320-226 technology requirements.

description: Type I-A or I-B construction required for new hospital buildings exceeding 55 feet in height
violation_template: PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — CONSTRUCTION TYPE: The proposed {occupancy} exceeds 55 feet in building height as measured per IBC 2021 §202. Per WAC 246-320 and Washington State Building Code adopting IBC 2021 Table 504.3, hospital buildings (I-2 occupancy, Risk Category IV) exceeding this height threshold must be classified as Type I-A or Type I-B construction. The cover sheet and structural notes for this project designate construction type as {construction_type}, which does not meet the required fire-resistive construction type for this building height. Revise the construction documents to reflect a compliant construction type with structural members meeting the required fire-resistance ratings.
fix_template:
1. Revise the cover sheet, architectural specifications (Division 01 and 07), and structural notes to designate the building as Type I-A or Type I-B construction per IBC 2021 Table 601.
2. Ensure all primary structural members (columns, beams, floor/roof construction) are provided with fire-resistance ratings consistent with the selected construction type (Type I-A: primary structural frame 3 hours, floors 2 hours; Type I-B: primary structural frame 2 hours, floors 2 hours) per IBC Table 601.
3. Coordinate with the structural engineer to confirm that all structural steel members are encased in fire-resistive assemblies or protected with intumescent coating with tested ratings per the selected construction type.
4. Update the building code analysis sheet to reflect the correct construction type, allowable height, and allowable area per IBC 2021 Table 504.

description: Medical waste management plan and compliant waste storage room required at project submittal
violation_template: PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — MEDICAL WASTE MANAGEMENT: The construction document submittal for the proposed {occupancy} does not include a medical waste management plan as required by WAC 246-320-131 and WAC 246-203. Washington-licensed hospitals must submit a medical waste management plan addressing biomedical waste, sharps disposal, and chemotherapy waste to WADOH at the time of construction document submittal. Additionally, the floor plans do not clearly identify a dedicated, separate, ventilated medical waste storage room with appropriate labeling and secure access. These deficiencies must be addressed prior to plan approval.
fix_template:
1. Prepare a medical waste management plan addressing biomedical waste (including biohazardous materials), sharps waste, and chemotherapy/hazardous pharmaceutical waste; the plan must identify storage procedures, container types, collection schedules, and disposal contractor information consistent with WAC 246-203.
2. Show on the floor plans a dedicated medical waste storage room, clearly labeled 'Biohazardous Waste Storage,' with a lockable door, smooth cleanable surfaces, floor drain, and mechanical exhaust ventilation (minimum 10 ACH, exhausted directly to outside with no air recirculation).
3. Confirm that the medical waste storage room is separate from general trash, linen, and clean/sterile supply storage areas and that access is restricted to authorized personnel.
4. Include the medical waste management plan as an appendix to the WADOH construction document submittal.

description: Hospital pharmacy must comply with WAC 246-878 and USP 797/800 for sterile and hazardous drug compounding
violation_template: PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — PHARMACY / STERILE COMPOUNDING: The pharmacy design for the proposed {occupancy} does not demonstrate compliance with WAC 246-878 (Washington Pharmacy Quality Assurance Commission) requirements applicable to hospital pharmacies performing sterile compounding. The construction documents must demonstrate that the clean room design for sterile compounding meets USP Chapter 797 (sterile preparation) and USP Chapter 800 (hazardous drug handling) environmental, HVAC, and physical design requirements, in addition to FGI 2022 pharmacy room design standards. No USP 797/800 design documentation or pressure relationship diagram for the clean room suite has been included in this submittal.
fix_template:
1. Provide a pressure relationship diagram for the pharmacy clean room suite showing the ISO classification of each space (ISO 5 primary engineering control, ISO 7 buffer room, ISO 8 ante room), directional airflow, and differential pressure setpoints per USP 797 and USP 800.
2. Include HVAC design parameters for the clean room on the mechanical drawings: supply air volume, HEPA filtration (ULPA for hazardous drug areas), temperature (66–72°F), relative humidity (30–60%), and minimum air change rates per USP 797/800.
3. Specify that all clean room construction materials (walls, floors, ceilings, pass-throughs) are non-shedding, non-porous, and cleanable; reference WAC 246-878 and USP 797/800 in the pharmacy specifications.
4. Coordinate the pharmacy design review with the Washington State Pharmacy Quality Assurance Commission (PQAC) and include evidence of PQAC pre-application consultation in the WADOH submittal if available.

description: Emergency generator must provide 96-hour on-site fuel supply with 10-second automatic transfer
violation_template: PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — IL-EP-001 (Emergency Power System): The submitted documents indicate an emergency generator with a fuel storage capacity of less than 96 hours at full load, which does not meet the Illinois Department of Public Health requirement under 77 IAC 250.210 and NFPA 110 Level 1. Additionally, the automatic transfer switch (ATS) sequence of operation does not confirm transfer to emergency power within the required 10-second interval for all Type 1 essential electrical system loads, including life safety and critical branches. Illinois hospitals must maintain uninterrupted emergency power capability for a minimum of 96 hours without resupply. The proposed fuel tank sizing and ATS coordination scheme must be revised prior to IDPH approval.
fix_template:
1. Recalculate generator full-load fuel consumption and provide manufacturer-certified fuel consumption data; size on-site fuel storage tanks to supply a minimum of 96 hours of continuous operation at rated load per 77 IAC 250.210 and NFPA 110-2019 Section 7.3.4.
2. Revise the automatic transfer switch specifications to confirm maximum transfer time of 10 seconds for all life safety and critical branch loads; include an ATS sequence-of-operations narrative on the electrical drawings.
3. Submit a Level 1 Emergency Power Supply (EPS) compliance statement signed and sealed by the engineer of record referencing NFPA 110 and 77 IAC 250.210.
4. Provide a load schedule for the essential electrical system separating life safety branch, critical branch, and equipment branch loads in accordance with NFPA 99-2021 and NFPA 70 Article 517.
5. Include fuel tank secondary containment details and Illinois EPA compliance documentation for any above-ground fuel storage exceeding 1,100 gallons per 35 IAC 732.

description: Airborne Infection Isolation (AII) room required in all general acute care hospitals; must maintain negative pressure with HEPA-filtered exhaust
violation_template: PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — IL-INF-001 (Airborne Infection Isolation Room): The submitted drawings do not indicate an Airborne Infection Isolation (AII) room or do not demonstrate that the proposed AII room meets the requirements of 77 IAC 250.230 and FGI Guidelines for Design and Construction of Hospitals. Illinois general acute care hospitals are required to provide a minimum of one AII room with continuous negative pressure differential (minimum -0.01 in. w.g. relative to the corridor), a minimum of 12 air changes per hour total (2 ACH outside air), and HEPA-filtered exhaust to the building exterior. The current mechanical schedules and room data sheets do not confirm these parameters. The exhaust discharge location does not appear to comply with ASHRAE 170 minimum separation requirements from air intakes and occupied areas.
fix_template:
1. Designate and clearly label a minimum of one AII room on the floor plan; provide a dedicated room data sheet confirming negative pressure of at least -0.01 in. w.g. relative to adjacent corridor and anteroom per 77 IAC 250.230 and ASHRAE 170 Table 7.1.
2. Update the mechanical schedule to show a minimum of 12 total ACH (minimum 2 ACH outdoor air) for the AII room; HEPA filtration (99.97% efficiency at 0.3 micron) must be installed on the exhaust stream before air is discharged to the exterior.
3. Provide exhaust outlet location on the site plan or building section demonstrating a minimum 25-foot separation from any outdoor air intake, operable window, or occupied pedestrian area per ASHRAE 170-2021 Section 7.4.
4. Include a pressure monitoring system with a visual and audible alarm at the room entrance and at the nursing station to continuously confirm negative pressure; tie alarm to the building automation system (BAS) per FGI 2022 Section 2.2-3.6.
5. Submit ICRA documentation confirming infection control measures during construction or renovation of the AII room area per 77 IAC 250.230.

description: ICRA Class III or IV required for all occupied hospital construction activities; formal ICRA plan must be submitted with permit application
violation_template: PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — IL-INF-002 (Infection Control Risk Assessment): The construction documents submitted for review do not include an Infection Control Risk Assessment (ICRA) plan as required by 77 IAC 250.230 for construction activity occurring within or adjacent to an occupied healthcare facility. The scope of work described — including demolition, HVAC duct penetrations, and wall openings in proximity to patient care areas — constitutes a Class III or Class IV ICRA activity level per the Association for Professionals in Infection Control (APIC) matrix. An ICRA plan detailing barrier types, negative pressure requirements, traffic control, and patient relocation protocols must be submitted to IDPH before permit issuance and construction commencement.
fix_template:
1. Complete an ICRA matrix assessment per APIC guidelines and the Joint Commission EC standards to determine the activity and risk class for each phase of construction; submit the completed ICRA form with the IDPH permit application per 77 IAC 250.230.
2. Provide a phasing plan showing temporary construction barriers (minimum 0.25-inch drywall or equivalent), locations of HEPA-filter equipped negative air machines, and directional airflow to prevent particulate migration into occupied patient care areas.
3. Document worker entry and egress routes, dust-control boot covers or tacky mat locations, and debris transport paths that avoid occupied corridors; include a daily ICRA log template for contractor use.
4. Identify a responsible infection control officer (ICO) by name and contact information; confirm ICO will conduct pre-construction walk-through and sign off on barrier installation before any demolition begins.
5. Submit the ICRA plan to the hospital's Infection Control Committee for review and approval prior to submission to IDPH; include the committee's written approval in the permit application package.

description: Operating room minimum 400 SF net (exceeds FGI 360 SF); minimum 20 ACH total ventilation required
violation_template: PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — IL-SU-001 (Operating Room Size and Ventilation): The proposed operating room(s) as dimensioned on the architectural drawings do not meet the Illinois IDPH minimum net floor area of 400 square feet exclusive of fixed casework, equipment alcoves, and walls, as required by 77 IAC 250.220. This Illinois-specific requirement exceeds the FGI 2022 minimum of 360 SF and takes precedence. Additionally, the mechanical room data sheets indicate total air change rates below the required 20 ACH minimum for operating rooms, with outdoor air supply below the required 4 ACH minimum. All supply air must be delivered through ceiling-mounted HEPA-filtered laminar or unidirectional diffusers over the surgical field. The current reflected ceiling plan does not demonstrate compliant supply diffuser placement.
fix_template:
1. Revise the architectural floor plan to provide a minimum 400 SF net area per operating room, measured from finished face of wall to finished face of wall and exclusive of all fixed or built-in casework and equipment alcoves, per 77 IAC 250.220.
2. Update the mechanical room data sheets and air handling unit schedules to confirm a minimum of 20 total ACH and minimum 4 ACH outside air for each operating room; provide engineering calculations demonstrating compliance.
3. Revise the reflected ceiling plan to show ceiling-mounted supply diffusers providing unidirectional (laminar) airflow across the surgical field; diffuser array must cover a minimum of the operating table footprint plus 12 inches on each side per ASHRAE 170-2021 Section 7.5.
4. Confirm positive pressure differential (+0.01 in. w.g. minimum) of the OR relative to the scrub corridor and adjacent spaces; provide a pressure relationship diagram on the mechanical drawings per ASHRAE 170 Table 7.1.
5. Provide room temperature and humidity control documentation showing OR setpoints of 68–75°F and 20–60% RH with independent controls per 77 IAC 250.220 and ASHRAE 170 Table 7.1.

description: Scrub sink required within 20 linear feet of each OR entry; minimum 2 scrub positions per operating room
violation_template: PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — IL-SU-002 (Scrub Facilities): The submitted floor plan does not demonstrate that each operating room is served by a scrub sink located within 20 linear feet of the OR entry door, as required by 77 IAC 250.220. Furthermore, the number of scrub positions shown adjacent to certain operating rooms is fewer than the required minimum of two (2) scrub positions per OR. Scrub positions must be located in the sterile corridor or scrub alcove directly serving the designated OR, and the measurement of 20 linear feet is taken along the most direct path of travel from the scrub sink to the OR entry. The current plumbing plans do not clearly dimension these distances, and the scrub sink count per OR must be confirmed.
fix_template:
1. Dimension the travel distance from each scrub sink to the corresponding OR entry door on the floor plan; confirm all scrub sinks are within 20 linear feet measured along the path of travel per 77 IAC 250.220.
2. Provide a minimum of two (2) scrub positions at each scrub station serving each operating room; label scrub positions clearly on the architectural and plumbing plans.
3. Specify hands-free (knee or foot-operated) controls for all scrub sinks; specify sensor-activated or wrist-blade faucets where knee controls are not feasible per FGI 2022 and IDPH infection control guidance.
4. Confirm plumbing fixture units and hot-water supply adequacy for simultaneous use of all scrub positions; include hot-water temperature maintenance provisions (thermostatic mixing valve at point of use, 100–120°F delivery) on plumbing drawings.
5. Verify that scrub alcoves do not obstruct the path of travel for sterile case carts between the sterile core and the operating room; include minimum 6-foot clear width in the adjacent sterile corridor on the floor plan.

description: ICU and NICU patient rooms must be single-bed; two-bed ICU configurations are not permitted in Illinois
violation_template: PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — IL-PR-001 (ICU/NICU Single-Bed Requirement): The submitted floor plan depicts two-bed configurations within the proposed Intensive Care Unit (ICU) and/or Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU). Illinois IDPH regulations under 77 IAC 250.310 require all ICU and NICU patient care spaces to be arranged as single-occupancy rooms. Multi-bed open-bay or two-bed ICU arrangements do not comply with Illinois requirements and cannot be approved by IDPH regardless of any waiver or variance from FGI standards. The floor plan must be revised to provide single-bed rooms throughout all critical care units before IDPH plan approval can be granted.
fix_template:
1. Revise the ICU and NICU floor plans to eliminate all multi-bed configurations; provide fully enclosed, single-occupancy patient rooms throughout each critical care unit per 77 IAC 250.310.
2. Confirm that each single-bed ICU room provides a minimum clear floor area of 200 SF (ICU) or 150 SF (NICU) exclusive of the toilet room and fixed casework; dimension the clear floor area on the floor plan.
3. Provide a family zone within or immediately adjacent to each single-bed room with space for at least one family member; include a recliner or fold-out sleeping surface and storage in the room layout.
4. Confirm that each ICU room includes a private toilet room with head wall or toilet directly accessible from the patient room without entering the corridor per 77 IAC 250.310 and FGI 2022 Section 2.2-2.6.
5. Submit a revised unit floor plan with an accurate room count summary table listing each room type, room number, and net area to confirm full compliance before resubmission to IDPH.

description: Minimum patient room area of 120 SF for single-occupancy; 100 SF per patient in semi-private (two-bed) rooms
violation_template: PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — IL-PR-002 (Patient Room Minimum Area): The proposed patient rooms as dimensioned on the submitted architectural drawings do not meet the Illinois IDPH minimum room area requirements under 77 IAC 250.310. Single-occupancy patient rooms must provide a minimum of 120 square feet of clear floor area, measured from finished face of wall to finished face of wall and excluding the toilet room, closets, lockers, wardrobes, alcoves, and fixed casework. Semi-private (two-bed) rooms must provide a minimum of 100 square feet per patient bed position under the same measurement convention. The current room dimensions result in net areas below these minimums for several rooms identified on the drawings. This deficiency must be resolved before IDPH will approve the permit.
fix_template:
1. Prepare a room area calculation table for all patient rooms showing gross room dimensions, deductions for toilet room, closets, and fixed casework, and resulting net clear floor area; confirm all single-occupancy rooms meet 120 SF net and all semi-private rooms meet 100 SF net per bed position per 77 IAC 250.310.
2. Revise the floor plan to enlarge any rooms that fall below the minimum; coordinate with structural drawings to confirm that any wall relocations are feasible within the structural bay.
3. Confirm that the minimum 3-foot clear circulation path is maintained around three sides of each patient bed after furniture placement; show bed placement and 3-foot clearance zone on a representative room layout drawing.
4. Confirm toilet room accessibility per Illinois Accessibility Code (IAC) and ADA Standards for Accessible Design; provide turning radius and fixture clearance dimensions on the toilet room floor plan.
5. Verify that revised room areas do not conflict with the approved plumbing, HVAC, or electrical layouts; resubmit coordinated architectural, mechanical, and plumbing drawings reflecting the corrected room sizes.

description: Smoke compartments in patient care areas must not exceed 22,500 SF; Illinois follows NFPA 101 Life Safety Code for healthcare occupancies
violation_template: PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — IL-FLS-001 (Smoke Compartment Maximum Area): The fire and life safety plans submitted for review indicate one or more smoke compartments within patient care areas that exceed the maximum allowable area of 22,500 square feet as required by NFPA 101-2021 Section 18.3.7 as adopted by Illinois under 77 IAC 250. The smoke compartments must be bounded by smoke barriers extending from the floor deck to the roof or floor deck above, with a minimum 1-hour fire resistance rating. Smoke barrier doors must be minimum 20-minute rated, self-closing, and equipped with vision panels. The current code-compliance narrative and plans must be revised to reflect compliant smoke compartment layouts throughout all patient care floors.
fix_template:
1. Recalculate the area of each smoke compartment on all patient care floors; revise the smoke barrier layout on the floor plan to ensure no compartment exceeds 22,500 SF per NFPA 101-2021 Section 18.3.7 and 77 IAC 250.
2. Confirm smoke barriers extend from the floor slab to the underside of the deck above (including through interstitial spaces, mechanical plenums, and ceiling cavities); show barrier continuity on building sections and reflected ceiling plans.
3. Specify smoke barrier doors as a minimum 20-minute fire-rated assembly, self-closing or automatic-closing upon smoke detection, with vision panels meeting NFPA 101 Section 8.3; show door hardware schedule and labeling on the door schedule.
4. Confirm that each smoke compartment contains or provides access to a refuge area that can accommodate the relocate-in-place population at 30 SF per non-ambulatory patient per NFPA 101-2021 Section 18.7.2; calculate and document refuge capacity on the life safety plans.
5. Coordinate with the fire alarm consultant to confirm that the smoke detection system activates automatic closing of all smoke barrier doors within the affected compartment; include a system narrative and sequence of operations in the fire alarm submittals.

description: IDPH plan review and approval required before construction commencement; Form IL-440 must be submitted with construction documents
violation_template: PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — IL-GEN-001 (IDPH Plan Review Authorization): Construction documents have been submitted for review; however, the application package does not include the completed and signed Illinois Department of Public Health Form IL-440 (Application for Plan Review of Health Care Facilities), or the form submitted is incomplete. Under 77 IAC 250.110, no construction, renovation, or alteration of a licensed healthcare facility may commence without prior written approval from IDPH. The submission must include the completed IL-440 form, applicable plan review fee, and a minimum of two (2) sets of signed and sealed construction documents. IDPH will not issue a plan approval letter until the application is complete. Commencement of construction prior to IDPH approval may result in enforcement action and required removal of non-approved work.
fix_template:
1. Complete and submit Illinois IDPH Form IL-440 (Application for Plan Review of Health Care Facilities) in full; ensure the form is signed by the facility's authorized representative and the engineer or architect of record per 77 IAC 250.110.
2. Calculate and remit the applicable IDPH plan review fee based on the estimated construction cost; include the fee payment (check payable to IDPH or online payment confirmation) with the application.
3. Submit a minimum of two (2) complete sets of construction documents bearing the wet or electronic seal of the licensed architect and all licensed engineers of record; digital submissions must comply with IDPH electronic submission standards.
4. Include a project narrative describing the scope of work, affected occupancy categories, estimated number of patients affected, and proposed construction phasing with dates; attach the narrative to the Form IL-440 application.
5. Do not issue a Notice to Proceed or allow any construction activity on the licensed facility premises until written IDPH plan approval is received; retain the IDPH approval letter on file and available for inspection throughout the construction period.

description: Illinois Energy Conservation Code (IECC 2021) commissioning required for building system projects exceeding $500,000 in construction cost
violation_template: PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — IL-ENV-001 (Building Energy Commissioning): The project as described exceeds the $500,000 construction cost threshold that triggers mandatory enhanced building commissioning under the Illinois Energy Conservation Code (IECC 2021) as adopted by the Illinois Capital Development Board and enforced through IDPH for licensed healthcare facilities under 77 IAC 250. The submitted construction documents do not include a commissioning plan, a designated Commissioning Authority (CxA), or a commissioning specification section. IECC 2021 Section C408 requires that all HVAC, electrical, and plumbing systems be subject to a documented commissioning process with a written commissioning plan submitted to IDPH prior to system startup. The omission of commissioning documentation constitutes a plan deficiency requiring resolution before permit approval.
fix_template:
1. Designate a qualified Commissioning Authority (CxA) who is independent of the design and construction team; provide the CxA's name, firm, and qualifications (ASHRAE CxP, BCxP, or equivalent) in the project manual and on the cover sheet of the commissioning specification.
2. Prepare and submit a Commissioning Plan consistent with IECC 2021 Section C408 and ASHRAE Guideline 0-2019; the plan must identify all systems subject to commissioning, required functional performance tests, acceptance criteria, and the commissioning schedule.
3. Include a commissioning specification section (typically Division 01) in the project manual directing the general contractor to facilitate commissioning activities; specify contractor submittals, prefunctional checklists, and startup documentation requirements.
4. Require the CxA to prepare and submit a Commissioning Report to IDPH upon project completion documenting the results of all functional performance tests, deficiencies identified and corrected, and a declaration of system readiness; submit the report with the Certificate of Occupancy application.
5. Coordinate commissioning requirements with IDPH plan review staff to confirm any state-specific reporting formats or IDPH submission requirements beyond IECC 2021 minimums; contact IDPH at (217) 782-7412 for current commissioning submission guidance.

description: AII room required in acute care hospitals; minimum negative pressure, 12 ACH, and HEPA filtration on exhaust
violation_template: PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — PA-INF-001 (Airborne Infection Isolation Room): The construction documents submitted for Pennsylvania Department of Health (DOH) review do not demonstrate compliance with the Airborne Infection Isolation (AII) room requirements of 28 Pa. Code §51.23. Each acute care hospital licensed in Pennsylvania must provide a minimum of one AII room with documented continuous negative pressure (-0.01 in. w.g. minimum relative to the adjoining corridor or anteroom), a minimum of 12 total air changes per hour with a minimum of 2 ACH of outdoor air, and HEPA-filtered exhaust (99.97% efficiency at 0.3 micron) discharged directly to the building exterior. The submitted mechanical schedules do not confirm the required pressure relationships, ACH rates, or HEPA filtration for the designated isolation room(s). Additionally, the HVAC system narrative does not address continuous monitoring of negative pressure differential with an alarm notification at the nursing station.
fix_template:
1. Designate and label a minimum of one AII room on the floor plan; provide a room data sheet confirming negative pressure of -0.01 in. w.g. or greater relative to adjacent corridor and anteroom, 12 total ACH (minimum 2 ACH outdoor), and HEPA exhaust per 28 Pa. Code §51.23 and ASHRAE 170-2021 Table 7.1.
2. Specify HEPA filter units (99.97% efficiency at 0.3 micron) on the exhaust system serving the AII room; provide manufacturer cut sheets and indicate HEPA unit location on the mechanical plans.
3. Show exhaust outlet location on the site plan or building section with minimum 25-foot separation from all outdoor air intakes, operable windows, and pedestrian areas per ASHRAE 170-2021 Section 7.4; include a note that exhaust shall not be recirculated to any other space.
4. Specify a continuous pressure differential monitoring device with a visual indicator at the room entrance and an audible/visual alarm at the nearest nursing station; connect the monitor to the building automation system (BAS) and require a documented response procedure per FGI 2022 Section 2.2-3.6.
5. Include a note on the drawings that the AII room must be tested and verified per ASHRAE 170 before occupancy; submit the commissioning report to PA DOH Division of Safety Inspection prior to obtaining the certificate of occupancy.

description: ICRA plan required with permit application for any construction or renovation in or adjacent to an occupied healthcare facility
violation_template: PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — PA-INF-002 (Infection Control Risk Assessment): The permit application submitted to the Pennsylvania Department of Health does not include a completed Infection Control Risk Assessment (ICRA) plan as required for construction and renovation activities in or adjacent to occupied healthcare facilities. Per Pennsylvania DOH guidance consistent with 28 Pa. Code Chapter 51 and Joint Commission Environment of Care standards, an ICRA plan must accompany any permit application for work performed in a licensed acute care hospital where construction activities could affect occupied patient care areas, ventilation systems, or utility distribution. The absence of a formal ICRA plan constitutes an incomplete submission; DOH will not process the permit application without this documentation.
fix_template:
1. Complete an ICRA risk classification matrix using the APIC or equivalent methodology; assess each construction phase for activity type (Type A–D) and risk level based on proximity to at-risk patient populations; submit the completed matrix with the PA DOH permit application.
2. Develop a written ICRA plan including temporary barrier specifications (type, material, installation method), negative air pressure maintenance requirements, HEPA-filtered negative air machine placement, and a monitoring schedule for the duration of construction.
3. Identify all patient care areas, supply distribution, and air handling units within 50 feet of the construction zone; document planned controls to prevent disruption of airflow patterns, water intrusion, and biological hazard spread.
4. Designate an Infection Control Risk Assessment Officer (ICRAO) who will conduct a pre-construction walk-through with the contractor and sign off on barrier installation; include the ICRAO's name, title, and contact information in the ICRA plan submitted to DOH.
5. Establish a daily ICRA inspection log to be maintained on-site throughout construction; log must record barrier integrity checks, pressure differential readings, and any corrective actions taken; make the log available to PA DOH inspectors upon request.

description: Operating room minimum 360 SF net (FGI standard); air pressure must be positive relative to scrub corridor and adjacent spaces
violation_template: PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — PA-SU-001 (Operating Room Size and Pressure Relationships): The operating room(s) depicted on the architectural drawings do not meet one or more of the following requirements of 28 Pa. Code §51.31 and the FGI 2022 Guidelines as adopted by Pennsylvania DOH: (1) minimum net floor area of 360 square feet exclusive of fixed casework, columns, and wall thickness, and (2) a maintained positive pressure differential of +0.01 in. w.g. or greater relative to the scrub corridor, substerile room, and all adjacent spaces. The mechanical schedules as submitted do not clearly establish the air pressure relationships for the surgical suite, and dimensioned area calculations are not provided for the operating rooms. Both deficiencies must be addressed before DOH plan approval can be issued.
fix_template:
1. Provide a dimensioned floor plan with net area calculations for each operating room, measured from finished face of wall to finished face of wall excluding all fixed casework, built-in equipment, and wall thickness; confirm each OR meets a minimum 360 SF net per 28 Pa. Code §51.31.
2. Prepare a pressure relationship diagram for the entire surgical suite showing all spaces and their pressure relationships relative to adjacent spaces; confirm ORs are positive (+0.01 in. w.g. minimum) relative to all adjacent spaces per ASHRAE 170-2021 Table 7.1.
3. Update the mechanical room data sheets to show a minimum of 20 total ACH (minimum 4 ACH outdoor air) for each OR; specify ceiling-mounted HEPA-filtered supply diffusers providing unidirectional airflow across the surgical table per ASHRAE 170-2021 Section 7.5.
4. Confirm supply air temperature and humidity control for each OR between 68–75°F and 20–60% RH; show independent thermostatic controls on the mechanical floor plan and confirm setpoints on the room data sheets.
5. Include a note that OR pressure relationships and air volume will be balanced and verified during commissioning; submit commissioning test results to PA DOH Division of Safety Inspection prior to operating room use.

description: Post-anesthesia care unit (PACU) minimum 80 SF per patient bed position; minimum 6 ACH total ventilation
violation_template: PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — PA-SU-002 (Post-Anesthesia Care Unit): The proposed Post-Anesthesia Care Unit (PACU) as depicted in the submitted documents does not comply with the requirements of 28 Pa. Code §51.31 in the following respects: (1) one or more PACU patient bed positions does not provide a minimum of 80 square feet of clear floor area as measured between the centerlines of the adjacent patient positions and the wall behind the head of the bed, and (2) the mechanical room data sheet for the PACU indicates total air change rates below the required minimum of 6 ACH. Pennsylvania DOH requires these minimums to ensure adequate space for emergency intervention and sufficient air quality for patients recovering from anesthesia. Revised drawings must address both the area deficiency and the ventilation deficiency.
fix_template:
1. Provide a dimensioned floor plan of the PACU clearly showing each patient bay and the associated clear floor area; confirm each bay meets a minimum 80 SF clear floor area measured per FGI 2022 methodology and 28 Pa. Code §51.31.
2. Annotate the total number of PACU bays and the total PACU area on the floor plan; confirm there is sufficient total floor area to accommodate all proposed bays at the 80 SF minimum.
3. Update the mechanical room data sheet for the PACU to reflect a minimum of 6 total ACH; provide engineering calculations showing PACU supply and exhaust air volumes and confirm the supply air system can maintain the minimum rate at design conditions.
4. Confirm a minimum of 2 ACH of outdoor air for the PACU; specify that PACU air is not recirculated to other occupancies and is exhausted or returned as required per ASHRAE 170-2021 Table 7.1.
5. Show that each PACU bay is served by medical gas outlets (oxygen, vacuum, air) at the head wall; provide the medical gas outlet schedule and confirm outlet quantities meet NFPA 99-2021 Table 5.1.9.2.1(a) for PACU.

description: Emergency power system must provide 96-hour on-site fuel and Level 1 EPS with 10-second automatic transfer per NFPA 110
violation_template: PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — PA-EP-001 (Emergency Power Supply System): The submitted electrical drawings and specifications do not demonstrate full compliance with the Pennsylvania DOH emergency power requirements under 28 Pa. Code Chapter 51 and NFPA 110 Level 1. Specifically, the fuel tank sizing calculations provided indicate less than 96 hours of on-site fuel storage at full generator load, and the automatic transfer switch (ATS) specifications do not explicitly confirm a maximum 10-second transfer time from normal to emergency power for all life safety and critical branch loads. Pennsylvania licensed acute care hospitals must maintain on-site fuel storage sufficient for 96 hours of continuous generator operation and must demonstrate that all essential electrical system loads receive power within 10 seconds of a normal supply interruption. Revised documentation must address both deficiencies.
fix_template:
1. Obtain generator manufacturer certified fuel consumption data at rated load; recalculate required fuel tank volume for 96 hours of continuous operation and confirm on-site fuel storage (including day tanks and sub-base tanks) meets this requirement; include the calculation in the permit submittal per 28 Pa. Code Chapter 51 and NFPA 110-2019 Section 7.3.4.
2. Revise ATS specifications to explicitly state a maximum 10-second transfer time; include a sequence of operations narrative on the one-line diagram confirming load transfer sequence for life safety branch, critical branch, and equipment branch per NFPA 70 Article 517 Part III.
3. Provide a full essential electrical system load schedule separating loads by branch (life safety, critical, equipment) with connected and demand loads; confirm generator kW rating is sufficient to carry the full connected essential electrical load.
4. Include secondary containment details for all fuel storage tanks meeting Pennsylvania DEP and EPA requirements; provide spill prevention and countermeasure (SPCC) plan reference if total above-ground oil storage exceeds 1,320 gallons per 40 CFR Part 112.
5. Coordinate with the PA DOH Division of Safety Inspection to schedule the required generator load bank test prior to certificate of occupancy; submit test results confirming rated kW output and transfer time within specified limits.

description: Minimum patient room area: 100 SF single-occupancy, 80 SF per bed in double-occupancy rooms
violation_template: PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — PA-PR-001 (Patient Room Minimum Floor Area): The architectural drawings submitted for Pennsylvania DOH review indicate patient room floor areas that do not meet the minimum requirements of 28 Pa. Code §51.23. Single-occupancy patient rooms must provide a minimum of 100 square feet of clear floor area, measured from finished wall face to finished wall face exclusive of toilet room, closets, and fixed wardrobes. Double-occupancy (two-bed) rooms must provide a minimum of 80 square feet of clear floor area per bed position under the same measurement method. One or more proposed patient rooms on the submitted drawings fall below these minimums. This deficiency must be corrected in the construction documents before DOH plan approval will be granted.
fix_template:
1. Prepare and include in the submission a room area summary table listing every patient room by room number, occupancy type (single/double), gross dimensions, deductions (toilet, closet, fixed casework), and resulting net clear floor area; flag any room below the applicable minimum.
2. Revise the floor plan to enlarge all non-compliant rooms to meet the minimum 100 SF (single) or 80 SF per bed (double) per 28 Pa. Code §51.23; coordinate revisions with structural, mechanical, and plumbing plans.
3. Show a representative room furniture layout for both a single-occupancy and a double-occupancy room demonstrating a minimum 3-foot clear passage on at least three sides of each patient bed per FGI 2022 patient room design criteria.
4. Confirm that each patient room includes a toilet room accessible directly from the patient room without entering the corridor; provide toilet room dimensions with accessible clearances per ADA Standards and Pennsylvania Accessibility Standards (34 Pa. Code Chapter 60).
5. Confirm that revised room areas comply with the window natural light requirement of 28 Pa. Code §51.23 (minimum window-to-floor ratio or minimum window area per bed); annotate window sizes on the floor plan and calculate compliance ratio.

description: Pharmacy sterile compounding area must comply with USP 797; requires separate negative-pressure ISO Class 7 cleanroom with ante-room
violation_template: PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — PA-PHARM-001 (Pharmacy Sterile Compounding Facility): The proposed hospital pharmacy includes sterile compounding operations but the submitted construction documents do not demonstrate compliance with USP Chapter 797 as required by the Pennsylvania State Board of Pharmacy and enforced by PA DOH under 28 Pa. Code Chapter 51 for licensed hospital pharmacies. The sterile compounding area must be designed as a separate, enclosed ISO Class 7 (or better) cleanroom space with a negative pressure differential relative to the adjacent ante-room and general pharmacy. The current floor plan does not show a compliant ante-room, and the mechanical data sheets do not indicate a classified HVAC system with the required air changes, pressure relationships, and HEPA filtration for a USP 797 Hazardous Drug Secondary Engineering Control (HD-SEC) space or non-hazardous compounding area.
fix_template:
1. Design the sterile compounding room as a fully enclosed, ISO Class 7 secondary engineering control (SEC) space per USP 797; show the SEC and its ante-room on the architectural floor plan with dimensions; confirm the ante-room is ISO Class 8 or better and provides an ISO Class 5 primary engineering control (PEC — biological safety cabinet or compounding aseptic isolator) within the SEC.
2. Establish pressure relationships: for non-hazardous compounding, the SEC must be positive relative to the ante-room; for hazardous drug compounding (HD-SEC), the SEC must be negative relative to the ante-room (-0.01 in. w.g. minimum); document pressure relationships on a pressure diagram on the mechanical drawings per USP 797 and ASHRAE 170-2021.
3. Provide HVAC design data confirming ISO classification through minimum total ACH (typically 30 ACH or as verified by particle count per ISO 14644-1) and HEPA-filtered (99.97%) supply air; include a particle count and viable air sampling protocol to be performed before occupancy.
4. Specify a seamless, cleanable, non-shedding floor, wall, and ceiling system for the cleanroom and ante-room; provide a finish schedule and detail showing coved base, sealed penetrations, and flush door frames; surfaces must withstand cleaning with sporicidal agents per USP 797 Section 5.
5. Coordinate the final pharmacy design with the Pennsylvania State Board of Pharmacy for pre-certification review; submit the cleanroom qualification (IQ/OQ/PQ) report to PA DOH Division of Safety Inspection as part of the certificate of occupancy package per 28 Pa. Code Chapter 51 and 49 Pa. Code Chapter 27.

description: Pennsylvania adopts NFPA 101-2021 for healthcare occupancies; automatic sprinkler protection required throughout all patient care areas per NFPA 13
violation_template: PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — PA-FLS-001 (Automatic Sprinkler Protection): The fire protection drawings submitted for Pennsylvania DOH review do not demonstrate complete automatic sprinkler protection throughout the proposed construction area and adjacent patient care occupancies as required by NFPA 101-2021 Section 18.3.5 (new healthcare occupancies) or Section 19.3.5 (existing healthcare occupancies) as adopted by Pennsylvania under 28 Pa. Code Chapter 51. Sprinkler systems must be designed and installed per NFPA 13-2022 and must cover all areas of the building without exception, including closets, corridors, equipment rooms, and interstitial spaces accessible to personnel. The drawings indicate unsprinklered areas within the proposed project scope. This deficiency must be resolved before PA DOH will issue plan approval.
fix_template:
1. Revise the fire protection drawings to provide complete coverage throughout all proposed project areas, including all rooms, closets, corridors, mechanical rooms, interstitial spaces, and above-ceiling areas, per NFPA 101-2021 Section 18.3.5 and NFPA 13-2022.
2. Confirm the sprinkler system design basis (hydraulic calculation area, density, water supply) on the fire protection drawings; provide hydraulic calculations and a water supply analysis using the most hydraulically demanding design area per NFPA 13-2022 Chapter 19.
3. Specify appropriate sprinkler head types for patient care areas: quick-response concealed heads are required in patient rooms and corridors per NFPA 13; document head selection on the sprinkler head schedule.
4. Coordinate the sprinkler system with smoke compartment layouts; confirm that all smoke barrier walls include listed fire sprinkler heads on both sides, and that escutcheons are compatible with smoke barrier wall assemblies.
5. Provide a fire protection system narrative identifying the system type (wet pipe, dry pipe, pre-action), supply source, water supply test data (within 12 months), and connection to the building fire alarm system; submit the narrative to PA DOH Division of Safety Inspection with the permit application.

description: PA DOH plan review required before construction exceeding $100,000; submit to Division of Safety Inspection with signed and sealed documents
violation_template: PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — PA-GEN-001 (PA DOH Plan Review Authorization): The submitted project involves construction, renovation, or alteration of a licensed acute care hospital with an estimated construction cost exceeding $100,000, which requires prior plan review and approval by the Pennsylvania Department of Health, Division of Safety Inspection, under 28 Pa. Code §51.11. The application package is incomplete or was submitted without the required fee, signed and sealed construction documents, or project narrative. PA DOH will not commence plan review until a complete application is received. No construction may begin prior to receipt of written DOH plan approval; commencement of work without approval may result in a stop-work order, penalty assessment, and required demolition of unapproved construction.
fix_template:
1. Submit a complete plan review application to the PA DOH Division of Safety Inspection, Bureau of Facility Licensure and Certification, including the completed Application for Review of Plans and Specifications (DOH-1052) signed by the facility administrator and the engineer or architect of record.
2. Include two (2) complete sets of signed and sealed construction documents (or a single set with an electronic submission per current DOH digital submission standards) covering architectural, structural, mechanical, plumbing, electrical, and fire protection disciplines.
3. Calculate and remit the plan review fee based on the current PA DOH fee schedule (typically based on estimated construction cost); include a check payable to the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania or the online payment receipt with the application.
4. Provide a written project narrative describing the scope, affected licensed areas, number and types of patient beds affected, estimated construction cost, project schedule, and proposed phasing to minimize patient care disruption.
5. Await receipt of written PA DOH plan approval before issuing a Notice to Proceed or allowing any construction activity to begin; retain the DOH approval letter on-site throughout construction and make it available to DOH inspectors and local building officials upon request.
code_references: Pennsylvania Act 12 of 1951 (Health Care Facilities Act)

description: Certificate of Compliance required before occupancy of new or renovated areas; final inspection by PA DOH required
violation_template: PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — PA-GEN-002 (Certificate of Compliance / Final Inspection): This plan review comment is issued as a pre-construction notice: per 28 Pa. Code §51.15, no newly constructed, renovated, or altered area of a licensed healthcare facility may be placed into service or occupied by patients until a Certificate of Compliance has been issued by the Pennsylvania Department of Health following a satisfactory final inspection. The Certificate of Compliance must be requested by the facility, and the DOH inspection must confirm that all construction was completed in accordance with the DOH-approved plans and applicable codes. The construction documents, as a condition of this approval, must include a note on the cover sheet prohibiting occupancy prior to receipt of the Certificate of Compliance.
fix_template:
1. Add a general note to the cover sheet of the construction documents stating: 'No newly constructed or renovated space shall be occupied by patients or placed into clinical service prior to receipt of a Certificate of Compliance issued by the Pennsylvania Department of Health, Division of Safety Inspection, per 28 Pa. Code §51.15.'
2. Upon substantial completion of construction, submit a written request for final inspection to the PA DOH Division of Safety Inspection, including the name and contact of the on-site representative, a list of all DOH-approved permits for the project, and the proposed occupancy date.
3. Ensure all punch list items, HVAC commissioning reports, fire alarm acceptance tests, sprinkler system acceptance tests, and medical gas certification results are complete and available for DOH inspector review at the time of the final inspection.
4. Make available during the final inspection the ICRA compliance log, all contractor as-built drawings, O&M manuals for new equipment, and the generator load bank test report; organize these documents in a project closeout binder accessible on-site.
5. After the Certificate of Compliance is issued by DOH, retain the original certificate permanently in the facility's compliance records and make it available for all future DOH licensing surveys and inspections per 28 Pa. Code §51.15.
code_references: Pennsylvania Health Care Facilities Act (35 P.S. §448.101 et seq.)

description: Coastal Georgia hospitals must comply with ASCE 7-22 wind design requirements; Risk Category IV wind loads apply to all licensed hospitals
violation_template: PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — GA-WIN-001 (Wind Design — Coastal Risk): The structural drawings submitted for Georgia Department of Public Health (DPH) review do not demonstrate that the proposed hospital facility has been designed as a Risk Category IV structure in accordance with ASCE 7-22 Chapter 26 for wind loading, as required for Essential Facilities under the Georgia State Minimum Standard Codes and O.C.G.A. §8-2-20. Hospitals are classified as Essential Facilities (Risk Category IV) and must be designed for the elevated basic wind speeds applicable to their geographic location as mapped in ASCE 7-22 Figure 26.5-1D. For facilities in coastal and near-coastal Georgia counties (Bryan, Brantley, Camden, Charlton, Chatham, Glynn, Liberty, Long, McIntosh), higher design wind speeds and additional wind-borne debris protection requirements apply. The current structural basis of design narrative does not identify the site wind speed, risk category, or compliance path for wind-borne debris region requirements.
fix_template:
1. Revise the structural basis of design to identify the site's basic wind speed from ASCE 7-22 Figure 26.5-1D for Risk Category IV; document the wind speed, exposure category, topographic factor, and all other applicable wind parameters on the structural drawings cover sheet.
2. Confirm the facility is designed as Risk Category IV (Essential Facility) per ASCE 7-22 Table 1.5-1; apply all applicable importance factors and increased design pressures associated with Risk Category IV throughout the structural and envelope design.
3. For projects within the wind-borne debris region (basic wind speed ≥ 130 mph or ≥ 140 mph in hurricane-prone regions per ASCE 7-22 Section 26.12.3), specify impact-resistant glazing or protective shutters for all exterior windows and doors meeting ASTM E1996/E1886; include a glazing schedule noting impact ratings for each product.
4. Provide roof-to-wall and wall-to-foundation continuous load path details on the structural drawings demonstrating complete uplift and lateral load transfer from the roof to the foundation for the design wind event; include connection schedules and calculations.
5. Submit the structural engineer's wind design calculations sealed by a Georgia-licensed Structural Engineer (SE) or Professional Engineer (PE) with demonstrated competency in wind design; submit calculations and signed structural drawings to Georgia DPH Office of Health Planning with the permit application per O.C.G.A. §31-7-1.
code_references: Georgia State Minimum Standard Building Code (IBC 2021 as adopted)

description: Emergency generator must provide 72-hour on-site fuel supply with 10-second automatic transfer per NFPA 110
violation_template: PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — GA-EP-001 (Emergency Power System): The electrical construction documents submitted for Georgia DPH review do not demonstrate compliance with the emergency power supply requirements of Rule 290-9-7-.04 and NFPA 110-2019 for Level 1 systems serving licensed acute care hospitals. Specifically, the fuel storage calculation submitted provides less than 72 hours of on-site fuel at rated generator load, and the automatic transfer switch (ATS) specification does not explicitly confirm a maximum 10-second transfer time from normal power loss to emergency power availability for life safety and critical branch loads. Georgia DPH requires a minimum 72-hour on-site fuel supply and confirmed 10-second transfer for all licensed hospital essential electrical systems. These deficiencies must be corrected before Georgia DPH will issue plan approval.
fix_template:
1. Obtain certified generator fuel consumption data from the manufacturer at rated kW output; calculate required fuel tank volume for 72 continuous hours of operation at rated load; revise fuel tank sizing and include calculations in the permit submittal per Rule 290-9-7-.04 and NFPA 110-2019 Section 7.3.4.
2. Revise the ATS specification to state a maximum 10-second transfer time from loss of normal power to emergency power delivery for all life safety branch loads; include a sequence-of-operations narrative on the electrical drawings per NFPA 70 Article 517 Part III.
3. Provide a complete essential electrical system load schedule separated into life safety, critical, and equipment branches with connected and demand loads; confirm the generator kW rating exceeds the total demand load of all branches simultaneously.
4. Detail secondary containment for all above-ground fuel storage tanks per Georgia EPD requirements; include a spill prevention plan reference and confirm compliance with Georgia Underground Storage Tank regulations (Rule 391-3-15) if any underground tanks are used.
5. Schedule a pre-occupancy generator load bank test with the Georgia DPH Office of Health Planning inspector and submit a test report confirming rated kW output, voltage and frequency stability, and ATS transfer time within 10 seconds before the certificate of occupancy is issued.

description: AII room required in acute care hospitals; minimum negative pressure and 12 ACH total ventilation required
violation_template: PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — GA-INF-001 (Airborne Infection Isolation Room): The construction documents submitted for Georgia DPH review under Rule 290-9-7-.03 do not demonstrate provision of an Airborne Infection Isolation (AII) room that meets the required ventilation parameters for acute care hospitals in Georgia. A minimum of one AII room must be provided with a continuous negative pressure differential of at least -0.01 in. w.g. relative to the adjacent corridor or anteroom, a minimum of 12 total air changes per hour (minimum 2 ACH outdoor air), and HEPA-filtered exhaust discharged directly to the building exterior without recirculation. The submitted mechanical schedules and room data sheets do not confirm these parameters for the designated isolation room(s), and the exhaust discharge location has not been identified on the site plan relative to air intake locations.
fix_template:
1. Clearly designate and label the AII room(s) on the floor plan; provide a room data sheet for each AII room showing negative pressure (-0.01 in. w.g. or greater), minimum 12 total ACH (minimum 2 ACH outdoor air), and HEPA exhaust per Rule 290-9-7-.03 and ASHRAE 170-2021 Table 7.1.
2. Specify HEPA filtration (99.97% minimum efficiency at 0.3 micron) on the exhaust system for all AII rooms; indicate HEPA unit location on the mechanical floor plan and provide a manufacturer's cut sheet with filter efficiency certification.
3. Identify exhaust outlet location on the site plan or building elevation; demonstrate minimum 25-foot horizontal separation from all outdoor air intakes, operable windows, and public pedestrian areas per ASHRAE 170-2021 Section 7.4.
4. Specify a continuous pressure differential monitoring device with a local visual indicator at the room entrance door and a remote audible/visual alarm at the nursing station; connect the monitor output to the BAS with a documented response protocol per FGI 2022 Section 2.2-3.6.
5. Include a start-up and verification test protocol on the mechanical drawings confirming that all AII room pressure, ACH, and filtration parameters will be verified by a qualified testing, adjusting, and balancing (TAB) agency before clinical occupancy; submit TAB report to Georgia DPH with the occupancy application.

description: Operating room minimum 360 SF net; positive pressure relative to corridor with minimum 20 ACH total ventilation
violation_template: PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — GA-SU-001 (Operating Room — Area and Ventilation): The proposed operating room(s) as depicted in the submitted drawings do not satisfy the requirements of Georgia DPH Rule 290-9-7-.03 in one or more of the following areas: (1) minimum net floor area of 360 square feet measured from finished face of wall to finished face of wall exclusive of fixed casework and wall thickness, and/or (2) a minimum of 20 total air changes per hour with positive pressure (+0.01 in. w.g. minimum) relative to the adjacent scrub corridor and all contiguous spaces. The architectural plans do not provide dimensioned room areas with deductions for fixed elements, and the mechanical room data sheets do not confirm the required ACH and pressure relationships for the surgical suite. Both deficiencies must be addressed in the permit submittal to Georgia DPH.
fix_template:
1. Provide a dimensioned floor plan with calculated net area for each operating room; show deductions for fixed casework, built-in equipment, and columns; confirm each OR meets 360 SF net minimum per Rule 290-9-7-.03 and FGI 2022 Section 2.1-3.3.
2. Prepare a pressure relationship diagram for the surgical suite showing all spaces and their relative pressure to adjacent spaces; confirm each OR is positive (+0.01 in. w.g. minimum) relative to the scrub corridor, sub-sterile room, and all adjoining spaces per ASHRAE 170-2021 Table 7.1.
3. Update mechanical room data sheets to confirm a minimum of 20 total ACH for each OR with a minimum of 4 ACH outdoor air; provide engineering calculations demonstrating design airflow volumes meet the minimum ACH at design conditions.
4. Specify ceiling-mounted supply diffusers providing unidirectional (laminar) airflow over the surgical field; diffuser array must encompass at least the operating table footprint plus a 12-inch margin on all sides; include a reflected ceiling plan showing diffuser layout per ASHRAE 170-2021 Section 7.5.
5. Confirm OR temperature (68–75°F) and relative humidity (20–60% RH) control with independent room-level controls; add setpoints to the room data sheet and provide a control sequence of operations narrative in the mechanical specifications.

description: Minimum 100 SF single-bed patient room; maximum 2 beds per room in medical/surgical units
violation_template: PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — GA-PR-001 (Patient Room Size and Configuration): The submitted architectural drawings indicate patient room configurations that do not comply with the requirements of Georgia DPH Rule 290-9-7-.03. Single-bed patient rooms must provide a minimum of 100 square feet of clear floor area measured from finished wall face to finished wall face, excluding the toilet room, closets, and fixed wardrobes. Additionally, Rule 290-9-7-.03 limits patient rooms in medical/surgical units to a maximum of two (2) beds per room; ward-style multi-bed rooms with more than two beds are not permitted in Georgia licensed acute care hospitals. One or more rooms depicted on the submitted drawings fall below the 100 SF minimum or exceed the two-bed maximum configuration.
fix_template:
1. Calculate and tabulate the net clear floor area for each patient room on all nursing units; list each room with its gross dimensions, deductions for toilet room, closets, and fixed elements, and resulting net area; confirm all single-bed rooms meet 100 SF minimum per Rule 290-9-7-.03.
2. Revise the floor plan to eliminate any patient rooms exceeding a two-bed configuration in medical/surgical or general acute care units; provide revised room count and bed count summary for each nursing unit.
3. Show representative room furniture layouts for single-bed and double-bed rooms demonstrating a minimum 3-foot clear path on three sides of each patient bed; confirm the clear path is maintained even with standard furniture in place.
4. Verify that each patient room provides a private toilet room directly accessible from the patient room without requiring the patient to enter the corridor; provide toilet room dimensions showing ADA-compliant clearances per Georgia accessibility requirements (O.C.G.A. §30-3-1 et seq.) and ADA Standards.
5. Confirm exterior window provision per Rule 290-9-7-.03 (windows in patient rooms providing natural light and, where feasible, outdoor views); annotate window sizes and sill heights on the floor plan; confirm minimum glazed area ratios are met.

description: NFPA 101-2021 Life Safety Code adopted statewide for healthcare occupancies; automatic sprinklers required throughout per NFPA 13
violation_template: PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — GA-FLS-001 (Automatic Sprinkler and Life Safety Code Compliance): The fire and life safety documents submitted for Georgia DPH review do not demonstrate full compliance with NFPA 101-2021 Life Safety Code as adopted statewide under O.C.G.A. §31-7-1 and enforced by Georgia DPH for licensed healthcare facilities. Specifically, the fire protection drawings indicate areas within the proposed project scope that lack automatic sprinkler coverage. Georgia licensed hospitals must be fully protected by an automatic sprinkler system designed and installed per NFPA 13-2022 throughout the building, including all closets, corridors, mechanical rooms, ceiling plenums, and interstitial spaces. Additionally, the life safety code compliance plan/code analysis does not address all smoke compartment areas for patient care floors. These omissions must be corrected before Georgia DPH will issue plan approval.
fix_template:
1. Revise fire protection drawings to provide complete automatic sprinkler coverage throughout all project areas, including rooms, corridors, closets, mechanical spaces, and ceiling plenums, per NFPA 101-2021 Section 18.3.5 and NFPA 13-2022; no unsprinklered areas are permitted in a licensed hospital.
2. Provide hydraulic calculations and a water supply analysis for the most hydraulically demanding design area per NFPA 13-2022 Section 19.2; include a water supply test data sheet (test within 12 months) and the hydraulic calculation summary on the fire protection drawings.
3. Revise the life safety code analysis to address smoke compartment layout for all patient care floors; confirm no smoke compartment exceeds 22,500 SF per NFPA 101-2021 Section 18.3.7; show smoke barrier locations, ratings, and door specifications on the floor plans.
4. Specify quick-response sprinkler heads in all patient sleeping rooms and adjacent corridors per NFPA 13-2022; provide a sprinkler head schedule noting response time index (RTI), temperature rating, orifice size, and coverage area for each head type.
5. Coordinate the sprinkler system with the fire alarm system; confirm that the sprinkler system water flow alarm initiates a supervisory signal at the fire alarm control panel and at the local monitoring station per NFPA 72-2022; include a system interface narrative in the fire alarm submittal.

description: Georgia DPH construction permit required before work begins on licensed hospital facilities; submit to Office of Health Planning
violation_template: PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — GA-GEN-001 (Georgia DPH Construction Permit): Construction documents for a licensed acute care hospital in Georgia require prior plan review and approval by the Georgia Department of Public Health, Office of Health Planning, as a condition of the facility's license under O.C.G.A. §31-7-1 and Rule 290-9-7. The submitted application package is incomplete; the required Georgia DPH permit application form, applicable fee, and/or signed and sealed construction documents are missing or deficient. Georgia DPH will not process the permit application until a complete submittal is received. No construction may begin prior to written Georgia DPH approval. Commencement of work without approval constitutes a violation of Rule 290-9-7 and may result in enforcement action by Georgia DPH, including a license sanction against the facility.
fix_template:
1. Complete and submit the Georgia DPH Office of Health Planning permit application, including all required fields; ensure the application is signed by the licensed hospital's authorized representative and the engineer or architect of record per Rule 290-9-7 and O.C.G.A. §31-7-1.
2. Include two (2) complete sets of construction documents bearing the wet or electronic signature and seal of all licensed design professionals of record (architect, structural engineer, mechanical engineer, plumbing engineer, electrical engineer, fire protection engineer) registered in Georgia.
3. Remit the applicable Georgia DPH plan review fee calculated per the current Office of Health Planning fee schedule; attach the payment receipt or fee calculation worksheet to the application.
4. Provide a written project narrative describing the full scope of work, affected licensed categories and beds, estimated construction cost, schedule of construction phases, and proposed infection control measures for work adjacent to occupied patient care areas.
5. Do not authorize contractors to begin construction on the licensed facility premises until written Georgia DPH plan approval is in hand; post the approval letter at the construction site and make it available to Georgia DPH inspectors, local building officials, and the facility's accreditation body upon request.

description: ICRA plan mandatory for all occupied hospital construction; must be filed with the permit application to Georgia DPH
violation_template: PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — GA-INF-002 (Infection Control Risk Assessment — Construction): The permit application submitted to the Georgia Department of Public Health, Office of Health Planning, does not include an Infection Control Risk Assessment (ICRA) plan as required by Rule 290-9-7-.02 for construction and renovation activities in or adjacent to occupied licensed hospital facilities. The scope of work described in the application — including demolition, above-ceiling work, and penetrations of existing walls in proximity to patient care areas — constitutes a Class III or Class IV ICRA risk activity under the APIC classification matrix. An ICRA plan addressing construction barrier type, negative pressure requirements, traffic control, dust and moisture containment, and patient relocation protocols must be submitted to and accepted by Georgia DPH before the construction permit can be issued.
fix_template:
1. Complete the ICRA risk classification matrix (per APIC guidelines or equivalent) for each phase and location of construction activity; determine the activity type (A–D) and patient risk level for each phase; document the completed matrix in the ICRA plan submitted to Georgia DPH per Rule 290-9-7-.02.
2. Develop a written ICRA plan specifying temporary construction barrier type (minimum 0.25-inch drywall for Class III activities or hard-wall isolation for Class IV), barrier installation locations, and provisions for HEPA-filtered negative air machines maintaining negative pressure within the construction zone.
3. Provide a phasing diagram showing the sequence of construction, location of barriers at each phase, contractor entry and egress routes, and debris transport paths that avoid occupied patient care corridors; include tacky mat locations at all construction zone exits.
4. Designate an Infection Control Risk Assessment Officer (ICRAO) responsible for pre-construction walk-throughs, daily barrier inspections, and sign-off on phased construction access; include the ICRAO's name and contact information in the submitted ICRA plan.
5.
