Establish an on-site daily ICRA inspection log documenting barrier integrity, negative pressure readings at barrier penetrations, and any corrective actions taken; present the completed log to the Georgia DPH inspector during all site inspections and retain records for a minimum of three years per Rule 290-9-7 documentation requirements.

description: Emergency generator 96-hour fuel supply with 10-second transfer and 30-day fuel tank inspection log required
violation_template: NCDHSR PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — EMERGENCY POWER (NC-EP-001): The electrical construction documents submitted for the {occupancy} project in {county} County, {city} do not demonstrate compliance with North Carolina's emergency electrical system requirements under 10A NCAC 14C .2202 and the FGI Guidelines for Design and Construction of Hospitals as adopted by NCDHSR. The following deficiencies have been identified: (1) the emergency generator fuel storage capacity has not been specified or demonstrated to provide a minimum of 96 hours of continuous operation at full essential electrical system load without resupply; (2) the automatic transfer switch (ATS) has not been confirmed to transfer the essential electrical system to emergency power within 10 seconds of normal power loss; and (3) the construction documents do not identify the fuel log station location or establish the facility's obligation to perform and record the required 30-day fuel tank inspection and level verification. These provisions are mandatory for all ODH-licensed hospitals. Deficiencies must be corrected on the permit drawings prior to approval by the NCDHSR Construction Section.
fix_template:
1. Revise the electrical drawings and fuel system specifications to document that on-site fuel storage is sized for a minimum of 96 continuous hours of full essential-load operation; include a load calculation schedule confirming the design load figure used for tank sizing.
2. Confirm on the single-line electrical diagram that each automatic transfer switch (ATS) serving essential electrical system loads is rated and programmed to complete transfer within 10 seconds of normal-power failure; reference the manufacturer's time-delay settings in the specifications.
3. Add a note on the mechanical or electrical site plan identifying the on-site fuel tank location, secondary containment provisions per NC DEQ requirements, and access route for resupply vehicles.
4. Include in the O&M section of the specifications a note establishing the facility's obligation to maintain a written 30-day fuel-tank inspection log per NFPA 110 Section 8.3 and NCDHSR licensing requirements; indicate where the log will be stored and who is responsible for entries.
5. Resubmit revised drawings to the NCDHSR Construction Section, 1202 Mail Service Center, Raleigh, NC 27699-1202, for continued review.

description: Airborne Infection Isolation (AII) room required with negative pressure, minimum 12 ACH exhaust, and HEPA filtration
violation_template: NCDHSR PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — INFECTION CONTROL / VENTILATION (NC-INF-001): The mechanical construction documents submitted for the {occupancy} project in {county} County do not demonstrate that the proposed Airborne Infection Isolation (AII) room(s) comply with the ventilation requirements of 10A NCAC 14C .1917 and the FGI Guidelines as adopted by North Carolina DHSR. The following deficiencies have been identified: the AII room(s) are not confirmed to maintain a continuous negative pressure differential of at least -0.01 inches water gauge (2.5 Pa) with respect to the adjacent corridor; the minimum exhaust airflow rate of 12 air changes per hour (ACH) total, with all exhaust discharged directly to the outdoors, has not been specified; and HEPA filtration (99.97% efficiency at 0.3 microns) has not been specified at the exhaust discharge point where recirculation to another space may occur. Failure to provide code-compliant AII rooms presents a direct patient safety risk and will preclude licensure of the facility.
fix_template:
1. Revise the HVAC design to establish a minimum negative pressure differential of -0.01 inches water gauge (2.5 Pa) in each AII room relative to all adjacent spaces; provide pressure-relationship diagrams on the mechanical drawings showing all room-to-room pressure differentials.
2. Confirm the exhaust system delivers a minimum 12 total air changes per hour in each AII room; provide an air-balance schedule listing supply CFM, exhaust CFM, net pressure relationship, and ACH for each isolation room.
3. Route all AII room exhaust ductwork to fans that discharge directly to the building exterior; show exhaust fan locations and duct routing on the mechanical floor plan and roof plan, confirming discharge points are separated from any air intakes per FGI Guidelines Section 2.1-3.6.
4. Where exhaust cannot be fully dedicated to outdoor discharge, specify HEPA filtration rated at minimum 99.97% efficiency at 0.3 microns at the exhaust terminal or air-handling unit prior to any recirculation; include filter housing access and replacement provisions in the specifications.
5. Resubmit revised mechanical drawings and air-balance schedule to NCDHSR Construction Section for continued review, and coordinate with the infection control officer to confirm ICRA requirements for occupied construction are addressed.
code_references: CDC Guidelines for Environmental Infection Control 2003

description: Operating room minimum 360 SF net area; positive pressure 20 ACH; temperature 68-75 degrees F; humidity 20-60 percent
violation_template: NCDHSR PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — SURGICAL SUITE / HVAC (NC-SU-001): Review of the architectural and mechanical construction documents for the {occupancy} project in {county} County reveals that the proposed operating room(s) do not comply with one or more of the minimum standards established under 10A NCAC 14C .1909 and the FGI Guidelines as adopted by NCDHSR. The identified deficiencies include: (1) one or more operating rooms appear to be less than the required 360 square feet net clear floor area, excluding fixed and moveable equipment; (2) the mechanical drawings do not specify that the OR is maintained at continuous positive pressure relative to adjacent corridors and sub-sterile areas; (3) a minimum of 20 total air changes per hour (ACH) has not been confirmed on the air-balance schedule; and/or (4) the HVAC specifications do not confirm maintenance of a temperature range of 68°F to 75°F and a relative humidity of 20% to 60% at all times the OR is occupied. All four requirements are mandatory for licensure and must be addressed before NCDHSR will approve the construction documents.
fix_template:
1. Verify on the architectural floor plan that each operating room provides a minimum 360 square feet of net clear floor area, measured exclusive of fixed casework, booms, columns, and other fixed obstructions; add a net-area calculation note to the drawings and revise room size or layout as necessary.
2. Revise the HVAC design to maintain a continuous positive pressure differential in each OR with respect to all adjacent spaces; update the pressure-relationship diagram to show the OR at higher pressure than the sub-sterile corridor and scrub sink alcove.
3. Update the air-balance schedule to confirm a minimum 20 total air changes per hour in each OR, with at least 4 ACH composed of outside air; specify laminar-flow or diffuser ceiling configuration per FGI Guidelines Section 2.1-3.6 if applicable.
4. Add mechanical specifications and control sequences confirming the temperature control system maintains 68°F to 75°F and the humidification/dehumidification system maintains relative humidity within 20% to 60% at all times; specify BAS monitoring with an alarm for out-of-range conditions.
5. Resubmit revised architectural and mechanical drawings — including the updated air-balance schedule and HVAC control sequences — to the NCDHSR Construction Section for review and approval.

description: Minimum patient room 120 SF single occupancy, 100 SF per bed semi-private; toilet within room or shared with one adjacent room only
violation_template: NCDHSR PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — PATIENT ROOM / ARCHITECTURAL (NC-PR-001): The architectural construction documents submitted for the {occupancy} project in {county} County do not demonstrate compliance with 10A NCAC 14C .1908 minimum patient room area and toilet access requirements. The following deficiencies have been noted: (1) one or more single-occupancy patient rooms appear to provide less than the required 120 square feet of clear floor area, measured exclusive of toilet rooms, closets, lockers, vestibules, and fixed equipment; (2) one or more semi-private (multi-bed) rooms appear to provide less than 100 square feet of clear floor area per bed; and/or (3) the in-room toilet room or water closet serving each patient does not open directly from the patient room or from a shared toilet accessible exclusively to no more than one immediately adjacent patient room. Shared toilet arrangements that require patients to enter a public corridor to reach the toilet are not permitted. NCDHSR will not approve documents that do not meet these minimum space standards.
fix_template:
1. Add net clear floor area calculations to the architectural floor plan for every patient room; confirm single-occupancy rooms are 120 SF minimum and semi-private rooms provide 100 SF per bed, measuring from finished wall face and excluding toilet rooms, closets, vestibules, and fixed equipment zones.
2. Revise any non-compliant rooms by adjusting room dimensions, relocating non-essential elements, or reconfiguring the unit layout to achieve the required clear floor area; clearly dimension all revised rooms on the drawings.
3. Confirm that every patient sleeping position is served by an in-room toilet room or a toilet room directly accessible from within the patient room and from no more than one immediately adjacent patient room; show the adjacency and interconnecting door on the floor plan.
4. Ensure each toilet room serving inpatients is accessible and meets ADA 2010 Standards for Accessible Design as adopted by North Carolina; provide dimensioned toilet room plans confirming turning radius and fixture clearances.
5. Resubmit revised architectural floor plans with area calculations and toilet adjacency notes to the NCDHSR Construction Section for review and approval.

description: NFPA 101-2021 adopted statewide; automatic sprinkler system per NFPA 13 required throughout all hospital occupancies
violation_template: NCDHSR PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — FIRE AND LIFE SAFETY (NC-FLS-001): The fire protection construction documents submitted for the {occupancy} in {county} County do not confirm full compliance with the 2021 edition of NFPA 101, Life Safety Code, as adopted in North Carolina under 10A NCAC 14C, and the North Carolina State Fire Code (NCSFC). The submitted plans do not clearly demonstrate that an automatic sprinkler system designed and installed in accordance with NFPA 13 is provided throughout the entire building, including all occupied spaces, mechanical rooms, storage areas, and interstitial spaces where required. The fire alarm system narrative and riser diagrams are also insufficient to confirm compliance with NFPA 72, National Fire Alarm and Signaling Code. All sprinkler and fire alarm systems in healthcare occupancies must be submitted to and approved by both NCDHSR and the local Authority Having Jurisdiction — typically the Office of the State Fire Marshal (OSFM) — before construction begins.
fix_template:
1. Provide complete NFPA 13 sprinkler system drawings, including hydraulic calculations, riser diagram, water supply test data, and a reflected ceiling plan showing all sprinkler head locations, types, and coverage areas for every space in the building.
2. Confirm on the drawings that sprinkler coverage extends to all spaces, including mechanical rooms, electrical rooms, storage rooms, elevator shafts (where applicable), and any interstitial or crawl space areas per NFPA 13 and NFPA 101-2021 Chapter 18.
3. Submit fire alarm system drawings and a complete system narrative per NFPA 72; include the initiating device schedule, notification appliance layout, FACP location, and annunciator panel locations on the architectural floor plans.
4. Obtain a separate permit and plan review from the North Carolina Office of the State Fire Marshal (OSFM) for all fire protection systems; provide NCDHSR with a copy of the OSFM approval letter or permit number prior to NCDHSR final approval.
5. Resubmit coordinated fire protection, fire alarm, and architectural drawings to NCDHSR and confirm coordination with the local fire jurisdiction for inspection scheduling.

description: NCDHSR Construction Section plan review and written approval required before construction begins; submit to Raleigh office
violation_template: NCDHSR PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — PLAN REVIEW / GENERAL (NC-GEN-001): This comment serves as notice that construction, renovation, or alteration of a licensed healthcare facility in North Carolina may not commence until the North Carolina Department of Health and Human Services, Division of Health Service Regulation (DHSR), Construction Section has reviewed and issued written approval of the construction documents under 10A NCAC 14C .0100. A review of the submission package for the {occupancy} project in {county} County, {city} indicates that one or more of the following required elements are incomplete or missing: (a) a completed NCDHSR Plan Submittal Form (DHSR-100); (b) a statement of program describing the proposed use, occupancy, licensed bed count, and project scope; (c) the name, license number, and seal of the licensed North Carolina architect or engineer of record; and/or (d) evidence of concurrent local building department submittal. Construction commenced prior to NCDHSR approval is a violation of 10A NCAC 14C .0100 and may result in a Notice of Violation, required demolition of non-compliant work, and delay of facility licensure.
fix_template:
1. Complete and submit a NCDHSR Plan Submittal Form (DHSR-100), available on the DHSR Construction Section website; include the facility license number, owner's representative contact information, and the name of the licensed North Carolina design professional of record.
2. Prepare a written Statement of Program describing the full scope of work, proposed changes to licensed bed count or occupancy type, affected departments, and phasing plan for any construction in an occupied facility; attach to the submission package.
3. Ensure all drawings bear the original seal, signature, and license number of a licensed North Carolina architect (for architectural work) and licensed North Carolina engineers (structural, mechanical, electrical, plumbing); unlicensed or out-of-state seals are not accepted without a Certificate of Authorization from the NC Board of Architecture or NCBELS.
4. Submit complete construction documents — including site plan, floor plans, reflected ceiling plans, elevations, details, and specifications for all engineering disciplines — to the NCDHSR Construction Section, 1202 Mail Service Center, Raleigh, NC 27699-1202; include three (3) paper sets or submit electronically through the DHSR ePlans portal.
5. Coordinate the NCDHSR submittal with the local building department submittal; provide NCDHSR with a copy of the local building permit application receipt, and do not begin construction until both the NCDHSR written approval and the local building permit have been issued.

description: ICRA plan required for all construction in or adjacent to an occupied healthcare facility; submit with permit application to NCDHSR
violation_template: NCDHSR PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — INFECTION CONTROL / CONSTRUCTION (NC-INF-002): The construction documents submitted for the {occupancy} renovation or addition project in {county} County do not include a completed Infection Control Risk Assessment (ICRA) as required by NCDHSR and the FGI Guidelines for Design and Construction of Hospitals as adopted by North Carolina DHSR. For any construction activity occurring within, immediately adjacent to, or sharing an HVAC system with an occupied and licensed healthcare facility, an ICRA must be prepared by the design team in coordination with the facility's infection preventionist and submitted to NCDHSR with the permit application. The ICRA must identify the dust and airborne-contaminant risk class for each affected area, specify physical containment barriers and their locations on the floor plan, define pressure relationships between the construction zone and occupied areas, and include a written monitoring and contingency plan. Without an approved ICRA, NCDHSR cannot grant construction approval for work in or adjacent to an occupied facility.
fix_template:
1. Convene a multi-disciplinary ICRA team — including the architect, contractor, facility infection preventionist, and facility engineering staff — to complete a formal Infection Control Risk Assessment using the FGI Guidelines ICRA matrix; assign an ICRA risk class (Class I through IV) to each area affected by construction activity.
2. Prepare an ICRA Construction Activity Plan (CAP) documenting construction zone boundaries, type and location of temporary containment barriers (dust walls, negative-pressure enclosures, or anterooms), and sequencing for construction phasing that minimizes patient exposure.
3. Produce an ICRA floor plan overlay — clearly keyed to the architectural floor plans submitted to NCDHSR — showing all barrier locations, entry/exit points for construction personnel, route for debris removal, and adjacent patient care areas with their sensitivity class designations.
4. Include a written ICRA monitoring protocol specifying daily pressure-differential checks at the construction zone boundary, frequency of air sampling during high-risk activities (e.g., demolition, concrete cutting), and the responsible party and escalation procedure for any ICRA breach.
5. Submit the completed ICRA documentation — including the risk-class matrix, CAP narrative, and ICRA floor plan overlay — to the NCDHSR Construction Section with the permit application package; do not begin demolition or construction in the occupied facility until NCDHSR has issued written approval.

description: Operating room requires minimum 4 ACH outside air of the 20 ACH total; no recirculation via room fan-coil or unit ventilator units permitted
violation_template: NCDHSR PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — HVAC / OPERATING ROOM VENTILATION (NC-HVAC-001): The mechanical construction documents for the {occupancy} project in {county} County do not confirm compliance with the outside-air and recirculation requirements for operating rooms under 10A NCAC 14C .1909, ASHRAE 170-2021 Table 7.1, and the FGI Guidelines as adopted by North Carolina DHSR. The air-balance schedule submitted does not confirm that each operating room receives a minimum of 4 air changes per hour (ACH) of 100% outside air as part of the required 20 total ACH. Additionally, the mechanical design appears to include room-mounted fan-coil units, unit ventilators, or other recirculation devices within the OR, which is expressly prohibited — all supply air to the OR must be delivered through the central air-handling unit with appropriate filtration; no local recirculation units serving the OR space are permitted. These deficiencies affect patient safety through risk of surgical site infection and must be corrected before NCDHSR will approve the mechanical documents.
fix_template:
1. Revise the air-balance schedule to document both the total ACH and the outside-air ACH for each operating room; confirm a minimum of 4 ACH of 100% outside air and 20 ACH total supply air for every OR space.
2. Verify the central air-handling unit(s) serving the OR suite include an outside-air economizer or dedicated OA damper sized to deliver at minimum 4 ACH to each OR; provide AHU schedules with outside-air CFM quantities on the mechanical drawings.
3. Remove from the OR design any room-mounted fan-coil units, unit ventilators, induction units, or other local recirculation devices; all conditioned supply air must originate from the central AHU with minimum MERV-14 supply filtration per ASHRAE 170-2021.
4. Provide a reflected ceiling plan for the OR showing supply air diffuser layout consistent with a unidirectional (laminar) or semi-laminar flow pattern over the surgical field per FGI Guidelines Section 2.2-3.4; confirm diffuser coverage, throw, and location relative to the surgical table.
5. Resubmit revised mechanical drawings — including updated AHU schedules, air-balance schedule, and OR reflected ceiling plan — to the NCDHSR Construction Section; coordinate with the infection control officer to confirm the ventilation design meets ICRA requirements for the facility.

description: Emergency power system 96-hour fuel supply required; written load-shedding plan required and submitted with construction documents
violation_template: ODH PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — EMERGENCY POWER (OH-EP-001): The electrical construction documents submitted for the {occupancy} project in {county} County, {city} do not demonstrate compliance with the emergency electrical system requirements of Ohio Administrative Code 3701-83-16 and the FGI Guidelines for Design and Construction of Hospitals as adopted by the Ohio Department of Health (ODH). The following deficiencies have been identified: (1) the generator fuel storage capacity has not been specified or demonstrated to provide a minimum of 96 hours of continuous operation at full essential electrical system load without resupply; and/or (2) a written load-shedding plan identifying which non-critical electrical loads will be sequentially dropped in the event of a prolonged emergency has not been included in the submission. Ohio Administrative Code 3701-83-16 requires both provisions for all licensed hospitals. Construction documents that omit or inadequately address these requirements will not be approved by the ODH Plans Examination Section, and the project may not proceed to construction until these deficiencies are resolved.
fix_template:
1. Provide a generator sizing calculation on the electrical drawings or in the specifications demonstrating that on-site fuel storage is sufficient for 96 continuous hours of operation at the calculated full essential electrical system load; include a load schedule tabulating all connected essential loads used in the sizing.
2. Specify the automatic transfer switch (ATS) performance: confirm that each ATS serving Type 1 essential electrical system loads (life safety and critical branches) transfers within 10 seconds of normal-power failure per NFPA 110 and FGI Guidelines Section 2.1-8.3.
3. Prepare and include in the construction documents a written Load-Shedding Plan identifying all non-essential and deferrable loads served by the emergency generator; organize loads by priority tier and document the sequence and method (manual or automatic) by which each tier will be shed under sustained emergency conditions.
4. Confirm on the site plan that the generator fuel tank location, secondary containment, vent pipe terminations, and fill-point access comply with Ohio EPA and local fire department requirements; note the 30-day testing and fuel-level inspection schedule in the O&M section of the specifications.
5. Resubmit revised electrical drawings, load calculations, and the Load-Shedding Plan to the ODH Plans Examination Section, 246 N. High Street, Columbus, OH 43215, for continued review and approval.

description: Airborne Infection Isolation (AII) room required with negative pressure, minimum 12 ACH, and direct exhaust to outdoors
violation_template: ODH PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — INFECTION CONTROL / VENTILATION (OH-INF-001): The mechanical construction documents submitted for the {occupancy} project in {county} County do not demonstrate compliance with the Airborne Infection Isolation (AII) room ventilation requirements of Ohio Administrative Code 3701-83-35 and ASHRAE 170-2021 Table 7.1 as adopted by ODH. The submitted mechanical drawings and/or air-balance schedule do not confirm one or more of the following mandatory requirements: (1) each AII room must be maintained at a continuous negative pressure differential with respect to the adjacent corridor and all connecting spaces; (2) a minimum of 12 total air changes per hour (ACH) must be provided, with all exhaust air discharged directly to the building exterior and not recirculated to any other space; and (3) the exhaust discharge point must be located and detailed to prevent re-entrainment into any air intake per ASHRAE 170-2021. Failure to provide properly designed AII rooms places patients and staff at risk for airborne pathogen transmission and will result in denial of ODH construction approval.
fix_template:
1. Add pressure-relationship diagrams to the mechanical drawings showing a minimum negative pressure differential of -0.01 inches water gauge (2.5 Pa) in each AII room relative to the adjacent corridor and all connecting vestibule or anteroom spaces; specify continuous monitoring via a visual pressure indicator (magnahelic gauge or electronic monitor) visible from the corridor.
2. Revise the air-balance schedule to confirm a minimum 12 total air changes per hour in each AII room; identify supply CFM, exhaust CFM, and net pressure relationship for each room, and provide a room-by-room summary table on the mechanical drawings.
3. Route all AII room exhaust ductwork to dedicated exhaust fans that discharge directly to the building exterior; show exhaust fan locations and duct routing on mechanical floor plans and roof plan, confirming that discharge points are a minimum of 25 feet from any operable window or air intake per ASHRAE 170-2021.
4. Specify that no air from the AII room exhaust system is recirculated to any other space; if a heat-recovery device is used, specify a non-cross-contaminating type (run-around coil or rotary wheel with purge sector) and provide documentation of the manufacturer's leakage performance.
5. Resubmit revised mechanical drawings, pressure-relationship diagrams, and air-balance schedule to the ODH Plans Examination Section in Columbus for review and approval; coordinate with the facility infection preventionist to document ICRA measures during construction.

description: Operating room minimum 360 SF net; 20 ACH total; humidity 20-60 percent; temperature 68-75 degrees F required
violation_template: ODH PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — SURGICAL SUITE / HVAC (OH-SU-001): Review of the architectural and mechanical construction documents for the {occupancy} project in {county} County reveals noncompliance with the operating room design standards required by Ohio Administrative Code 3701-83-37 and the FGI Guidelines for Design and Construction of Hospitals as adopted by ODH. One or more of the following mandatory requirements have not been met: (1) the net clear floor area of one or more operating rooms is less than the required minimum of 360 square feet, exclusive of fixed and moveable equipment; (2) the air-balance schedule does not confirm a minimum of 20 total air changes per hour; (3) the HVAC design does not specify or demonstrate maintenance of relative humidity within the 20% to 60% range; and/or (4) the temperature control specifications do not confirm maintenance of a temperature range of 68°F to 75°F when the OR is in use. All four requirements are mandatory under OAC 3701-83-37. Documents with unresolved OR deficiencies will not receive ODH approval.
fix_template:
1. Add net clear floor area calculations for each operating room to the architectural floor plan; confirm a minimum of 360 square feet net, measured from finished face of wall to finished face of wall and excluding fixed casework, columns, equipment bays, and structural projections; revise room dimensions or layout as needed.
2. Update the air-balance schedule on the mechanical drawings to list for each OR: supply air CFM, exhaust air CFM, total ACH, outside-air ACH, and pressure relationship (positive with respect to all adjacent spaces); confirm a minimum 20 total ACH and minimum 4 OA ACH per ASHRAE 170-2021 Table 7.1.
3. Specify humidity monitoring and control: include humidification and dehumidification capability in the AHU or in-room, sized and controlled to maintain RH between 20% and 60% at all occupied times; specify BAS alarms for RH values outside this range and document a response protocol.
4. Specify a temperature control system capable of maintaining 68°F to 75°F in each OR under full surgical load and all seasons; provide equipment schedules confirming sensible cooling and heating capacity; specify thermostat locations inside the OR and confirm that nursing staff can request setpoint adjustments within the permitted range.
5. Resubmit revised architectural floor plans and mechanical drawings — including the updated OR air-balance schedule, AHU equipment schedule, and HVAC control sequence — to the ODH Plans Examination Section for review and approval.

description: Minimum 100 SF single-occupancy patient room; 80 SF per bed double-occupancy; in-room toilet required for ICU patient rooms
violation_template: ODH PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — PATIENT ROOM / ARCHITECTURAL (OH-PR-001): The architectural construction documents submitted for the {occupancy} project in {county} County do not comply with the minimum patient room area requirements and toilet access standards of Ohio Administrative Code 3701-83-32 and the FGI Guidelines as adopted by ODH. The following deficiencies have been identified: (1) one or more single-occupancy patient rooms appear to provide less than 100 square feet of clear floor area, exclusive of toilet rooms, closets, vestibules, and alcoves; (2) one or more double-occupancy (two-bed) rooms appear to provide less than 80 square feet of clear floor area per bed space; and/or (3) one or more patient rooms designated as intensive care unit (ICU) beds do not provide an in-room toilet and handwashing station within the room envelope as required by OAC 3701-83-32 for ICU settings. These standards are prerequisites for ODH facility licensure and must be addressed in revised construction documents.
fix_template:
1. Provide net clear floor area calculations on the architectural floor plan for every patient room; confirm single-occupancy rooms are 100 SF minimum and double-occupancy rooms provide 80 SF per bed space, measuring from finished face of wall and excluding toilet rooms, closets, vestibule areas, and fixed equipment footprints.
2. Revise any non-compliant rooms by adjusting room dimensions, removing non-essential fixed elements from the room footprint, or reconfiguring the floor plan; clearly dimension all revised patient rooms on the submitted drawings.
3. For all ICU patient room positions, confirm that a private toilet room with water closet and handwashing sink is provided within the room envelope and accessible without entering a public corridor; show the toilet room on the floor plan with interior dimensions and confirm ADA-compliant accessible clearances per the 2010 ADA Standards as adopted in Ohio.
4. Verify that all patient toilet rooms comply with Ohio Plumbing Code (OPC) requirements for fixture supply and drain connections; confirm handwashing sinks in patient rooms meet ODH infection control standards with hands-free (sensor or wrist-blade) operation specified in the plumbing fixture schedule.
5. Resubmit revised architectural floor plans with room-by-room area calculations and annotated toilet adjacency diagrams to the ODH Plans Examination Section, 246 N. High Street, Columbus, OH 43215, for review and approval.

description: Ohio Fire Code Chapter 19 healthcare occupancies; NFPA 101-2021 and NFPA 13 automatic sprinklers required throughout
violation_template: ODH PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — FIRE AND LIFE SAFETY (OH-FLS-001): The fire protection and life safety construction documents submitted for the {occupancy} project in {county} County do not demonstrate compliance with the Ohio Fire Code (OFC) Chapter 19 governing healthcare occupancies, the 2021 edition of NFPA 101 (Life Safety Code) as adopted by ODH, and NFPA 13 (Standard for the Installation of Sprinkler Systems). Specifically, the submitted documents do not adequately confirm: (1) that an automatic sprinkler system designed and installed in accordance with NFPA 13 is provided throughout the entire facility, including all mechanical spaces, storage rooms, and interstitial areas; (2) that the fire alarm system meets NFPA 72 requirements with full-coverage notification appliances and voice evacuation; and/or (3) that the construction type, occupancy separation, corridor fire ratings, and exit access travel distances comply with NFPA 101-2021 Chapter 18 for new healthcare occupancies or Chapter 19 for existing healthcare occupancies. ODH will not issue plan approval for healthcare facilities with unresolved fire and life safety deficiencies.
fix_template:
1. Provide complete NFPA 13 sprinkler system drawings including: a site and floor-plan layout showing all sprinkler head types and locations, hydraulic calculations with water supply analysis, riser diagram, and a specification section referencing the NFPA 13 edition being applied; confirm full building coverage including all storage, mechanical, and interstitial spaces.
2. Submit NFPA 72 fire alarm system drawings including initiating device locations, notification appliance layout, mass-notification or voice-evacuation system design, FACP location, and a complete system narrative; confirm supervised automatic sprinkler water-flow and tamper-switch monitoring.
3. Provide a code analysis on the drawings or in a separate code compliance narrative demonstrating compliance with NFPA 101-2021 Chapter 18 (new) or Chapter 19 (existing): confirm construction type, occupancy classification, compartmentation (smoke compartment areas no greater than 22,500 SF), fire-rated corridor construction, exit access travel distances, and suite arrangements.
4. Coordinate with the Ohio State Fire Marshal's Office (OSFM) and local fire department for separate fire protection system permits; provide ODH with a copy of the OSFM or local fire department approval before ODH issues a final construction approval.
5. Resubmit coordinated fire protection, fire alarm, and architectural code-compliance drawings to the ODH Plans Examination Section and confirm that the local Authority Having Jurisdiction has been notified of the project.

description: Ohio Department of Health plan review required; submit to Columbus office before beginning construction on any licensed healthcare facility
violation_template: ODH PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — PLAN REVIEW / GENERAL (OH-GEN-001): This comment is issued pursuant to Ohio Administrative Code 3701-83-05, which requires that construction documents for the new construction, substantial renovation, or alteration of any ODH-licensed healthcare facility be submitted to and approved by the Ohio Department of Health Plans Examination Section before construction may begin. A review of the submission package for the {occupancy} project in {county} County, {city} indicates that the submittal is incomplete. One or more of the following elements are missing or deficient: (a) a completed ODH Building Project Registration form; (b) design professional seals and signatures from licensed Ohio architects and engineers of record on all discipline drawings; (c) a project description or program statement identifying the scope of work, affected licensed occupancy, bed count changes, and project cost; and/or (d) evidence of a concurrent local building department permit application. Beginning construction without a written ODH plan approval is a violation of OAC 3701-83-05 and may result in a Stop Work Order, required correction of non-compliant work at the owner's expense, and delay of ODH facility licensure.
fix_template:
1. Complete and submit the ODH Building Project Registration form available on the ODH Health Care Regulation website; include the ODH facility license number, facility address, name of the owner's representative, total estimated construction cost, and names of all licensed Ohio design professionals of record.
2. Ensure all construction drawings are sealed, signed, and dated by a licensed Ohio architect (architectural drawings) and licensed Ohio professional engineers (structural, mechanical, electrical, plumbing, and fire protection drawings) per Ohio Revised Code Chapter 4703 and Chapter 4733; unlicensed or out-of-state seals require a specific authorization from the applicable Ohio licensing board.
3. Prepare a written project description covering: project type (new construction, addition, renovation, change of use), affected departments, scope of licensed services impacted, any change to licensed bed count or service types, phasing plan, and estimated construction schedule.
4. Submit three (3) paper sets of complete construction documents (or electronic submission through the ODH e-Plans portal) to the ODH Plans Examination Section, 246 N. High Street, 7th Floor, Columbus, OH 43215; include all architectural, structural, mechanical, electrical, plumbing, fire protection, and civil drawings together with specifications and energy compliance documentation.
5. Submit a concurrent application for a local building permit to the Authority Having Jurisdiction over the project site; provide ODH with a copy of the local permit application receipt, and do not begin construction until both the ODH written approval and the local building permit are in hand.

description: Certificate of Occupancy from local AHJ and ODH survey required before the facility may open or expand licensed services
violation_template: ODH PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — LICENSURE / CERTIFICATE OF OCCUPANCY (OH-GEN-002): This comment is issued as advance notice of the two-step approval process required before any newly constructed or renovated space within the {occupancy} facility in {county} County may be placed into service or occupied by patients. Pursuant to Ohio Administrative Code 3701-83-07, the facility must obtain: (1) a Certificate of Occupancy (CO) issued by the local Authority Having Jurisdiction (the local building department) confirming that the construction meets the adopted local building code; and (2) a completed ODH on-site survey by an ODH Healthcare Surveyor confirming that the completed space meets all applicable ODH licensing regulations before the facility begins providing services from that space. Neither approval alone is sufficient — both must be obtained before patients may be seen in the new or renovated area. ODH will schedule the on-site survey only after the facility notifies ODH in writing that construction is complete and a local CO has been issued. Occupying or providing services in a space before both approvals are obtained is a licensing violation under Ohio Revised Code §3702.30.
fix_template:
1. Upon substantial completion of construction, schedule and pass all required inspections with the local building department; obtain the final Certificate of Occupancy (CO) or Temporary Certificate of Occupancy (TCO) from the local AHJ and retain the original for the facility's permanent records.
2. Upon receipt of the local CO or TCO, notify the ODH Healthcare Regulatory Section in writing — including the ODH facility license number, name of the licensed administrator, a description of the completed space, and a copy of the local CO — to request an ODH on-site licensure survey; allow a minimum of 30 days for ODH to schedule the survey.
3. Ensure the facility is fully ready for the ODH survey before the survey date: all equipment is installed and operational, staff are trained and in place, required policies and procedures are in place, and the space is furnished and ready for patient use; a survey finding of substantial non-compliance will require a repeat survey and may delay licensure.
4. Do not allow patients to occupy the new or renovated space, or to receive services from it, until the ODH Surveyor has provided written notice of a satisfactory survey outcome and ODH has issued an amended or updated facility license covering the new space or service.
5. Retain copies of the local CO, ODH survey report, and the updated ODH license in the facility's permanent regulatory compliance files and make them available for inspection upon request by ODH or any accreditation body.

description: Sterile compounding pharmacy must comply with USP 797; negative pressure ISO 7 cleanroom required for hazardous drug compounding
violation_template: ODH PLAN REVIEW COMMENT — PHARMACY / STERILE COMPOUNDING (OH-PHARM-001): The construction documents submitted for the sterile compounding pharmacy within the {occupancy} project in {county} County do not demonstrate compliance with USP General Chapter <797> (Pharmaceutical Compounding — Sterile Preparations) as required by the Ohio State Board of Pharmacy (OSBP) under Ohio Administrative Code 3715-27. The following deficiencies have been identified: (1) the pharmacy cleanroom suite does not clearly demonstrate ISO 7 (Class 10,000) or better air cleanliness classification for the buffer room where sterile preparations are compounded, with continuous positive pressure maintained with respect to the ante-room and adjacent non-classified areas for non-hazardous compounds; (2) for any space designated for Category 1 or Category 2 sterile hazardous drug (HD) compounding, the construction documents do not specify a negative-pressure ISO 7 buffer room with a positive-pressure ISO 7 ante-room, with all HD room exhaust discharged directly to the building exterior through HEPA filtration; and/or (3) the air-balance schedule and room pressure diagrams required to verify cleanroom pressure cascades are not included in the mechanical submission. Failure to design the compounding pharmacy to USP <797> standards may result in denial of the Ohio State Board of Pharmacy operating license and ODH facility approval.
fix_template:
1. Classify each cleanroom space in the pharmacy suite by ISO cleanroom classification (ISO 5, ISO 7, or ISO 8) on the architectural floor plan; confirm the buffer room(s) achieve ISO 7 at a minimum and that a primary engineering control (PEC) with ISO 5 conditions (laminar airflow hood or biological safety cabinet) is located within the buffer room.
2. For non-hazardous sterile compounding: specify the buffer room at a continuous positive pressure differential of at least +0.02 to +0.05 inches water gauge (5 to 12.5 Pa) relative to the ante-room, and the ante-room at positive pressure relative to the adjacent general pharmacy or corridor; provide a pressure-cascade diagram on the mechanical drawings.
3. For hazardous drug (HD) sterile compounding: specify the HD buffer room at a continuous negative pressure of at least -0.01 to -0.03 inches water gauge (-2.5 to -7.5 Pa) relative to the ante-room, and the ante-room at positive pressure relative to the adjacent corridor; provide dedicated HEPA-filtered exhaust for the HD buffer room discharging directly to the building exterior; confirm no recirculation of HD room exhaust air to any other space.
4. Update the air-balance schedule to list supply CFM, exhaust CFM, net pressure, total ACPH, and ISO classification for each cleanroom space; confirm a minimum of 30 ACPH in each ISO 7 buffer room per USP <797> Table 5 and FGI Guidelines recommendations; include a room-by-room pressure-cascade diagram as a dedicated mechanical drawing sheet.
5. Coordinate the pharmacy construction documents with the Ohio State Board of Pharmacy (OSBP) registration requirements under OAC 4729-17 and provide ODH with a copy of the OSBP facility registration or pre-application correspondence; resubmit revised mechanical drawings and pharmacy floor plan to the ODH Plans Examination Section, 246 N. High Street, Columbus, OH 43215, for review and approval.
